sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: When North Carolina law requires a railroad-crossing stop, within what distance range from the nearest rail must you halt?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: When the railroad statute's conditions apply, you must stop no more than fifty feet and no less than fifteen feet from the nearest rail, and wait until you can cross safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Which active crossing devices or personnel legally trigger a mandatory railroad stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: That stop is required when a visible electric or mechanical signal warns of an approaching train, or when a crossing gate is down or a flagger is signaling a train.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: Even without gates, which two train-approach situations require you to stop at a crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: The stop is also required when a train within roughly one thousand five hundred feet sounds a signal and is an immediate hazard, or when a train is plainly visible and dangerously close.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: What counts as stopping too close versus stopping too far back at a railroad crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: The stopping zone at a railroad crossing is between fifteen and fifty feet from the nearest rail, closer than fifteen being too near and farther than fifty too far.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: How does North Carolina's audible train-horn distance compare in scale with your bumper's stopping zone?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: The audible-train trigger refers to a train within roughly one thousand five hundred feet, while the stopping zone itself is measured in tens of feet from the rail.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: May drivers or pedestrians go around, under, or through a crossing gate that is closed or moving?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: No driver may go through, around or under a crossing gate or barrier while it is closed or moving, and pedestrians may not pass it in any way either.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: How should vehicles position themselves while waiting at a railroad crossing, and when are two lines legal?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: While stopped for a crossing, keep as far right as possible and do not form two lines of traffic unless the road is marked for four or more lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: How is breaking North Carolina's railroad signal law classified, and when does an employer face penalties too?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Breaking the railroad signal law is an infraction, and an employer who knowingly lets a commercial driver break it also commits an infraction and faces a civil penalty.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: What does a yellow-and-black advance RR sign tell you to do as you approach?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: A yellow and black RR sign warns that a railroad crossing is ahead, so look both ways and listen because you may need to stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: Who holds the right of way over every road user—even police, fire, and ambulances—and what if a stop sign is posted?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: A train always has the right of way, even over police, fire and ambulance vehicles, and if the crossing has a stop sign you must stop fully before crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: Roughly how much distance does a train traveling fifty-five miles per hour need to come to a stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: A train going fifty-five miles per hour needs more than a mile to stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: How should you approach and depart a railroad crossing sign, and what rule applies to stopping on the tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: At a crossing sign, approach carefully, be ready to stop for a train, move on carefully once it passes, and never stop on the tracks for any reason.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What shape marks the crossing itself, and what does a smaller plaque mounted beneath it indicate?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: The crossbuck is the X-shaped sign at the crossing itself, and a smaller sign beneath it shows when there is more than one track.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: When crossing warning lights activate, when must you stop—and is driving through lowered gates ever lawful?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: When crossing signals start, you must stop before the gates come down across your side, and moving through a crossing with the gates down is unlawful.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Why is driving along or across railroad tracks anywhere outside an official grade crossing illegal?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: Railroads are private property, so driving on or across tracks anywhere other than a designated crossing is illegal.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: What is your legal duty toward an approaching train at a rural crossing marked only by a bare crossbuck?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: You must always yield to a train, even at a crossing marked only by a crossbuck with no lights or gates.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Which intersection signal rule matches flashing red lights mounted on a railroad crossbuck?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: Flashing red lights at a crossbuck mean you stop exactly as you would for any flashing red traffic signal.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: How does your duty at a crossbuck with flashing red lights compare with a bare crossbuck lacking lights or gates?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: At a crossbuck with flashing red lights you stop as for any flashing red signal, while at a crossbuck with no lights or gates you must still yield to any train.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: Why must you wait until red lights stop flashing instead of rolling forward the instant a caboose clears?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Do not start moving the moment a train passes, because a second train may be coming either way; wait until the red lights stop flashing.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: Which four commercial or transit vehicle types should you expect to stop at railroad crossings even without a train?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: Expect to stop behind vehicles that must stop at crossings, such as school buses, passenger carriers, for-hire vehicles and placarded vehicles hauling explosives or hazardous materials.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: What should you do if warning lights start flashing or gates begin lowering while your car is already on the tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: If the lights start flashing or the gates begin lowering while you are on the tracks, keep moving: do not stop or back up, since the warning allows time to clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: Can a lowering crossing gate physically trap your car on the tracks if it drops ahead of you?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: Crossing gates are flexible and cannot trap you, so drive through a gate that comes down beyond you; stopping to back up could stall the car.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: Even though flexible gates cannot trap you, what everyday traffic mistake easily pins cars onto railroad tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Gates will not trap you but stopped traffic can, so make sure the traffic ahead will not halt and leave you on the tracks.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: How does your crossing response flip depending on whether signals start before you enter or while you are on the rails?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: Before the signals start you stop short of the lowering gates, but if you are already on the tracks when they start you keep moving and do not stop or back up.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: What three pieces of emergency information appear on the Blue Sign posted at every North Carolina highway-rail crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Every highway-rail crossing in North Carolina must post an Emergency Notification System Blue Sign in each direction showing the crossing ID number, railroad name and an emergency phone number.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: What is the quickest way to halt an approaching train during a track emergency, and how is your location identified?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: Using the Blue Sign to call the railroad directly is the fastest way to get a train stopped in an emergency, and each crossing has its own unique USDOT identification number.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: What immediate action must everyone take if your vehicle stalls on or right beside railroad tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: If your vehicle stalls on or near the tracks, get out right away and walk quickly along the road to a safe spot away from the tracks.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: When a car stalls on the tracks, which step comes first—calling the Blue Sign number or getting everyone out?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: A stalled car on the tracks means get out and move away first, and only then call the railroad using the Blue Sign, not the other way round.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: Who handles active crossing emergencies via the Blue Sign versus reports of damaged or missing signs?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: The Blue Sign number reaches the railroad for crossing emergencies, while damaged or missing signs go to the Federal Railroad Administration.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: Why must right-turning city drivers watch carefully for a bicyclist riding straight through the intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: Because bicyclists ride to the right of cars, a cyclist going straight through an intersection is at risk from a motorist turning right.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: What is the safe move if you realize too late that you are in the wrong lane for a city turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: If you find you are in the wrong lane for a turn in the city, continue to the next intersection and turn there.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: Which visual clue on the car ahead warns that you are cruising inside its driver's blind spot?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Avoid riding alongside another car: when the forward car's inside mirror is out of your view, you are likely sitting in its driver's blind spot.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: Beside avoiding lane weaving, how should you divide through travel versus turns on a multi-lane one-way street?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: Do not weave between lanes, and on a one-way street use the center lanes for through travel and the outside lanes for turns.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: Which three physical factors often make rural roads deadlier than congested city streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: Rural roads are often more dangerous than heavy city traffic because they may be narrower, darker and faster.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: Why are primary-highway cruising speeds unsafe on secondary country roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: Secondary roads tend to have steeper hills, sharper curves and short sight distances, so they cannot be driven safely at speeds suited to primary highways.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: Which design features make interstate highways statistically safer than conventional roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: Interstates are safer because opposing traffic is separated, entry and exit points are fewer, and there are no railroad crossings, sharp curves, stop signs or traffic signals.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: How should you use the acceleration lane when merging onto an interstate highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: When entering an interstate, stay in the acceleration lane until you match the speed of traffic, then merge safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: Which interstate lanes are for cruising versus passing, and what following rule helps prevent common rear-end crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: On the interstate keep right and use the left lanes to pass, and avoid tailgating with the two-second rule, since rear-end crashes are among the most frequent there.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: How often does North Carolina recommend stopping at interstate rest areas, and where must you never halt?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: Stop at rest areas often, ideally at least once every one hundred miles, and never stop in a travel lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: After pulling well off the interstate for a breakdown, how do you signal distress by day and at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: After a breakdown, get well off the road, tie a white cloth to the antenna or left door handle and raise the hood; at night turn on the emergency flashers or parking lights.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: How does proper interstate breakdown procedure reinforce the rule against stopping in travel lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: A breakdown calls for pulling far off the road with a white cloth and raised hood, and the interstate rule is never to stop in a travel lane.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: When should you signal and begin braking as you take an interstate exit?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: To exit, signal well ahead, move into the deceleration lane without slowing first, and then keep to the posted exit speed.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: How do speed changes in an acceleration lane contrast with speed changes in a deceleration lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: On entry you speed up in the acceleration lane to match traffic, while on exit you move into the deceleration lane before slowing down.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: Why is driving far below the posted speed limit hazardous on an interstate, and how should you pace yourself?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: On the interstate it is dangerous to drive far below the posted limit; follow the flow of traffic as long as you are not speeding.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: What three moves are forbidden if you miss your interstate exit, and what must you do instead?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: If you miss your exit, do not slow down, back up or turn around; go on to the next exit and find a way back from there.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.front: What immediate steps must you take if you accidentally enter an interstate ramp going the wrong way?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.expected_back: If you enter an interstate going the wrong way, pull onto the right shoulder and stop, then turn around when the way is clear; watch for DO NOT ENTER signs to avoid this.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: Why do you keep driving forward after a missed exit yet stop immediately on the right shoulder after a wrong-way entry?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: A missed exit is handled by driving on to the next one, while entering the wrong way is handled by pulling onto the right shoulder, stopping and turning around when clear.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.front: From how many feet away at night should high beams versus low beams reveal a person ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.expected_back: At night you should be able to see a person two hundred feet away with high beams and seventy-five feet away with low beams.

sec10-card-sec10-F41.front: Which two mechanical or loading factors knock headlights out of alignment and blind oncoming drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.expected_back: Badly aimed headlights glare into the eyes of other road users; vibration can knock them out of line, and a heavily loaded rear can tilt the beams up.

sec10-card-sec10-F42.front: What color and visibility distance apply to taillights, and what color and distance apply to the license-plate lamp?
sec10-card-sec10-F42.expected_back: Taillights must be red and visible from at least five hundred feet, and a white light must make the license plate readable from at least fifty feet.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: Can you pair all four North Carolina night-lighting distances—high beams, low beams, taillights, and license plate?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: High beams should reveal a person at two hundred feet and low beams at seventy-five feet, while taillights must be visible at five hundred feet and the plate light must light the numbers at fifty feet.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.front: What three immediate steps should you take right after hitting an animal or spotting an injured one?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.expected_back: After hitting an animal or finding an injured one, pull safely to the roadside, stay in the car with the doors locked and turn on the hazard lights.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.front: Why should you never walk up to an animal that your vehicle has struck?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.expected_back: Do not walk up to an animal you have struck, because it may be dangerous.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.front: What is North Carolina's number-one rule in any sudden driving emergency?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.expected_back: In any emergency, the first rule is not to panic but to react quickly and correctly.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.front: What three steps slow a manual-transmission car when the regular brakes fail?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.expected_back: If the brakes fail in a manual car, shift to a lower gear, release the clutch and apply the emergency brake.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.front: What two controls should you use if the brakes fail in an automatic car?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.expected_back: If the brakes fail in an automatic car, apply the emergency brake and move the gear lever into the low range.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.front: How does handling brake failure in a manual car differ from handling it in an automatic?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.expected_back: With failed brakes, a manual car downshifts and releases the clutch before the emergency brake, while an automatic applies the emergency brake and selects low range.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.front: Why should you still force low gear and the emergency brake during brake failure despite possible wear?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.expected_back: Using the emergency brake and low gear this way may damage them, but with failed brakes there is no better option.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.front: How do you dry wet brakes safely after driving through water?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.expected_back: To dry wet brakes, drive a short distance while pressing lightly on the brake pedal so the friction heat evaporates the water.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.front: How and when should you set up your speed control for a long or steep downhill grade?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.expected_back: On a long or steep downhill, control speed with a lower gear rather than the brake pedal, shifting down at the top before you start down.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.front: When do you drag light brake pressure briefly, and when do you rely on a lower gear instead?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.expected_back: Wet brakes are dried with light brake pressure over a short drive, while a long downhill calls for a lower gear instead of the brake pedal.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.front: What steps should you follow if your accelerator sticks down while driving?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.expected_back: If the gas pedal sticks, tap it or lift it with your foot, shift to neutral and brake firmly without locking the wheels, then get completely off the road.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.front: How does your gear choice for a stuck gas pedal differ from your gear choice for failed brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.expected_back: A stuck gas pedal calls for shifting to neutral and braking firmly, whereas brake failure calls for a lower gear and the emergency brake.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.front: What ride change tells you to stop and inspect your tires, and how does a sudden blowout feel?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.expected_back: An unexplained bumpy ride is a reason to stop and check the tires; a blowout announces itself with a loud noise and a swerve.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.front: What should you do with the steering wheel and gas pedal the instant a tire blows out?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.expected_back: In a blowout, grip the wheel firmly and keep the car straight in your lane, then slow down by lifting off the accelerator.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.front: When is it safe to touch the brake pedal and pull off the road after a tire blowout?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.expected_back: After a blowout, do not brake until the engine has slowed the car enough for you to keep control, then pull completely off the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.front: What three setup steps come before you start changing a flat tire?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.expected_back: Before changing a flat, move fully off the road, set the parking brake and put out flares if you have them.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.front: How do your actions while rolling through a blowout differ from starting a roadside flat change?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.expected_back: During a blowout you hold the wheel straight and avoid braking until the engine slows the car, while a flat tire change starts only once the car is fully off the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.front: How must passengers exit during a tire change, and where must they never stand?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.expected_back: During a tire change, all passengers must get out on the passenger side and wait off the road, never standing in front of or behind the car.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.front: Which lights should run and how do you stop the vehicle from rolling during a tire change?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.expected_back: Turn on the flashers and parking lights and block the wheels so the car cannot roll while the tire is changed.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.front: What should you do instead of trying to fix a disabled car right next to passing traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.expected_back: Never try to repair a car where it is exposed to passing traffic; call a tow truck or mechanic instead.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.front: Where should the car sit and where should everyone wait after a roadside breakdown?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.expected_back: In a breakdown, move the car fully onto the shoulder, get everyone out on the passenger side and stand well away from the car, not in front of it or behind it.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.front: How do you signal that your broken-down car needs help by day and after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.expected_back: To ask for help after a breakdown, tie a white cloth to the left door handle or radio aerial and raise the hood; after dark use the parking lights or flashers.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.front: Which visual markers ask for breakdown help, and which doors must everyone use to get out?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.expected_back: A breakdown signal for help is a white cloth on the left door handle or aerial plus a raised hood, and everyone exits on the passenger side.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.front: Which night-visibility items should stay in your vehicle at all times for emergencies?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.expected_back: Keep a flashlight or flares in the car at all times for emergencies.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.front: What two immediate warnings and speed steps come first if an oncoming car crosses the center line?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.expected_back: If an oncoming vehicle crosses the center line into your path, slow down at once and sound the horn.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.front: Which direction must you steer if an oncoming vehicle enters your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.expected_back: When a vehicle crosses into your lane, keep to the right, even if that means leaving the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.front: What two panic moves must you avoid if your wheels drop off the pavement edge onto the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.expected_back: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, do not brake hard or jerk back toward the road, since you could skid or roll over.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.front: How do you safely bring your car back onto the pavement after dropping onto the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.expected_back: To recover from running onto the shoulder, ease off the gas, steer straight, let the engine slow the car, and return gradually only once traffic is clear and you are nearly stopped.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.front: How does recovering from a dropped wheel differ from escaping an oncoming car in your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.expected_back: Running onto the shoulder means no hard braking and no sharp turn back, while an oncoming car in your lane means keep right even off the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.front: Which three slick road surfaces raise skid risk, and how should you adjust speed on them?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.expected_back: Wet roads, ice and packed snow make skids more likely, so reduce speed gradually on them.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.front: How should you brake to prevent a skid in an ABS car compared with a non-ABS car?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.expected_back: To avoid a skid with ABS, press the brake firmly and steadily without pumping; without ABS, pump the brakes gently.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.front: What is the key pedal difference when trying to avoid a skid with ABS versus without ABS?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.expected_back: With ABS you hold firm steady pressure to avoid a skid, but without ABS you pump the brakes gently.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.front: What should you do with the gas pedal and steering wheel once a skid starts?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.expected_back: In a skid, ease off the gas and steer toward the direction the rear of the car is sliding.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.front: What steering adjustment is needed right as your skidding car begins to straighten out?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.expected_back: As the car begins to straighten out of a skid, turn the wheel back the other way so you do not over-steer.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.front: In what exact order do the two steering moves happen during skid recovery?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.expected_back: In a skid you first steer toward the rear's slide and then steer back as the car straightens, so the two steering moves happen in sequence.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.front: What should you do if an oncoming collision looks unavoidable?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.expected_back: If a crash seems likely, sound the horn, keep right and turn away from oncoming traffic, even into an open field off the road.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.front: How should you respond if a car is about to rear-end you and the lane ahead is open?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.expected_back: If you are about to be struck from behind with clear road ahead, accelerate away, be ready to brake if space runs out, brace yourself and press your head against the head rest.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.front: Which two protective actions go together when a rear-end hit is coming and space ahead is open?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.expected_back: If a rear impact is coming and the road ahead is clear you accelerate away, but you also brace and press your head against the head rest.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.front: How should you hold the steering wheel when a collision is about to strike your car?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.expected_back: If you are about to be hit, hold the steering wheel tightly.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.front: Along with staying ready to steer, what last-resort move shields you right before glass shatters?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.expected_back: If a crash is about to happen, be ready to turn quickly to try to control the car, and as a last resort shield your face from breaking glass with your arms and hands.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.front: How does North Carolina law treat bystanders who stop to help crash victims, and what is excluded?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.expected_back: North Carolina law shields people who stop to help at a crash from civil liability, except for intentional wrongdoing or unruly conduct.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.front: What is every driver legally required to do immediately when involved in any crash?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.expected_back: A driver involved in a crash must stop immediately; failing to stop breaks the law.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.front: Once stopped at a crash scene, what three priorities must be handled right away?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.expected_back: At a crash scene, take steps to prevent further crashes, help the injured and make sure someone notifies law enforcement right away.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.front: When should crash vehicles on a highway lane, ramp, or shoulder be moved onto the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.expected_back: If nobody is hurt or killed in a crash on a highway lane, ramp or shoulder, each car that can be driven safely should be moved out of the travel lane onto the shoulder.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.front: Which injuries or apparent property-damage total require immediate reporting to the nearest law enforcement agency?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.expected_back: You must report a crash to the nearest law enforcement officer or agency right away if anyone is killed or injured or total property damage appears to be one thousand dollars or more.

sec13-card-sec13-F38.front: What two penalties can follow if you fail to report a legally reportable crash?
sec13-card-sec13-F38.expected_back: Not reporting a reportable crash can lead to prosecution and suspension of your driver license.

sec13-card-sec13-F39.front: Beyond police, whom should you notify after any crash, and what DMV paperwork can follow?
sec13-card-sec13-F39.expected_back: You should also report any crash to your insurance company, and in some cases you must file DMV forms proving liability insurance.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.front: How does the threshold for mandatory police reporting differ from notifying your insurance company?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.expected_back: A crash must be reported to police right away for any death or injury, or for apparent damage of one thousand dollars or more, while reporting to your insurer is advised for every crash.

sec13-card-sec13-F40.front: Which five pieces of driver, vehicle, and coverage information must be exchanged at a crash?
sec13-card-sec13-F40.expected_back: After a crash you must give your name, address, license number, vehicle registration number and insurance company, and collect the same from the others involved.

sec13-card-sec13-F41.front: What must you do if you cannot identify the other occupants or the owner of damaged property?
sec13-card-sec13-F41.expected_back: If you cannot identify the other occupants or the owner of damaged property, write down everything you can and give it to the nearest law enforcement officer.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.front: Which two roadway locations use traffic signals to control both drivers and pedestrians?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.expected_back: Traffic signals control both vehicles and pedestrians at some intersections and at some mid-block crosswalks.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.front: What movements does a circular green light allow, and who gets the right of way when you turn?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.expected_back: A circular green light lets you go straight or turn with caution, but turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.front: What does a steady circular yellow light warn, and how should you decide whether to stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.expected_back: A circular yellow light warns that red is coming: stop unless you are too close to stop safely, in which case continue carefully through.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.front: Why must you never press the gas to beat a yellow light before red appears?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.expected_back: Never speed up on a yellow light to try to get through before it turns red.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.front: Under what two conditions may you turn right at a steady circular red light?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.expected_back: A steady circular red means stop, and you may then turn right after a complete stop unless a NO TURN ON RED sign is posted.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.front: Whom must you yield to after stopping before making a permitted right turn on red?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.expected_back: A driver turning right on red must yield to other traffic and to pedestrians in the intersection or starting to cross nearby in front of the stopped traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.front: What fine range applies if you fail to yield to a pedestrian while turning right on red?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.expected_back: Failing to yield to such a pedestrian while turning right on red carries a penalty of at least one hundred dollars and no more than five hundred dollars.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.front: What type of movement does a lit green arrow grant in the direction it points?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.expected_back: A green arrow gives a protected movement, allowing you to enter the intersection carefully in the direction the arrow points.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.front: How does turning on a circular green differ from turning on a green arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.expected_back: A circular green lets you turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, while a green arrow gives you a protected turn.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.front: Who must yield when a U-turn driver and an opposing right-turn driver both have green arrows?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.expected_back: When a U-turn and an opposing right turn both have green arrows at once, the U-turning driver yields to the right-turning driver.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.front: What must drivers turning in the direction of a steady red arrow do?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.expected_back: A red arrow means drivers turning in that direction must stop.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.front: How does a steady circular red differ from a steady red arrow when you want to turn?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.expected_back: A steady circular red still allows a right turn after a full stop unless signed otherwise, while a red arrow stops all turning traffic in that direction.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.front: What is ending when a yellow arrow lights up, and what three displays might follow it?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.expected_back: A yellow arrow warns that the protected green arrow is ending and will change to a circular green, a circular red or a red arrow.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.front: How does the meaning of a circular yellow light differ from a yellow arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.expected_back: A circular yellow means stop if you safely can, while a yellow arrow means the protected arrow phase is about to end.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.front: On a combined arrow-and-circle signal head, what controls turning cars when no arrow is lit?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.expected_back: Some signals combine protected arrows with unprotected circular lights; when no arrow is lit, circular lights control both through and turning traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.front: When both arrows and circular lights shine together on a signal, which controls turns and which controls straight traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.expected_back: When arrows and circular lights show together, the arrows control turning traffic and the circular lights control through traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.front: How must you treat an intersection when its traffic light is completely dark or malfunctioning?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.expected_back: At a signal that is dark or malfunctioning, treat the intersection as if every approach had a stop sign.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.front: When does the all-way-stop rule NOT apply at a broken or dark traffic light?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.expected_back: The all-way-stop rule for a broken signal does not apply when an officer or other authorized person directs traffic or another control device is working.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.front: What is the default rule at a dark traffic light, and what two situations override it?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.expected_back: A dark or broken traffic signal means an all-way stop, unless an officer is directing traffic or another device is working.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.front: Which roadside control matches a flashing red light, and when may you enter?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.expected_back: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop and wait until you can enter without interfering with approaching traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.front: Which roadside control matches a flashing yellow light, and how should you drive through it?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.expected_back: A flashing yellow light means the same as a warning sign: slow down and go on with caution.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.front: How does your duty at a flashing red light compare with your duty at a flashing yellow light?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.expected_back: A flashing red works like a stop sign and a flashing yellow works like a warning sign.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.front: What does a flashing yellow arrow allow, and what must you do before completing the turn?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow permits the turn shown, but you must first yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.front: On a flashing-yellow-arrow head, what do the solid red arrow and solid yellow arrow tell you?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.expected_back: On a flashing yellow arrow signal head, a solid red arrow means stop with no turn allowed, and a solid yellow arrow means get ready to stop.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.front: How does a flashing yellow arrow differ from a solid yellow arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.expected_back: A flashing yellow arrow means turn after yielding, while a solid yellow arrow means prepare to stop.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.front: What does a solid green arrow allow on a flashing-yellow-arrow signal head?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.expected_back: A solid green arrow on that head allows the turn without yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, though you still proceed with caution.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.front: What display may a right-turn signal head show at the top instead of a red arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.expected_back: Signal heads for right turns may show a steady circular red instead of a red arrow.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.front: What stream of traffic does a freeway ramp meter regulate?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.expected_back: A ramp meter controls traffic entering a freeway from an interchange entrance ramp.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.front: What do steady red and steady green mean when you pull up to a ramp meter?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.expected_back: At a ramp meter, steady red means stop and wait, and steady green means go down the ramp and merge onto the freeway.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.front: What should you do when an entrance ramp meter is dark with neither red nor green lit?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.expected_back: If a ramp meter is dark, showing neither red nor green, you may continue without stopping and merge or yield as conditions allow.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.front: How does your response to a red ramp meter differ from a dark ramp meter?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.expected_back: A ramp meter showing red means stop and wait, but a ramp meter showing nothing at all means you may merge without stopping.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.front: Where are hybrid beacons installed, and how do they look before someone triggers them?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.expected_back: Hybrid beacons can control traffic at mid-block crosswalks and at the entrances of emergency response facilities, and stay dark until a pedestrian or responder activates them.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.front: In what three-step light sequence does a hybrid beacon wake up once activated?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.expected_back: Once activated, a hybrid beacon flashes yellow, then shows steady yellow and then steady red so moving vehicles can stop safely.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.front: What must drivers do while a hybrid beacon displays steady red?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.expected_back: While a hybrid beacon shows steady red, vehicles stay stopped as pedestrians cross or emergency vehicles leave their station.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.front: When may you drive through a hybrid beacon after it switches from steady red to flashing red?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.expected_back: When the hybrid beacon switches to flashing red, stay stopped until the pedestrians or emergency vehicles have cleared; then, after a full stop, you may proceed while it still flashes.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.front: At a hybrid beacon, how does steady red differ from flashing red?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.expected_back: At a hybrid beacon, steady red means stay stopped, while flashing red lets you go after a full stop once the crossing is clear.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.front: What display does a hybrid beacon return to once its crossing cycle finishes?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.expected_back: After its cycle, a hybrid beacon goes dark again until the next activation.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.front: How do a hybrid beacon's warning stages differ from the colors shown on a ramp meter?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.expected_back: A hybrid beacon begins with flashing yellow and then steady yellow before red, unlike a ramp meter that shows only red or green.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: For vehicles built since nineteen fifty-five, what lamp colors and daylight visibility distance apply to brake and turn lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: Every motor vehicle built since nineteen fifty-five must have red or amber lights that come on with the brakes or turn signals, visible for at least one hundred feet in normal daylight.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Must brake and turn-signal lamps sit inside the taillight housing, or may they be mounted separately?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Those brake and turn lights may be built into the taillights or mounted separately; either arrangement is allowed.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: Can you pair North Carolina's daylight visibility distance with the mounting rule for brake and turn lamps?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Brake and turn lights must show for at least one hundred feet in daylight, and they may either share the taillight housing or be mounted on their own.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: Why is keeping signal lenses clean and bulbs working critical once daylight fades?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Keep light lenses clean and the lights working, because hand signals are hard for other drivers to see after dark.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: When should you adjust your mirrors, and what exact view should the inside and side mirrors frame?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Check and set the mirrors before driving: the inside mirror shows straight behind, and the side mirrors show the left and right rear while just barely showing the car's own side.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: Which three core capabilities must the brakes provide on any motor vehicle driven on public roads?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: Any motor vehicle on a public road must have brakes able to control it, stop it and hold it in place.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: How many independent ways of applying the brakes should well-maintained factory brake systems provide?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: Factory brakes should be kept in good condition and provide two separate ways of applying the brakes.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Under full foot pressure, how high above the floorboard must a healthy brake pedal remain?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: When pressed all the way, the brake pedal should stay at least one-third of its original distance above the floor; if not, have the brakes checked and repaired.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: What mechanical trouble does a slowly sinking brake pedal point to, and what should you do about brake squeaks?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: A brake pedal that slowly sinks under steady foot pressure means the hydraulic system needs checking, and squeaking brakes should also be inspected.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: Which three emergency-braking advantages do anti-lock brakes help deliver?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: Anti-lock brakes (ABS) help with stability against spin-outs, with steering where you intend, and with stopping distance.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: What foot technique maximizes anti-lock braking, and what habit weakens it?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: With ABS, brake hard and hold firm, steady pressure; pumping the pedal or easing off reduces how well ABS works.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: Why is pumping the brake pedal the exact wrong instinct in an ABS-equipped car?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: With anti-lock brakes you press hard and hold steady, which is the opposite of pumping the pedal.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: What simple step should you take every time you walk away from an unattended vehicle to prevent theft?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: To discourage theft, never leave the key in the ignition of a vehicle you are not attending.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: Which structural defects or minimum tread measurement make a tire legally unsafe in North Carolina?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: A tire is legally unsafe if a cut, crack or wear exposes the cord, if it shows tread separation or chunking, or if tread depth is under one sixteenth inch.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What specific damage or grip problems come from under-inflated tires compared with over-inflated tires?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Under-inflated tires wear out faster and are more likely to blow out, while over-inflated tires lose traction and wear down the center of the tread.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: How do tire failure modes flip when air pressure drops too low versus climbs too high?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: Under-inflated tires wear fast and risk blowouts, while over-inflated tires lose grip and wear the middle of the tread.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: Can you match North Carolina's legal fraction for minimum tire tread with the fraction for brake-pedal height?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: A tire becomes unsafe below one sixteenth inch of tread, while the brake pedal must stay at least one-third of its travel above the floor.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: How often and under what tire-temperature condition should you check tire pressure against manufacturer specs?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: Check tire air pressure at least once a month, preferably while the tires are cool, following the manufacturer's recommended pressure.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: Which vehicles are legally allowed to mount emergency lights or sirens in North Carolina?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: Only law enforcement and emergency vehicles are permitted to carry emergency lights or sirens.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: From how far away must a licensed vehicle's horn be audible, and what tone quality is forbidden?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: Every licensed motor vehicle needs a working horn that can be heard from at least two hundred feet without an unreasonably loud or harsh sound.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: Under what circumstance should you tap your horn, and how promptly must a dead horn be repaired?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: Use the horn only as a reasonable warning, never needlessly, and get a failed horn fixed right away.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: What floor and ceiling apply simultaneously to a legal vehicle horn in North Carolina?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: The horn must be heard from at least two hundred feet, yet it must not give an unreasonably loud or harsh sound, so both limits apply at once.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: What two emissions or sound outputs does a required working muffler hold down?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Every motor vehicle must have a working muffler, which reduces smoke and excess noise.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: What deadly hazard comes from an exhaust leak, and what simple window habit does the handbook recommend?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: An exhaust leak can let carbon monoxide into the cabin, which can cause drowsiness, unconsciousness or death, so the handbook suggests driving with a window open about one inch.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: Which three body-motion symptoms warn of bad suspension that could trigger a loss of control?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: Swaying, leaning hard in turns or constant bouncing can signal a suspension problem, which should be inspected and fixed at once because it can cause loss of control.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: Which bulbs blink when emergency flashers activate, and who may switch them on?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: The emergency flashers blink all four turn signals and may be used by any vehicle to warn of danger or show it is stopped or disabled.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: Who may use four-way hazard flashers compared with emergency beacons and sirens?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: Hazard flashers may be used by any vehicle, while emergency lights and sirens are reserved for law enforcement and emergency vehicles.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: Roughly how much extra per gallon can fuel cost climb for every five miles per hour driven above sixty?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: For fuel economy, each five miles per hour driven above sixty miles per hour can add up to about thirty cents per gallon in cost.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: By up to what percentage can aggressive starts and hard braking raise fuel consumption?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: Sudden starts and hard stops can raise fuel use by as much as forty percent.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: When should you shut off a waiting engine, and where is the speed crossover between open windows and air conditioning?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: To save fuel, switch off the engine if you will wait more than a couple of minutes, and open the windows below forty miles per hour but use air conditioning above it.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: How much fuel economy or gasoline can a dirty air filter and a loose gas cap cost you?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: A clogged air filter can lower mileage by about ten percent, and a loose fuel cap can let up to thirty gallons of gas a year escape.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: How many seconds—and roughly what urban distance—ahead should defensive drivers scan?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: Good drivers look ten to fifteen seconds ahead, roughly one city block, to avoid last-second stops and lane changes.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: About how often should you flick your eyes across the mirrors to catch tailgaters?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: Glance at the mirrors about every ten seconds to spot a vehicle following too closely, taking your eyes off the road only for an instant.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How does your forward scanning lead-time compare with how often you check your mirrors?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Look ten to fifteen seconds ahead of the car, but check the mirrors about every ten seconds.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: During which four driving situations should you check behind your vehicle and scan blind spots?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: Check behind you and your blind spots when changing lanes, backing, slowing down or going down a long hill.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: Where do vehicle blind spots sit, and how must you verify they are empty before moving sideways?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: Blind spots are the areas near the left and right rear corners that mirrors cannot show, so turn your head and look over your shoulder before a lane change or turn.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: Why are properly aimed mirrors still not enough by themselves right before changing lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Mirrors show the scene behind, but the rear-corner blind spots need a quick look over the shoulder.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: When parked cars, bushes, buildings, glare, or dirty glass hide cross traffic, how should you clear the corner?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: Glare, a dirty windshield, cars parked near an intersection, bushes or buildings can also block your view; ease forward until you can see clearly.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: Which five maneuvers call for signaling—even on a seemingly empty street—and what comes before signaling?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: Signal whenever you plan to slow, stop, turn, change lanes or leave the curb, even with no one in sight, but first confirm the move is safe.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.front: Although electric turn signals legally replace hand signals, what sky condition can hide whether they are blinking?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.expected_back: Turn-signal lights legally replace hand signals, but low morning or evening sun on the lenses can make it hard to tell whether they are flashing.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.front: How far ahead must you signal normally versus when the speed limit is forty-five miles per hour or higher?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.expected_back: Signal for at least the last one hundred feet before turning or stopping, and at least the last two hundred feet before a turn when the speed limit is forty-five miles per hour or higher.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: At what posted speed limit does North Carolina's required turn-signal distance jump from one hundred to two hundred feet?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Signal at least one hundred feet before a turn or stop in general, and at least two hundred feet before a turn where the limit is forty-five miles per hour or more.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.front: How do you position your left arm and fingers out the window to signal a left turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.expected_back: Hand signals use the left arm out the driver's window: arm straight out with finger pointing for a left turn.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.front: How do you hold your left forearm, hand, and palm to signal a right turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.expected_back: For a right turn by hand, hold the arm out with the forearm and hand raised and the palm forward.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.front: Which arm angle and palm direction tell drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.expected_back: To signal slowing or stopping by hand, point the arm and hand downward with the palm facing back.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: Can you match straight out, forearm up, and pointed down to their three hand-signal meanings?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.memory_hook: Straight left, up right, down stop
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Arm straight out means a left turn, forearm up means a right turn, and arm pointed down means slowing or stopping.

sec11-card-sec11-F37.front: How should you clear a tailgater behind you, and where within your lane should you normally ride?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.expected_back: If a driver follows too closely, change lanes and signal for that driver to pass; stay centered in your lane with space on both sides.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.front: When trapped between two simultaneous hazards of unequal severity—like oncoming cars and a child on a bike—who gets wider margin?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.expected_back: When facing two unavoidable dangers at once, give the most room to the one that is worst or most likely, such as a child on a bicycle rather than oncoming cars.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.front: How do you handle two equally serious hazards—such as parked cars on one side and oncoming traffic on the other?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.expected_back: If two dangers are equally serious, such as oncoming traffic and parked cars, stop and let the oncoming vehicles pass before going on.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: How does defensive strategy shift between two unequal dangers and two equally serious dangers?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: With unequal dangers give more room to the most likely one, but with equal dangers stop and let oncoming traffic go by.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: Is exceeding the posted speed limit inside a North Carolina highway work zone ever lawful?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Driving faster than the posted speed limit inside a highway work zone is unlawful.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Where does a North Carolina highway work zone legally begin and end?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: A highway work zone runs from the first sign marking where the zone begins to the last sign marking where it ends.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: When a sign at the start of a work zone lists a speeding penalty, how does it apply to your ticket?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: If a sign at the start of a work zone lists a speeding penalty, that penalty is added on top of any other penalty for the speeding conviction.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How do the start and end signs of a work zone relate to whether the extra speeding penalty applies?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: A work zone begins at the first work zone sign and ends at the last one, and an extra speeding penalty applies only when a sign at the start lists it.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: What single road environment reserves orange signs with black lettering on the approach and inside?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Orange signs with black lettering are used only to identify work zones, both on the approach and inside the zone.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: Who is stationed ahead when you pass a Flagger warning sign, and how should you prepare?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: A Flagger sign means a worker in an orange vest ahead is directing traffic with a STOP and SLOW paddle, so stay alert and be ready to stop.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: Why should you act promptly on black-on-orange advance lane-closure signs instead of waiting until the cones?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Black-on-orange advance signs may tell you to act, such as moving to another lane, and they give that message early enough that you should not wait until the last moment.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Why is driving noticeably slower than surrounding work-zone traffic a leading cause of rear-end crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: In work zones, going slower than the traffic around you is a leading cause of rear-end collisions, because confined lanes may leave no escape route.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: Which four physical devices or personnel guide vehicles safely through highway work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: Barricades, cones, drums and flaggers are the traffic control devices used to guide drivers safely through a work zone.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: During which clock window and visibility threshold does North Carolina law require headlights?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: North Carolina law requires headlights from sunset to sunrise and whenever you cannot see more than four hundred feet ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: Can North Carolina's headlight statute trigger in the middle of the afternoon—and at what exact distance?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: Headlights are required from sunset to sunrise and also whenever visibility drops to four hundred feet or less, even in daytime.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: What equipment switch must accompany your windshield wipers whenever bad weather hits in North Carolina?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: North Carolina requires every driver to turn on headlights whenever the windshield wipers are in use because of bad weather.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: When should you select low beams versus high beams during nighttime driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: At night use low beams in the city, and on the open road use high beams except when approaching or following another vehicle.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: Which three visibility and human factors make driving after dark riskier than daytime travel?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: Night driving is riskier because visibility is lower, more impaired and tired drivers are out, and oncoming headlights can blind you.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: How should you respond if an approaching driver leaves high beams blazing in your face?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: If an oncoming driver keeps high beams on, blink your high beams once as a reminder; if they still do not dim, stay on low beam.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: If your single high-beam reminder fails to make an oncoming car dim, why must your switch stay on low?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: Flash your high beams once to remind an oncoming driver to dim, but if they do not, keep your own lights on low rather than switching to high beams.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: Where should you aim your eyes—and how should you adjust speed—when oncoming headlights glare at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: To avoid headlight glare at night, slow down and look slightly toward the right edge of the road instead of into oncoming lights.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: What rule caps how fast you may safely drive on a dark road at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: Never drive so fast at night that you could not stop within the stretch of road you can actually see.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: Which lights go on and which switch off when you park beside a highway after dark?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: When parked on or beside a highway at night, turn on the emergency flashers and switch off the headlights so they do not blind oncoming drivers.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What two in-car tools fight low sun glare, and what is your backup move if glare still blinds you?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: For sun glare, lower the visor and wear sunglasses; if that is not enough, pull off to the roadside until you can drive safely.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: Which two vehicle switches and what speed adjustment apply whenever rain falls?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: In rain you must use your headlights and wipers, and you should drive more slowly than normal.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: How many times farther can stopping take on slick pavement, and how much following distance should you leave?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: Stopping on slippery pavement can take from two to ten times as far as on dry pavement, so allow at least double the usual following distance.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: How does North Carolina's slippery-road stopping multiplier connect to its wet following-distance rule?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.memory_hook: Up to tenfold stop, double gap
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: Wet pavement can stretch stopping distance from two to ten times, which is why the following gap should be at least doubled.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: During which exact minutes of a rainfall are roads slickest, and what makes them so greasy?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: Roads are slickest in the first ten to fifteen minutes of rain, when water mixes with oil, dirt, dust and rubber on the surface.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: At minimum, how many miles per hour slower than dry conditions should you drive on wet pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: On wet pavement drive at least five to ten miles per hour slower than you would on dry pavement.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: Why must cruise control stay switched off both during and after rain?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: Never use cruise control during or after rain, because the time spent switching it off in a hydroplane could cost you control.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: Once rain stops falling, why is re-engaging cruise control still dangerous on wet roads?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Cruise control stays off not only while it rains but also after the rain, since releasing it during a hydroplane costs time you may not have.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: At how low a speed and in how thin a film of water can tires lift into a hydroplane?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Hydroplaning happens when a thin layer of water lifts the tires off the road, and it can begin at speeds as low as thirty miles per hour in water just over one eighth inch deep.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: What exact pedal and steering actions recover grip when your car begins hydroplaning?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.memory_hook: Ease off gas, skip brakes, straight
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: If you hydroplane, lift your foot off the gas, do not brake, keep the wheel straight and let the car slow until the tires grip again.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: Can you pair the onset speed and water depth of hydroplaning with the correct foot response?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: Hydroplaning can start at about thirty miles per hour in water just over one eighth inch deep, and the response is to ease off the gas without braking.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: How do tread depth and inflation pressure affect hydroplaning risk and skid control?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Deep, open tire tread helps prevent hydroplaning, while worn or under-inflated tires raise the risk; for skid handling, tire pressure on the high side of the maker's range is better.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: Which four visual, sound, or steering cues warn that standing water sits on the pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: Signs of standing water include reflections on the surface, dimples from raindrops, a slushing tire sound and a loose feel in the steering.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: How long after a storm ends can leftover roadside puddles still trigger hydroplaning?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Puddles left by rain can cause hydroplaning for hours or even days after the rain stops.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.front: Since nineteen seventy, what share of North Carolina tropical-weather deaths came from inland flooding—and how many involved flooded roads?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.expected_back: Since nineteen seventy, inland flooding has caused eighty-five percent of tropical-weather deaths in North Carolina, and half of those involved people driving onto roads known to be flooded.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Why must you never drive through standing water covering a roadway?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: Never drive through standing water on a road, since it may be deeper than it looks and part of the road may be washed out.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: What depth of fast-moving water sweeps a car sideways, and what depth floats or rolls it?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: About six inches of fast-moving water can sweep a car off the road, and about twelve inches can float it or roll it over.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: How do six inches and twelve inches of rushing floodwater differ in what they do to a passenger car?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: About six inches of fast water can sweep a car off the road, while about twelve inches can float or overturn it.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: What full sequence of steps keeps you alive when fog grows so thick you can barely see?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.memory_hook: Pull far off, flashers, exit right
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: If fog is so thick you can barely see, pull well off the road, stop, secure the car, turn on the flashers, exit on the passenger side and stay away from the road.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: Which headlight beam, speed habit, and traffic checks apply when you must drive through lighter fog?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: If you must drive in fog, use low beams, slow down, watch for the taillights ahead and keep an eye on vehicles behind you.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: How does your fog game-plan switch between blinding zero-visibility fog and passable mist?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: In thick fog you pull far off and exit on the passenger side, while in drivable fog you use low beams and watch for the taillights ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: Which three roadway spots freeze over before regular ground-supported asphalt as temperatures drop?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: Bridges, overpasses and shady spots are often the first places to freeze as temperatures fall.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: Besides running wipers and low beams in snow, how drastically should you cut speed on packed snow versus glare ice?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: In a snowstorm, slow down and use wipers and low beams; cut speed by more than half on packed snow and slow to a crawl on ice.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.front: How should you accelerate and test grip on snow or ice, including in a manual-transmission car?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.expected_back: On snow or ice, speed up gently, test your steering and braking feel, and in a manual car start in second gear or higher with a slow clutch release.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.front: How much extra stopping distance should you leave on snow or ice, and what slows the car best?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.expected_back: Allow at least three times the normal stopping distance on snow or ice, and when stopping keep off the brake so the engine slows the car.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: Why does North Carolina pair triple stopping distance on snow and ice with staying off the brake pedal?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: On snow or ice allow at least three times the normal stopping distance, and to stop you lift off the brake and let the engine do the slowing.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.front: Do tire chains and snow tires let you start, stop, or steer briskly on packed snow and ice?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.expected_back: Chains and snow tires can still slide on ice and packed snow, so you cannot start, stop or steer quickly in those conditions.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.front: What two driving habits cut down wildlife strikes, especially around twilight and night?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.expected_back: Wildlife collisions can be reduced by slowing down and scanning road edges, especially at dawn, dusk and into the night.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.front: How does hitting a deer at thirty-five miles per hour compare with striking one at fifty-five or faster?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.expected_back: Slower speed improves survival for both deer and driver: a deer hit at thirty-five miles per hour is far less likely to be fatal than one hit at fifty-five miles per hour or more.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.front: During which daily hours and yearly seasons must drivers watch hardest for crossing animals?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.expected_back: Animals are most active at dawn, at dusk and in the first few hours after dark, and spring and fall migrations call for extra caution.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.front: When should you use high beams in animal country—and why switch them off when an animal stands ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.expected_back: Use high beams only when there is no oncoming traffic and no animal right ahead, since bright lights can freeze some animals in place.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: Why must you drop out of high beams even with zero oncoming cars once an animal appears on the road?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Use high beams only with no oncoming traffic and no animal directly ahead, because bright beams can freeze some animals in the road.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.front: Once a single deer darts across your lane, what should you immediately expect?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.expected_back: Many animals such as deer travel in groups, so after seeing one, expect others to follow close behind.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.front: How should you steer, brake, and warn if an animal steps directly into your roadway?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.expected_back: When an animal is in the roadway, hold your lane and brake firmly to stop if you can; a short honk of the horn is also an option.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: Which two sides of your health shape how you drive, and what health standard does holding a driver license require?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Both physical and mental health shape how you drive, and a driver license requires that you be in good health.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: How can a short-term illness like a cold, headache, or flu affect you behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: Even a short illness such as a cold, a headache or the flu can leave you less alert and slower to respond behind the wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: At fifty-five miles per hour, how fast does a car cover a football field—making even a brief nod-off deadly?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: At fifty-five miles per hour a vehicle covers the length of a football field in three point seven seconds, so even a brief nod-off is dangerous.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: How severe are drowsy-driving crashes typically, and where and under what cabin condition do they happen most often?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Crashes caused by drowsiness tend to be serious and happen most often on fast rural highways when the driver is traveling alone.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: What warning signs tell you that drowsiness is taking over while you drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Signs of drowsiness include not remembering the last few miles, hitting a rumble strip or drifting out of your lane, yawning again and again, and struggling to focus or keep your eyes open.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: What should you do when you grow tired behind the wheel, and how much does a short nap with caffeine help?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: If you grow tired while driving you should stop; a nap of fifteen to forty-five minutes and some caffeine help only for a while.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: How often should you stop on a long road trip, and what should you do during each break?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: On a long drive, take a break at least every two hours: leave the car, stretch and walk briskly.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: What daily mileage ceiling and medication precaution does the handbook recommend for road trips?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: The handbook suggests capping your driving at about three hundred to four hundred miles a day and avoiding medicines that make you drowsy.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: How does the emergency nap-and-caffeine tactic differ from the standard long-trip break rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: A short nap with caffeine is only a temporary help for fatigue, while the long-trip habit is a stop at least every two hours.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: How does the North Carolina handbook define distracted driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: Distracted driving means any activity that might pull your attention away from the main job of driving.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: Beyond texting and phone calls, what everyday cabin activities does the handbook list as common driving distractions?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Common distractions include texting, phone use, eating or drinking, talking with passengers, grooming, reading maps, using navigation, watching video and adjusting audio equipment.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: How does distraction hurt your reaction speed and hazard detection on the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: Distracted drivers respond more slowly to events such as a car slowing to turn or pulling out of a side road, and they miss hazards like pedestrians or debris more often.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: What physical control problem makes many distractions especially dangerous during a sudden emergency?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Many distractions make it harder to steer clear of a crash because they take at least one hand off the steering wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Under what narrow circumstances—and timing—does the handbook advise using a phone on a trip?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: Use a phone while driving only when truly necessary, for emergencies or to reach a parent, legal guardian or spouse, and only at a safe time and place.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: What three practical phone habits does the handbook recommend before and during a drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: Let a passenger make the call for you, let unanswered calls go to a message, and secure the phone so it cannot fly around in a crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: Which cell-phone actions are illegal for every driver on North Carolina streets, highways, and public vehicular areas?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: North Carolina makes it unlawful to text or email on a cell phone while driving on a public street, highway or public vehicular area.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: What cell-phone rule applies to a driver under eighteen while the vehicle is moving, and what is the lone exception?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: A driver under eighteen may not use a cell phone or related technology at all while the vehicle is moving, except to call nine one one in an emergency.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How does North Carolina's cell-phone ban for all drivers differ from the stricter ban for drivers under eighteen?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: Every driver is barred from texting or emailing while driving, but a driver under eighteen is barred from using a phone at all while moving, apart from a nine one one emergency call.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: What mobile-device rule applies to anyone operating a school bus on a public road or vehicular area?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: No one may drive a school bus on a public road or vehicular area while using a cell phone or other mobile-device technology.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: How do the texting and under-eighteen phone rules differ legally from the handbook's family-call advice?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: The texting ban and the under-eighteen ban are laws, while advice to use a phone only for emergencies or family contact is a safety reminder rather than a separate legal rule.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: Which categories of medicine can impair driving, and what two precautions should you take when using them?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: Both prescription and over-the-counter medicines can affect driving, so learn how a medicine affects you and drive as little as possible while taking it.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Roughly what percentage of all traffic deaths involve alcohol, according to the North Carolina handbook?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: The handbook states that about thirty-eight percent of all traffic deaths involve alcohol.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: What category of drug is alcohol, and how does it change brain speed behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the brain, so you cannot respond, decide or react quickly.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: How does alcohol distort a driver's sense of speed, distance, and personal risk?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: Alcohol weakens your judgment of speed and of distance to other cars, people or objects, and gives false confidence that leads to bigger risks.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: Why do impaired drivers often miss signals, side-street cars, or walkers while concentrating on steering—and what else suffers?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Alcohol makes it hard to handle more than one task, so while steering you may miss traffic lights, cars from side streets or pedestrians; it also upsets balance and causes sleepiness.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: What is the single thing that sobers up a drinker—and which three popular remedies fail?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Only time sobers a drinker; coffee, a large meal or a cold shower will not.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: Why will drinking coffee, eating a large meal, or taking a cold shower never make an impaired person safe to drive?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: Coffee, a big meal and a cold shower do nothing to sober a drinker; only the passing of time does.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: What practical alternatives does the handbook suggest so nobody ever drinks and drives?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Ways to avoid drinking and driving include planning a ride in advance, sharing a taxi, taking public transit, staying overnight with a friend, or riding with someone who has not been drinking.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: Across a typical driving lifetime, what are the approximate odds of suffering serious injury or death in a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Across a typical lifetime behind the wheel, the odds of a serious injury or death in a crash are roughly one in three.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Who must wear a properly fastened seat belt whenever a belt-equipped vehicle moves forward on a North Carolina road?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: In a vehicle built with seat belts, the driver and every passenger must wear a properly fastened belt whenever the vehicle moves forward on a North Carolina street or highway.
