sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: How do air bags or automatic shoulder harnesses affect your legal duty to fasten seat belts and lap belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: Seat belts are still required in vehicles with air bags, and if the vehicle has automatic shoulder harnesses the lap belt must also be worn.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: Why is riding unbuckled illegal even when your car features both air bags and motorized shoulder harnesses?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Air bags never excuse the seat belt, and a vehicle with an automatic shoulder harness still requires the lap belt to be fastened.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: When does a medical, physical, or psychological condition exempt someone from North Carolina's seat-belt mandate?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: The seat belt law exempts an occupant of a noncommercial vehicle whose medical or physical condition, or professionally certified phobia, prevents proper restraint.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: Which two groups of on-duty delivery carriers are exempted from wearing seat belts along their routes?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: Rural letter carriers of the Postal Service on duty and newspaper carriers delivering along their route are exempt from the seat belt law.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Under what speed ceiling are frequent-stop delivery drivers or passengers exempt from fastening seat belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: Drivers or passengers who keep stopping to leave the vehicle or deliver items are exempt if the vehicle goes no faster than twenty miles per hour between stops.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: What exact speed limit keeps the frequent-delivery seat-belt exemption legal between stops?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: The frequent-delivery seat belt exemption applies only if the vehicle stays at or below twenty miles per hour between stops.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: Which three farming, vehicle-equipment, or full-seating situations are exempt from the North Carolina seat-belt law?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: Other exemptions cover property-carrying vehicles used for farming within the state, vehicles not legally required to have belts, and situations where every belted or restraint-equipped seat is already taken.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: Who can ride unbuckled in a motor home, and what living-facility count must that motor home meet?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: In a motor home, occupants other than the driver and front-seat passengers are exempt when the motor home has at least four of the listed living facilities.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: Out of every ten children killed while riding unrestrained, how many could properly used safety seats save?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: Correctly used safety seats could save seven of every ten children who die while riding unrestrained.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: What defines the best child safety seat, and where can families find affordable rental programs?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: The best child seat is one used on every ride that fits your car and has a comfortable harness or shield, and low-cost rentals are often offered by local groups, hospitals and health departments.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: Up to what passenger age is the driver legally responsible for securing young riders in federally compliant restraints or belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: A driver carrying any passenger under sixteen must make sure each one is secured in a child restraint or seat belt meeting the federal standards in force when it was made.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: Which age and weight combination requires a child to ride in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: A child younger than eight who weighs under eighty pounds must ride in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: When a vehicle has an active front passenger airbag and a rear seat, which children must ride in back?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: When a vehicle has an active front passenger air bag and a rear seat, a child under five weighing under forty pounds must ride in the rear unless the restraint is built for use with a front air bag.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How do the age-and-weight thresholds differ between the child-restraint rule and the front-airbag rear-seat rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: A child under eight and under eighty pounds needs a weight-appropriate restraint, while the rear-seat rule near an active front air bag covers a child under five and under forty pounds.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.front: When may a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds be secured with a properly fitted lap belt alone?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.expected_back: If no seat has a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint, a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds may ride with a properly fitted lap belt alone.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: What seating condition must be true before a forty-to-eighty-pound child under eight may legally use a lap belt alone?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: A lap belt alone is allowed for a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds only when no seat has a lap and shoulder belt for the restraint.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.front: How long should children stay in a booster seat after outgrowing harnessed seats, and how must an adult belt fit?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.expected_back: Children who have outgrown safety seats should use federally compliant booster seats until an adult belt fits: lap belt snug on the hips, not the stomach, and shoulder belt across the shoulder and chest, not the face or throat.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.front: At up to what speed does an airbag burst from the dashboard during a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.expected_back: An air bag bursts out of the dashboard at up to two hundred miles per hour, faster than an eye blink, so it is far from a soft pillow.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.front: Where does the handbook say children aged twelve and younger should ride?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.expected_back: Children aged twelve and younger should ride buckled up in a rear seat.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.front: Where must an infant in a rear-facing safety seat never be placed?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.expected_back: An infant in a rear-facing safety seat must never ride in the front seat of a vehicle that has a passenger-side air bag.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.front: Where across your body should the lap belt and shoulder belt rest to work safely alongside airbags?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.expected_back: Air bags only supplement belts: wear the lap belt under the abdomen and low on the hips, and the shoulder belt over the collarbone, away from the neck and across the breastbone.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.front: How should the driver and front passenger seats be positioned relative to the dashboard, especially for shorter riders?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.expected_back: Move the driver and front passenger seats as far back as practical, especially for shorter people.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.front: Who must wear a safety helmet on a motorcycle or moped, and which federal standard must that helmet meet?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.expected_back: Every motorcycle or moped operator and passenger must wear a safety helmet meeting Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard two hundred eighteen.

sec06-card-sec06-F46.front: What liner feature and manufacturer marking identify a compliant motorcycle helmet—and what about aftermarket stickers?
sec06-card-sec06-F46.expected_back: A compliant helmet has a firm polystyrene liner about one inch thick and a DOT symbol fixed permanently on the back by the maker; a sticker added later does not make it legal.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: Why does slapping a separately purchased DOT sticker onto a helmet fail to make it legal?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: A DOT symbol fixed permanently by the manufacturer marks a compliant helmet, while a DOT sticker sold separately or added by the rider does not.

sec06-card-sec06-F47.front: Which age group is barred from riding in the open cargo bed of a pickup truck, and who bears responsibility?
sec06-card-sec06-F47.expected_back: North Carolina bars children younger than sixteen from riding in the open bed of a pickup truck, and the driver is responsible for compliance, though the statute has some exemptions.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: How does the age guideline for riding in a car's rear seat compare with the age ban for open pickup beds?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Riding in the rear seat is advised for children twelve and under, while riding in an open pickup bed is prohibited by law for children under sixteen.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Which four situations exempt children from North Carolina's ban on riding in an open pickup bed?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: The pickup-bed rule for children does not apply when a supervising adult rides in the bed, in an emergency, in a parade, or while the vehicle serves an agricultural enterprise.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: What fine and record impact come with violating the child pickup-bed rule?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Breaking the pickup-bed rule brings a ticket and a twenty-five dollars fine; it is an infraction with no court costs, license points or insurance surcharge.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: How much hotter than outside air can a sunny parked car climb, even with a window cracked?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: A parked car in the sun can get roughly forty to fifty degrees hotter inside than outside, even with a window cracked, so leaving children or animals inside can cause heat stroke or death.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: Why is warming up a car dangerous when snow blocks the tailpipe?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: In winter, snow blocking the exhaust pipe while the car warms up can force carbon monoxide inside; the gas cannot be seen, smelled or tasted but is poisonous.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: Who holds the right of way in marked or unmarked crosswalks where no traffic signals exist?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: At an intersection with no traffic signals, pedestrians in a marked crosswalk, or in an unmarked one formed by extending the sidewalk lines, have the right of way.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: Which lights govern pedestrians at signalized intersections without dedicated walk signals, and when shouldn't they start?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: Where ordinary signals control an intersection, pedestrians follow the same signals as drivers going their direction and should not begin crossing on red or yellow.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: Who has the right of way when a pedestrian crosses on green and a vehicle turns across that path?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: A pedestrian crossing on a green signal has the right of way over every vehicle, including one turning across the pedestrian's path.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: How does a pedestrian's right to cross on green contrast with starting across on yellow or red?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: A pedestrian crossing on green has the right of way even over a turning car, while a pedestrian should not start crossing on red or yellow.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: How must drivers act when a signal shifts to yellow or red with someone still mid-crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: If the light turns yellow or red while a pedestrian is still in the street, drivers must let that person finish crossing safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: Which three mobility cues give a blind pedestrian special legal protection at an unsignaled intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: At an unsignaled intersection the law gives special consideration to a blind pedestrian who holds out a white cane, a red-tipped white cane, or has a guide dog.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Which signal rules pedestrians where Walk and Don't Walk lights operate, and what does Walk grant?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Where Walk and Don't Walk signals operate, pedestrians obey them instead of the regular lights, and crossing on Walk gives them the same right of way as a green light.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: When both regular traffic lights and Walk or Don't Walk signals are working, which governs pedestrians?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Walk and Don't Walk signals, when operating, override the regular traffic lights for pedestrians.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: How should you respond if you have a green light and a pedestrian steps out against red?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: If you are going through on green and a pedestrian steps into your path against a red signal, warn them with your horn.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: When must you sound your horn around pedestrians, and what if a walker keeps moving without right of way?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: The law requires a horn warning whenever a turn, stop or start from a parked spot may affect a pedestrian, and if the pedestrian keeps going the driver must stop; yield even when the pedestrian is not entitled to it.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: What is the maximum legal speed for a regular North Carolina school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: A school bus may travel no faster than forty-five miles per hour

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: During which morning and afternoon time windows does the handbook urge extra caution for school buses?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Be especially careful during school bus hours, generally seven to nine a.m. and two to four p.m.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What triggers a mandatory school-bus stop, and which three things must happen before you drive again?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: When a school bus shows its mechanical stop arm or flashing red lights to load or unload, approaching drivers must stop and stay stopped until the arm is withdrawn, the lights go off and the bus begins moving.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: May you proceed once children finish crossing in front of a stopped school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: The school bus stop applies whenever the stop arm is out or the red lights flash, and it lasts until the arm is withdrawn, the lights go off and the bus moves again, not just until the children have crossed.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: Which directions of traffic must stop when a school bus halts for passengers on a two-lane road?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: On a two-lane road, traffic in both directions must stop for a school bus that stops for passengers.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.front: Who must stop for a school bus on a two-lane road that has a center turning lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.expected_back: On a two-lane road with a center turning lane, all traffic in both directions stops for the school bus.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.front: Who must stop for a school bus on a four-lane road that has no median separation?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.expected_back: On a four-lane road with no median separation, all traffic in both directions stops for the school bus.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: On a highway having at least four travel lanes plus a center turn lane, who stops for a school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: On a road of four or more lanes with a center turning lane, only the traffic behind a stopped school bus has to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: When a median divides a highway with at least four lanes, which drivers stop for a school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: On a divided highway of four or more lanes with a median, only traffic following the school bus must stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: Which multi-lane or turn-lane road setups stop both directions for a school bus versus following traffic only?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: A two-lane road with a center turning lane and a four-lane road with no median both require traffic in both directions to stop for a school bus, while a divided highway with a median or a road of four or more lanes with a turning lane requires only following traffic to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: Which four emergency vehicle types always hold right of way when running flashing lights and sirens?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Police cars, ambulances, fire engines and rescue vehicles using flashing lights and sirens always have the right of way.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: How should you respond when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches from ahead or behind?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: When an emergency vehicle approaches from ahead or behind, pull to the right-hand curb or edge and stop completely, staying there until it passes or an officer waves you on.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: Which drivers are exempt from pulling over and stopping for an approaching emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Every vehicle must yield to an approaching emergency vehicle, except traffic going the opposite way on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: On undivided or ordinary roads do both directions yield to emergency vehicles, and what is the lone exception?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: Drivers in both directions yield to an approaching emergency vehicle, and the only exception is opposite-direction traffic on a four-lane limited-access highway with a center median.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: How close to a responder vehicle halted at a wreck or roadside scene is parking forbidden?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Do not park within one hundred feet of an emergency vehicle stopped at a crash or giving assistance.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: How far back must you stay from fire trucks answering an alarm, and what must you never cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Stay at least one block away from fire trucks answering an alarm, and never drive over a fire hose.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: How does the crash-scene parking buffer compare with the distance kept from fire trucks answering an alarm?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: The parking buffer near an emergency vehicle stopped at a crash is one hundred feet, while the buffer from fire trucks answering an alarm is one block.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.front: What does the move-over law require on a multi-lane road when a lit emergency or service rig sits within twelve feet?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.expected_back: Move-over law: when an authorized emergency or public service vehicle with warning lights on is parked within twelve feet of the road and you have two or more lanes your way, change out of the lane closest to it and stay out until clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.front: What does the move-over law require when you have only one lane in your direction past a stopped emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.expected_back: If you have only one lane in your direction, slow down and keep a reduced, safe speed until you are fully past the stopped emergency vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: How does your move-over duty change between two-plus lanes and a single lane in your direction?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: With two or more lanes in your direction the move-over law means changing lanes away from the stopped vehicle, but with only one lane it means slowing to a reduced safe speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.front: What three immediate steps should you take when police lights or a siren come on behind your car?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.expected_back: When police lights or a siren appear behind you, stay calm, signal, and pull to the right off the travel lanes at the nearest safe spot.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.front: How do you acknowledge an officer behind you when there is no safe place to pull over right away?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.expected_back: With no safe place to stop right away, switch on your four-way flashers and slow by about ten miles per hour to show the officer you know, then drive lawfully to the nearest safe area.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: Should you stop directly inside an active travel lane if police signal you where no shoulder exists?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: When police signal you and no safe stop exists, you slow by about ten miles per hour with four-way flashers and keep going, rather than stopping in the travel lane.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.front: What may you do before pulling over if you genuinely doubt whether an unmarked vehicle is real law enforcement?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.expected_back: If you honestly doubt that an unmarked car is real police, you may call nine one one before pulling over and give your name and location to confirm the stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.front: Once pulled over for police, what do you do with gear, window, engine, electronics, and seat belts?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.expected_back: Once stopped, shift to Park, lower the window, turn off the engine and silence devices; everyone stays seated, and you keep your seat belt on unless the officer asks otherwise.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.front: Where should the driver, front passenger, and back-seat passengers keep their hands during a traffic stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.expected_back: Keep both hands on the steering wheel, have passengers keep their hands visible, and have back-seat riders rest their hands on the front seatback.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.front: What does North Carolina law require you to give at a stop, and what about further questioning?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.expected_back: State law requires you to identify yourself and hand over your license and vehicle registration; after that you may decide whether to answer further questions.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: How does your legal duty to show license and registration compare with answering additional officer questions?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: You must identify yourself and produce your license and registration, but after that answering further questions is your choice.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.front: How must weapons be stored without a permit, and what must a concealed-carry permit holder tell the officer?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.expected_back: Never reach for a weapon during a stop; a weapon must be in plain view or locked away unless there is a proper permit, and a concealed weapon permit holder must tell the officer a weapon is in the vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.front: During a traffic stop, when may occupants exit the car or search under seats and in the glove box?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.expected_back: Do not get out, or let passengers get out, unless told to, and do not dig under seats or in the glove box for documents unless the officer asks.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.front: Does signing a North Carolina traffic citation admit guilt, and where do you contest it?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.expected_back: Signing a traffic ticket does not admit guilt; argue your side in court rather than at the roadside.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.front: What charge grade applies if someone resists, delays, or obstructs law enforcement at a roadside stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.expected_back: Resisting, delaying or obstructing an officer during a traffic stop is a class two misdemeanor.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.front: What steps should you take if you believe an officer acted improperly during a stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.expected_back: If you believe an officer behaved improperly, write down what happened and report it promptly to the officer's agency, whose name appears on the ticket.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: What happens to a driver whose failure to signal forces a motorcyclist to switch lanes, leave the road, or crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: A driver who fails to signal properly and forces a motorcycle to change lanes or leave the road will be charged and fined, and the same applies if a crash with damage or injury results.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.front: Under what weather, light, and pavement conditions—and in what crash types—do most farm-equipment wrecks happen?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.expected_back: Most crashes with farm equipment happen on clear days, in daylight, on dry paved roads, and they are usually sideswipes or angle crashes.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.front: What misread maneuver frequently causes drivers to crash while trying to pass farm machinery?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.expected_back: These crashes often happen when farm machinery slows to turn left and a following driver tries to pass, sometimes after mistaking the operator's left-hand signal for a wave to pass.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.front: May you pass slow farm machinery in a no-passing zone, and what visual hazard hides from behind?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.expected_back: Passing farm equipment in a no-passing zone is illegal, and the machine may be wider than it looks from behind.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.front: When is the only advisable moment to pass farm equipment on a public road?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.expected_back: The only advisable time to pass farm equipment on a public road is when the operator pulls off at a practical spot to let traffic by.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: How do no-passing zones and operator pull-offs govern passing farm machinery?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: Passing farm equipment in a no-passing zone is illegal, and the only advisable pass is after the operator pulls off the road to let traffic by.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.front: What front light and rear light—or reflector substitute—must farm equipment display?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.expected_back: Farm equipment must show one white light in front and a red light at the rear visible for up to five hundred feet, or two red reflectors at least four inches across in place of that rear light.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.front: How does North Carolina law classify bicycles, and do impaired-driving laws apply to cyclists?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.expected_back: North Carolina law treats bicycles as vehicles, so bicyclists must obey the same traffic laws as drivers, including the DWI laws.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.front: Where should motorists expect to encounter bicyclists, and when might a cyclist take the entire lane?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.expected_back: Drivers should expect bicyclists in the roadway, and traffic conditions may require a bicyclist to use the full travel lane.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.front: Which three road spaces may cyclists use, and what three factors guide that choice?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.expected_back: Bicyclists may ride in a bike lane, on a paved shoulder or in a regular travel lane, choosing based on road conditions, hazards and conflicts with right-turning cars.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.front: Which three core roadway rules must bicyclists obey just like motor-vehicle drivers?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.expected_back: Like drivers, bicyclists must ride on the right side of the road, stop for stop signs and red lights, and give hand signals.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.front: When may you overtake a bicyclist, and what is the safest way to pass?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.expected_back: Pass a bicyclist only with plenty of clearance and no oncoming traffic in the other lane; changing lanes is the safest way to pass.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.front: Which passing statutes govern overtaking a bicycle on a North Carolina road?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.expected_back: Passing a bicyclist lawfully means following the same vehicle passing laws that apply to passing any other vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.front: Why must bicyclists always ride with the flow of traffic rather than facing it?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.expected_back: Bicyclists should ride with the flow of traffic, never facing it, because drivers often fail to look toward a wrong-way rider.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.front: Where are bicycles allowed, and which three classic car-versus-bike crash patterns must you watch for?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.expected_back: Expect bicycles on every road except where they are expressly banned, and watch for left-cross, drive-out and right-hook collisions.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.front: What front and rear visibility distances are required on a bicycle ridden at night?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.expected_back: At night a bicycle must have a front light visible from at least three hundred feet and a rear red light or reflector visible from at least two hundred feet.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.front: How does a bicycle's required nighttime front-light distance compare with its rear red visibility distance?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.expected_back: A bicycle at night needs a front light seen from three hundred feet but a rear red light or reflector seen from only two hundred feet.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.front: Which bicycle riders and passengers must wear an approved helmet and use a saddle seat?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.expected_back: Every bicycle rider and passenger under age sixteen must wear an approved bicycle helmet and sit on a saddle seat.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.front: What weight or height cutoff requires a young bicycle passenger to ride in a restraining seat?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.expected_back: A bicycle passenger under forty pounds or under forty inches tall must ride in a bicycle restraining seat.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.front: How does the age cutoff for bicycle helmets differ from the size cutoff for restraining seats?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.expected_back: The bicycle helmet rule covers riders and passengers under sixteen, while the restraining seat rule covers passengers under forty pounds or forty inches.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.front: What share of crash deaths are pedestrians in cities compared with rural areas?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.expected_back: In cities about two of every five people killed in motor vehicle crashes are pedestrians, compared with about one in ten in rural areas.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.front: How much higher is the pedestrian share of motor-vehicle deaths in cities than in rural areas?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.expected_back: Pedestrians make up about two of every five crash deaths in cities but only about one in ten in rural areas.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.front: Which three groups make up most pedestrians killed in traffic crashes?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.expected_back: Most pedestrians killed are children, elderly people or people who had been drinking.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.front: Which side of the road should pedestrians use, and what color helps drivers spot them?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.expected_back: Pedestrians should walk on the left side of the road facing traffic and wear or carry something white.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.front: What should you carry and stay ready to do when walking along a road after dark?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.expected_back: On foot at night, carry a flashlight and be ready to step aside, since drivers may not see you.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.front: How does the safe side of the road for a pedestrian differ from the legal side for a bicyclist?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.expected_back: Pedestrians walk on the left facing traffic, which is the opposite of the ride-with-traffic rule for bicyclists.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.front: How do heavy trucks accelerate—especially uphill—and how can their sheer size trick your eyes?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.expected_back: Heavy trucks gain speed slowly, especially uphill, and their size can make them seem slower than they really are.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.front: Why do big trucks swing wide on turns, and what must you check before passing one drifting left?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.expected_back: A truck's rear wheels do not follow its front wheels, so it needs extra room to turn; check its turn signal before passing a truck that seems to start a left turn.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.front: What happens to a heavy truck's brakes on long downhill grades, and how does stopping change?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.expected_back: Truck brakes heat up on downhill runs, which means the truck needs more distance to stop.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.front: How can passing or riding beside a large truck affect your car's handling?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.expected_back: Wind currents from a large truck beside you can affect your steering, so give trucks plenty of room.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.front: Why is it dangerous to assume a truck driver sitting twice as high as you can see everything?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.expected_back: Truck drivers sit about twice as high as car drivers, but it is a false assumption that they can see everything around them.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.front: How far do a tractor-trailer's blind no-zones stretch in front, beside, and behind the rig?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.expected_back: A tractor-trailer's no-zones reach up to twenty feet in front of the cab, along both sides especially beside the cab, and up to two hundred feet behind.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.front: How many times longer is a truck's rear no-zone compared with its front no-zone?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.expected_back: A truck's front no-zone extends up to twenty feet, but its rear no-zone extends up to two hundred feet.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.front: Why must you never linger in a truck's no-zone, and what quick mirror check tells if you're visible?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.expected_back: Lingering in a truck's no-zone makes it harder for the trucker to steer clear of danger; if you cannot see the driver in the side mirror, the driver cannot see you.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.front: How do recreational vehicles compare with passenger cars in size, acceleration, braking, and turns?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.expected_back: Recreational vehicles are typically longer, higher and wider than cars, speed up and stop more slowly, and need more turning room.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.front: What happens to sightlines on both ends when you follow closely behind a recreational vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.expected_back: The closer you get to a recreational vehicle, the more it blocks your view, and its driver has much larger blind spots than a car driver.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.front: What two stability hazards should you anticipate around a vehicle pulling a trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.expected_back: Near a vehicle towing a trailer, watch for sway in crosswinds or on slippery curves, and know that sudden braking can make the trailer jackknife.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.front: How much clear road ahead can it take to safely overtake a vehicle towing a trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.expected_back: Passing a trailer and its towing vehicle safely can take a half mile of clear road.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.front: What passing-distance and hard-braking facts go hand in hand around towed trailers?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.expected_back: Passing a vehicle towing a trailer may need a half mile of clear road, and braking hard near it risks a jackknife.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.front: How much right-of-way respect do motorcycle and moped riders get compared with four-wheeled vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.expected_back: Give motorcycle and moped riders the same right-of-way consideration as any other driver.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.front: How much lane width belongs to a motorcycle, and how must you pass one?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.expected_back: A motorcycle is entitled to its full lane, so pass it by changing lanes exactly as you would for a larger vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.front: Where in the lane do mopeds ride, and what minimum clearance must you leave on their left?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.expected_back: Mopeds ride on the right side of the lane, and when passing one you must stay at least two feet to its left.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.front: How does passing a motorcycle legally differ from passing a moped in North Carolina?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.expected_back: To pass a motorcycle you change lanes because it owns its full lane, while to pass a moped you keep at least two feet to its left.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.front: Why is generous side clearance critical whenever your car passes any two-wheeled rider?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.expected_back: Leave enough room when passing any cyclist so your vehicle's windstream cannot make the rider lose control.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.front: Before which maneuvers—and one turn in particular—must you double-check blind spots for motorcycles and mopeds?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.expected_back: Motorcycles and mopeds can be completely hidden in blind spots, so look for them before turning, changing lanes or pulling out, especially when turning left.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.front: What share of North Carolina motorcycle crashes involve a car, and who is usually at fault?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.expected_back: About two-thirds of North Carolina motorcycle crashes involve a car, and in most of them the car driver is at fault, often saying the motorcycle went unseen.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.front: When do motorcycles stop faster than cars, and what two conditions make them stop slower?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.expected_back: Most motorcycles stop faster than cars, but they stop more slowly with a passenger or on poor surfaces where hard braking could cause a fall.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.front: Which two situations stretch out a motorcycle's stopping distance compared with dry solo riding?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.expected_back: Motorcycles usually stop faster than cars, but more slowly with a passenger or on poor road surfaces.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.front: Which four loose or wet road hazards threaten riders ahead, and what does wobbling tell you?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.expected_back: Sand, gravel, wet leaves or water on the pavement can make a rider ahead lose control, and a wobbling or hesitant rider is likely a beginner who needs extra room.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.front: How should you adjust following distance behind a motorcycle or moped on slick pavement, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.expected_back: Never crowd a motorcycle or moped, and leave a longer following distance on slippery roads because two wheels are easily destabilized.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.front: At which three rough or metal roadway features should you give riders extra space?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.expected_back: Give riders extra room at railroad crossings, on rough roads and on metal surfaces such as steel bridge joints and grating.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.front: What federal helmet standard and strap rule apply to every moped operator and passenger?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.expected_back: Moped riders and all passengers must wear a helmet meeting Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard two hundred eighteen with the retention strap fastened.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.front: What wheel count, engine-size cap, and transmission rule define a moped in North Carolina?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.expected_back: North Carolina defines a moped as a two- or three-wheeled vehicle with a motor of no more than fifty cubic centimeters and no external shifting device.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.front: What is the legal top speed of a moped, and are faster-built models allowed on North Carolina roads?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.expected_back: A moped's top speed may not exceed thirty miles per hour, and mopeds built to go faster are illegal to use in North Carolina.

sec16-card-sec16-F40.front: What minimum age and credential are required to ride a moped on public roads, and what about DWI?
sec16-card-sec16-F40.expected_back: To operate a moped on a public road you must be at least sixteen and hold a valid N.C. driver license or ID card, and impaired driving laws apply to moped riders too.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.front: What are North Carolina's three headline numbers for moped engine size, top speed, and rider age?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.expected_back: A moped is limited to a motor of fifty cubic centimeters and a top speed of thirty miles per hour, and its operator must be at least sixteen.

sec16-card-sec16-F41.front: Where in the lane should moped riders stay, and what two lane-sharing moves must they avoid?
sec16-card-sec16-F41.expected_back: Moped riders should keep right in the lane, never share a lane with another vehicle, and never squeeze between parked cars and moving traffic at an intersection.

sec16-card-sec16-F42.front: What clothing colors and turn signals should moped riders use to stay conspicuous?
sec16-card-sec16-F42.expected_back: Moped riders should wear light or bright clothing and use electric turn signals if fitted, or hand signals otherwise.

sec16-card-sec16-F43.front: Since July 2015, what DMV registration and plate rules apply to every North Carolina moped?
sec16-card-sec16-F43.expected_back: Since July two thousand fifteen, every moped must be registered with the DMV and display a license plate on the rear at all times.

sec16-card-sec16-F45.front: Which DMV form proves moped ownership when the owner lacks a manufacturer's certificate of origin?
sec16-card-sec16-F45.memory_hook: File affidavit M V R fifty-eight
sec16-card-sec16-F45.expected_back: A moped owner without the manufacturer's certificate of origin can use form MVR-fifty-eight, an affidavit of facts, as proof of ownership.

sec16-card-sec16-R10.front: When did moped registration become mandatory, and what backup form covers missing origin paperwork?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.expected_back: Moped registration has been required since July two thousand fifteen, and an owner lacking the certificate of origin may file form MVR-fifty-eight instead.

sec16-card-sec16-F46.front: Who is held legally responsible when trash is tossed or blown out of a moving vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F46.expected_back: Littering is illegal in North Carolina, and the driver is held responsible when litter is thrown or blown from the vehicle.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.front: How does the fine range for a first littering conviction compare with a repeat offense within three years?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.expected_back: A first littering conviction is fined two hundred fifty dollars to one thousand dollars, while a repeat within three years is fined five hundred dollars to two thousand dollars.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: What license status applies to every North Carolina driver under eighteen, and why do special laws govern them?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: Every driver under eighteen is a provisional licensee, and special laws apply because this group has a much higher crash rate.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Which North Carolina residents by age and vehicle class qualify for a Level One Limited Learner Permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.memory_hook: Ages fifteen to seventeen, Class C
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: The Level One Limited Learner Permit is for North Carolina residents at least fifteen but under eighteen who will drive vehicles needing a Class C license.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What driver education certificate — including minimum classroom and behind-the-wheel hours — must a teen present before taking the permit test?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: Before taking the permit test, a teen must show a certificate for an approved driver education course with at least thirty hours in the classroom and six hours behind the wheel.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: When a driver is under eighteen, for which tests must they present that thirty-plus-six driver education certificate beforehand?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: A driver under eighteen must show the driver education certificate, at least thirty classroom hours and six behind-the-wheel hours, before testing for either a learner permit or a license.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: Which three tests must a Level One Limited Learner Permit applicant pass?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: A Level One applicant must pass the written, sign and vision tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Who must sign the application for a minor's learner permit or driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: A parent or legal guardian must sign for a minor's permit or license.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: Who is allowed to serve as a Level One supervising driver, and how long must they have held a valid license?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: A supervising driver must be a parent, grandparent or guardian, or a responsible adult the parent or guardian approves, and must hold a valid license that has been held for at least five years.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: During the first six months with a Level One permit, what daily hours and supervision rule apply?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: For the first six months, a Level One permit holder may drive only from five a.m. to nine p.m., and only with the supervising driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: Once you have held a Level One permit for six full months, how do your legal driving hours and supervision rules stand?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Once six months have passed since Level One was issued, the holder may drive at any hour, still with a supervising driver.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Across both time phases of a Level One permit, what changes after month six and what never changes?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: Level One has two time phases: in the first six months driving is limited to five a.m. to nine p.m., and after that any hour is allowed, but a supervising driver is required in both phases.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Under a Level One permit, what restraint rule covers every rider, and who is allowed in the front row?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: With a Level One permit, every passenger must wear a seat belt or ride in a child safety seat, and only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: Which graduated licensing stage restricts the front seat strictly to the teen driver and the supervising driver?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: The front-seat rule belongs to Level One: only the driver and the supervising driver may sit in front.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: Where is a Level One driver barred from using a cell phone or any connected cell-phone technology while driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: A Level One driver may not use a cell phone or any connected cell-phone technology while driving on a public street, highway or public vehicular area.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: Which specific recipients make up the only cell-phone exception for a North Carolina teen driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: The only cell phone exception for a teen driver is an emergency call to an emergency operator, a hospital, doctor's office or clinic, an ambulance service, a fire department, a law enforcement agency, or a parent, legal guardian or spouse.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: How many months must a teen hold the Level One permit before applying for a Limited Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A teen must keep the Level One permit for nine months before applying for the Limited Provisional License.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: How many total behind-the-wheel hours — and how many night hours — must appear on the Level One driving log?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: The Level One driving log must record at least sixty hours behind the wheel, with at least ten of those hours at night.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: How does the driving log define daytime driving versus night driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: For the log, daytime driving means sunrise to sunset while there is daylight, and night driving means after sunset when there is no daylight.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: Who signs the Level One driving log, and when do you turn it in to the Division?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: The supervising driver signs the driving log, and it is turned in to the Division when the teen applies for the Limited Provisional License.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: How do the calendar holding period and the driving-log hour rule work together before Level Two?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: The Level One holding period is nine months, while the driving log needs at least sixty hours with ten at night; these are different requirements that both apply before Level Two.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Which three types of convictions must be completely absent for the previous six months to advance to Level Two?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: To move up to Level Two, the teen must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions during the previous six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: What age range qualifies for the Level Two Limited Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: The Level Two Limited Provisional License is for drivers at least sixteen but under eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: During which daily hours — and for which direct trips at any hour — may a Level Two driver drive alone?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: A Level Two driver may drive alone from five a.m. to nine p.m., and at any hour when going straight to or from work or a volunteer fire, rescue or emergency medical service they belong to.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: When is a Level Two holder allowed to drive without a supervisor on board?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: A Level Two license holder may drive unsupervised between five a.m. and nine p.m., and at any hour when traveling straight to or from work or any volunteer fire, rescue, or emergency medical organization in which they serve.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: At Level Two, what restraint rule covers passengers, and where must a supervisor sit whenever supervision is required?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: At Level Two, all passengers must be belted or in a child safety seat, and when supervision is required the supervising driver sits beside the driver.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: When driving unsupervised at Level Two, how many under-twenty-one passengers from outside your household are allowed — and how do household riders differ?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: When driving unsupervised at Level Two, a driver may carry one passenger under twenty-one from outside the household, plus one additional outside passenger under twenty-one who is a student being driven directly to or from school, while there is no under-twenty-one limit when all passengers live in the driver's household.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: Under what single condition may an unsupervised Level Two driver carry one extra under-twenty-one passenger from outside the household?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: One additional under-twenty-one passenger from outside the household is allowed only when that passenger is a student being driven directly to or from school.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: When driving unsupervised at Level Two, how does the household-member rule change the moment a non-household rider under twenty-one gets in?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: When driving unsupervised at Level Two, there is no under-twenty-one passenger limit if every passenger lives in the driver's household, but under-twenty-one household members may not ride in the vehicle while under-twenty-one non-household members are aboard.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: Which riders trigger the unsupervised Level Two passenger limit, and what mixing trap catches household riders?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: The Level Two passenger limit counts under-twenty-one passengers from outside the household when driving unsupervised; household members alone have no limit, except they cannot ride with under-twenty-one non-household passengers.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: How do cell-phone rules and exceptions at Level Two compare with Level One?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: Level Two drivers face the same cell phone ban and the same short list of emergency-call exceptions as Level One drivers.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: How long must a teen hold the Level Two license before applying for a Full Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: A teen must hold the Level Two license for at least six months before applying for the Full Provisional License.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: What minimum holding period separates a Level Two Limited Provisional License from a Full Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: A Level Two Limited Provisional License must be held for at least six months before applying for a Full Provisional License.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: What conviction-free record is required over the prior six months to move up to Level Three?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: To move up to Level Three, the driver must have had no moving violation, seat belt or cell phone convictions in the previous six months.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: How can an eligible driver upgrade to a Level Three Full Provisional License — or to a regular Class C license at age eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: An eligible driver can upgrade from Level Two to the Level Three Full Provisional License online, and can upgrade to a regular Class C license online at age eighteen.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: Which three graduated limits disappear once a teen earns a Full Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: A Full Provisional License drops the Level One and Level Two limits on driving hours, supervision and passengers.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: If a Full Provisional licensee is still under eighteen, what cell-phone rule applies while driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: A Full Provisional licensee who is still under eighteen may not use a cell phone while driving, apart from the same emergency calls.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: After a Full Provisional License removes hour, supervision, and passenger caps, which restriction still binds drivers under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: The Full Provisional License lifts the hour, supervision and passenger limits, yet a driver under eighteen still may not use a cell phone except for listed emergency calls.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: What should a new North Carolina resident aged fifteen to seventeen who already holds an out-of-state permit or license do?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: A new North Carolina resident aged fifteen to seventeen who holds a permit or license from elsewhere should contact a local driver license office to learn which permit or license they qualify for.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: How does the DMV monitor a provisional licensee's driving record compared with an adult's, and when might it reach out?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: The DMV watches a provisional licensee's driving record more closely and may contact the driver after certain convictions or crashes.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: How much alcohol or drugs may a provisional licensee consume before or while driving, and what penalty hits upon conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: A provisional licensee may not drive after or while consuming any amount of alcohol or drugs, and a conviction brings a one-year license revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: Why is thinking in terms of a blood-alcohol percentage wrong for a provisional licensee?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: For a provisional licensee the alcohol rule is any amount, not a blood alcohol limit, and a conviction means a one-year revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: Which specific phone, typing, and reading actions are illegal for a provisional licensee behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: A provisional licensee may not use a cellphone, type multiple letters or text to communicate, or read email or text messages while driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: Who must have a seat belt properly fastened when a provisional licensee drives a moving vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: Everyone riding in a moving vehicle driven by a provisional licensee must have a seat belt properly fastened.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: Which two school disciplinary actions lasting more than ten consecutive days cost a student their license, and for how long?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.memory_hook: Over ten days, lose twelve months
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: A student loses their license if suspended from school for more than ten days in a row, or sent to an alternative educational setting for discipline for more than ten days in a row, and the loss lasts twelve months.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Under North Carolina's Lose Control, Lose Your License law, what exact school-discipline threshold triggers a twelve-month suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Under Lose Control, Lose Your License, a student loses their license for twelve months upon receiving a suspension for more than ten consecutive days or a disciplinary assignment to an alternative educational setting for more than ten consecutive days.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: Give two examples of safety restrictions that can be placed on a North Carolina driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: A license can be restricted for safety, for example to driving only while wearing corrective lenses or only with equipment needed to drive safely.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: How does the law treat a driver who operates outside the limits of a license restriction?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: A driver who goes outside the limits of a license restriction is treated as driving without a license.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: Why must you stay strictly inside every restriction printed on your driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: If your driver license has a restriction, you may drive only within the limits of that restriction; otherwise the law treats you as driving without a license.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: What may the DMV do to verify documents you bring in, and what happens to any altered document?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: The DMV may copy your documents or hold them briefly to check that they are genuine, and it rejects any document that shows alteration.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: Which three core identity, residence, and status facts must a first-time North Carolina applicant prove?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: A first-time North Carolina applicant must prove full name and date of birth, North Carolina residence address, and a Social Security number or legal presence in the U.S.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: Beyond identity and residence documents, what coverage proof must a driver license applicant present?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: Applicants for a driver license must also show proof of vehicle liability insurance.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.front: Does the phrase Not for Federal Identification invalidate a North Carolina license, learner permit, or ID card for state purposes?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.expected_back: A North Carolina card marked Not for Federal Identification is still a valid state license, permit or ID.

sec02-card-sec02-F42.front: Starting May seven, two thousand twenty-five, where do holders of a Not for Federal Identification card need extra documents?
sec02-card-sec02-F42.expected_back: Beginning May seven, two thousand twenty-five, holders of a Not for Federal Identification card need extra documents to board commercial flights or enter federal facilities, military bases or nuclear power plants that require identification.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: Which three groups — homeless applicants, legally blind applicants, and older seniors — qualify for a free ID card, and what paperwork does each need?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: A free identification card is available to applicants who are homeless with a shelter letter, legally blind with a physician letter, or seventy or older with no extra papers needed.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: Beyond homelessness, blindness, or age seventy, what two medical or disability records qualify someone for a free ID card?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: A free ID card is also available when your driving record shows a medical cancellation, or when you have a developmental disability documented by a primary care provider's letter.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: In what physical format must required automobile liability insurance proof be presented, and what phone shortcut is rejected?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: Some license applicants must show printed proof of automobile liability insurance; a picture of it on a phone is not accepted.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: Which three licensing or privilege situations require you to show proof of liability insurance?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: Insurance proof is required when applying for an original license, including an out-of-state transfer, when a license is restored after suspension or revocation, and when a court grants a Limited Driving Privilege.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: How many days after issuance do Form DL-one hundred twenty-three, insurance binders, and certificates stay valid?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: Form DL-one hundred twenty-three, insurance binders and certificates are only good for thirty days after they are issued.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: What step with your insurance agent prevents delays before you head to the driver license office?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: To avoid delays, get Form DL-one hundred twenty-three from your insurance agent before you go to the license office.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Who signs Form DL-123A — the certification of insurance exemption — at the license office?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: An applicant who owns no currently registered vehicle and does not drive someone else's non-fleet private passenger vehicle signs a certification of exemption, Form DL-123A, at the license office.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: What driving restriction comes with signing the insurance exemption, and what fee plus proof lifts it later?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: That exemption limits the driver to Fleet Vehicles Only, and removing it costs a sixteen dollars and seventy-five cents duplicate fee plus proof of financial responsibility.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: How does Form DL-one hundred twenty-three differ in purpose and effect from Form DL-123A?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Form DL-one hundred twenty-three is proof that you carry liability insurance and is valid for thirty days, while Form DL-123A is a signed exemption for people who own no registered vehicle and limits them to fleet vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: What did the two thousand five REAL ID Act change, and what federal rules does North Carolina's REAL ID satisfy?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: The REAL ID Act of two thousand five raised security standards for state licenses and ID cards, and North Carolina's REAL ID meets federal identification rules for the TSA and federal facilities.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: What visual mark on a North Carolina license, learner permit, or ID card shows that it is a REAL ID?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: A REAL ID is a North Carolina license, learner permit or ID card that carries a star.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: Which air travelers — including teens — and which facility visitors are affected by REAL ID rules?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: REAL ID rules affect domestic commercial air travelers, including unaccompanied minors under eighteen, and visitors to federal sites that require ID such as military bases, prisons and nuclear plants.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: If you do not hold a REAL ID, can you still enter ID-required federal sites or fly, and what should you do beforehand?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: Without a REAL ID you can still enter those federal sites, but you must bring additional documents, so check with the agency, such as the TSA, before you go.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What exact four-word notice must federal law print on the face of every non-REAL ID license or ID card?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Federal law requires every non-REAL ID license or ID card to show the words Not for Federal Identification on its face.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: When did NCDMV start issuing REAL ID and non-REAL ID cards, and how much extra does a REAL ID cost?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: NCDMV started issuing REAL ID and non-REAL ID cards in May two thousand seventeen, and a REAL ID costs nothing extra beyond the usual fees.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Compare a REAL ID and a non-REAL ID card on face markings, driving validity, and price?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: A REAL ID shows a star, while a non-REAL ID card says Not for Federal Identification; both are valid for driving and cost the same.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: Once you establish residence in North Carolina, how many days do you have to get a state license or learner permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: A new resident must get a North Carolina license or learner permit within sixty days of establishing residence.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: How fast must a new resident apply for and receive a North Carolina CDL to keep commercial driving privileges?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: A new resident who wants to keep a commercial license from another jurisdiction must apply for and receive a North Carolina CDL within thirty days of becoming a resident.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How does the new-resident licensing deadline differ between a regular North Carolina license and a CDL?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: A new resident has sixty days to get a regular North Carolina license, but only thirty days to get a North Carolina CDL if they want to keep commercial privileges.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: If an applicant has lived in North Carolina less than twelve months, what search must DMV complete before issuing a card?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: For an applicant who has lived in North Carolina less than twelve months, DMV must finish a National Sex Offender Public Registry search before issuing a license or ID card.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: Which tests may a new resident applying for a Class C license have to take — and when is a road test added?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: A new resident applying for a Class C license may have to take the knowledge, vision and traffic signs tests, plus a driving test if the examiner thinks it is needed.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: Who counts as a nonresident under North Carolina licensing rules?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: A nonresident is someone whose legal residence is in another state, territory or jurisdiction, or in a foreign country.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: Which four common groups — from travelers and college students to military families — count as nonresidents?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Examples of nonresidents include travelers passing through, out-of-state college students who plan to go home, service members stationed in North Carolina who plan to return home, and spouses of nonresident service members.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: What separates a nonresident like a visiting college student from a new resident who must get a North Carolina license?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: A nonresident, such as an out-of-state student who plans to return home, is different from a new resident, who has established residence in North Carolina and must get a license.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.front: How does North Carolina store customer photos and signatures, and what data feature sits on every license or ID?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.expected_back: North Carolina stores customer photos and signatures digitally, and each license or ID card has a bar code holding customer data.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.front: Because cards are produced centrally, what sixty-day document lets you drive right away and when does your permanent card arrive?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.expected_back: Licenses are made at a central location, so after testing and a photo you receive a temporary driving certificate valid for sixty days, and the new card arrives by mail within sixty days.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: How long is your temporary driving certificate valid, and why isn't your plastic license handed over at the counter?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: The temporary driving certificate is valid for sixty days, and the permanent card is mailed within sixty days from a central location rather than printed at the office.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.front: While waiting for your new card in the mail, what may you keep using for photo identification?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.expected_back: You may keep using your current license or ID card as photo identification until the new one is delivered.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.front: What card orientation applies under twenty-one, and how do the colored birthday bars differ under eighteen versus eighteen to twenty?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.expected_back: Drivers under twenty-one get a vertical license or ID card; under eighteen it has red and yellow bars marking the eighteenth and twenty-first birthdays, and from eighteen to twenty one red bar marks the twenty-first birthday.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Which age group gets both red and yellow birthday bars on a vertical card, and which gets only a single red bar?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: The red and yellow bars appear only on cards for applicants under eighteen, marking both the eighteenth and twenty-first birthdays, while applicants aged eighteen to twenty get only a single red bar.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.front: On what annual date does a North Carolina license expire, and how many years does it last by age at issuance?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.expected_back: A license expires on your birthday: one issued at ages eighteen through sixty-five lasts eight years, and one issued at sixty-six or older lasts five years.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.front: What exact age line decides whether a newly issued North Carolina license lasts eight years or five years?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.expected_back: A North Carolina driver license expires on your birthday and lasts eight years when issued at ages eighteen through sixty-five, or five years when issued at age sixty-six or older.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.front: When does DMV mail a renewal reminder card, what does it tell you, and is bringing it mandatory?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.expected_back: About six months before a license expires, DMV mails a reminder card showing how many years the renewal will last, but you can renew without the card.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.front: How many days before expiration may you renew a North Carolina driver license?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.expected_back: A license may be renewed any time within one hundred eighty days before it expires.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.front: Which test is always required when you renew your license in person at a driver license office?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.expected_back: Renewing at a driver license office requires a vision test.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.front: If you show up to renew without your current or expired license in hand, what must you show the examiner?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.expected_back: If you renew without your current or expired license, you must show the examiner two identification documents.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: How is your vision verified differently when renewing in person versus renewing by mail?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: Renewing in person always includes a vision test, while renewing by mail instead requires a vision statement signed by a licensed physician.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.front: How long must a resident be out of state continuously to renew by mail, and when does that temporary license end?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.expected_back: A resident who has been out of state for at least thirty days in a row may renew by mail, getting a temporary license that ends sixty days after returning to North Carolina or on its printed expiration date, whichever is first.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.front: Beyond thirty continuous days away, what address, Class C expiration, photo age, record, vision, affidavit, age-cap, and cycle rules govern civilian mail renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.expected_back: Civilian renewal by mail is open to a resident outside North Carolina for at least thirty continuous days who has a permanent verifiable North Carolina residence address, a Class C license expired no more than two years, a DMV photo from the past five years, an NCDMV record of a Social Security number or federal legal-presence document, a physician-signed vision statement, a signed and dated National Sex Offender Affidavit, and an age no older than seventy-two on the request date, and it may be used only every other renewal cycle.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.front: How often may eligible drivers renew by mail, and which two license types can never use mail renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.expected_back: Renewal by mail is allowed only every other renewal cycle, and commercial and full provisional licenses can never be renewed by mail.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.front: What documents — and optional address option — let an active-duty service member stationed outside North Carolina renew by mail?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.expected_back: An active-duty service member living outside North Carolina may renew by mail with military orders and a front-and-back copy of the military ID, using a host family address if needed.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.front: With active-duty paperwork, how early before expiration can a military renewal happen, and how old may the DMV photo on file be?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.expected_back: With papers showing active duty, a military renewal may be done more than a year before expiration, and the DMV photo may be up to eight years old.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: Compare the maximum age of the DMV photo on file for a civilian mail renewal versus a military mail renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: Civilian renewal by mail requires a DMV photo from the last five years, while the military version allows a photo up to eight years old.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.front: How many times in a lifetime may a military-designation license be renewed by mail, and which family members also qualify?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.expected_back: A military-designation license may be renewed by mail no more than two times in the holder's lifetime, and military spouses and dependents may also renew by mail.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.front: Under what expiration condition can a military dependent holding a full provisional license upgrade to Class C at age eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.expected_back: A military dependent with a full provisional license can upgrade to Class C at age eighteen if the license has been expired no more than one year.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.front: When does a service member returning to North Carolina actually need to visit a driver license office?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.expected_back: A returning service member does not need to visit a license office until the license is due for renewal.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.front: How can a qualified veteran add a VETERAN designation at their next renewal, and what extra fee applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.expected_back: A qualified veteran can add a VETERAN designation by bringing an honorable discharge form such as the DD-two hundred fourteen, and it is added at the next renewal at no extra charge.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.front: What option and fee apply if a veteran wants the VETERAN designation added before their next scheduled renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.expected_back: A veteran who wants the designation before renewal can get it on a duplicate license for the usual duplicate fee.

sec03-card-sec03-F41.front: What license-status rule governs getting a duplicate, and what two ways can you replace a lost or stolen license?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.expected_back: To get a duplicate, the license must not be expired, suspended or cancelled; a lost or stolen license can be replaced by showing two DMV-approved identification documents, or online if you know your license number.

sec03-card-sec03-F42.front: What must you do within sixty days after changing your address, and what single address-change situation is exempt?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.expected_back: After an address change you must tell the division within sixty days and get a duplicate license, unless the address changed through government action without you moving.

sec03-card-sec03-F43.front: What sixty-day DMV steps follow a name change, and how far ahead should you update Social Security first?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.expected_back: After a name change you must notify the division within sixty days and get a duplicate, and you should update Social Security at least twenty-four hours before visiting DMV.

sec03-card-sec03-F44.front: Which official records or notarized form prove a legal name change, and which jurisdictions must have issued them?
sec03-card-sec03-F44.expected_back: A name change is proven by a certified marriage certificate, court or Register of Deeds records, or a notarized Form DL-one hundred one, issued by an agency of the United States, Puerto Rico, a U.S. territory or Canada.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.front: What deadline and card requirement do address changes and name changes share, and when is an address change not a violation?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.expected_back: An address change and a name change both require notifying the division within sixty days and getting a duplicate, but a government-made address change without moving is not a violation.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.front: At what blood alcohol concentration is every driver impaired—and can impairment start well below that mark?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.expected_back: At a blood alcohol concentration, or BAC, of zero point zero eight percent every driver is impaired, and many people are affected at far lower levels.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: At what blood alcohol concentration does crash risk begin climbing, and what happens to fatal crash odds at zero point zero eight?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Crash risk begins rising at a BAC of zero point zero five percent, and at zero point zero eight percent the chance of causing a fatal crash is greater still.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: How does the zero point zero five blood alcohol mark differ from the zero point zero eight mark for car drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: The zero point zero five figure is where crash risk starts to rise, not a legal limit; the legal per se limit for a car driver is zero point zero eight.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: How did the Safe Roads Act of nineteen eighty-three reshape North Carolina's impaired-driving laws?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: The Safe Roads Act of nineteen eighty-three replaced all earlier North Carolina drunk-driving laws with a single offense called Driving While Impaired, or DWI.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: How can prosecutors prove a DWI charge without relying on a specific blood alcohol number?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: DWI can be proven by showing that alcohol, drugs or both appreciably impaired the driver's physical or mental faculties.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Which blood alcohol concentrations automatically prove DWI for a regular vehicle driver versus a commercial vehicle driver?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: DWI can also be proven by a BAC of zero point zero eight percent or more, or zero point zero four or more when driving a commercial motor vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: How does a commercial motor vehicle driver's per se DWI limit compare to an ordinary motorist's limit?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: The per se DWI limit is zero point zero eight for an ordinary driver but zero point zero four for a driver of a commercial motor vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: What roadside enforcement tool do North Carolina DWI statutes authorize officers to use?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: North Carolina DWI laws allow law enforcement to set up roadblocks to check for impaired drivers.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: What two types of chemical testing may an officer request after charging a driver with DWI?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: A driver charged with DWI will be asked to take a chemical test of breath or blood.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: What immediate revocation and additional DMV revocation hit your license if you refuse a required chemical test?
