sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Refusing a required chemical test brings an immediate license revocation of at least thirty days and a further DMV revocation of at least twelve months.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: How much of a willful-refusal revocation must pass before a judge can ever consider granting a limited driving privilege?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: In some cases, once six months of a willful-refusal revocation have passed, a judge may grant a limited driving privilege.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What happens to your driving privilege right away if your chemical test hits zero point zero eight—or zero point zero four commercially?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: A test result of zero point zero eight or more, or zero point zero four or more in a commercial motor vehicle, means your driving privilege is revoked immediately for at least thirty days.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How does the license revocation for refusing a chemical test compare with failing it at zero point zero eight?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.memory_hook: Both thirty days, refusal adds year
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Refusing the chemical test brings at least thirty days of immediate revocation plus at least twelve months from DMV, while failing it at zero point zero eight or more brings an immediate revocation of at least thirty days.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Can prosecutors introduce your chemical test reading—or your refusal to take the test—against you in court?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: Both your chemical test result and any refusal to be tested can be used as evidence in court.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: May a driver sip beer or any other alcoholic drink while operating a vehicle in North Carolina?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: Drinking any alcoholic beverage while driving, beer included, is prohibited.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.front: What is North Carolina's rule on carrying an open container of alcohol inside a vehicle, including the passenger area?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.expected_back: Carrying an open container of any alcoholic beverage in a vehicle, including in the passenger area, is prohibited.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: What rule governs open or unopened alcohol inside the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle on a public road?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: In the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle on a public road, alcohol is banned whether the container is open or closed.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: How does the passenger-area alcohol container rule differ between a regular car and a commercial vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: An open container is banned anywhere in a car's passenger area, while in a commercial vehicle's passenger area even closed containers are banned.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: How are North Carolina DWI punishment levels structured, and what mandatory penalty hits on a second DWI conviction?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Punishment levels rise with the seriousness of the offense, and a second DWI conviction requires time in jail.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: Alongside punishment, how do North Carolina DWI laws address potential alcohol problems for high-risk versus lower-BAC offenders?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: DWI laws aim to help offenders with alcohol problems as well as punish them: repeat offenders and high-BAC drivers are checked for an alcohol problem, and lower-BAC offenders attend alcohol safety school.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: What evaluation must every driver convicted of DWI finish before DMV will reinstate driving privileges?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: Anyone convicted of DWI must complete a substance abuse assessment before driving privileges are reinstated.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: How long is the mandatory license revocation for a first DWI conviction in North Carolina?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: A first DWI conviction brings a mandatory one-year license revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: When does a second DWI conviction trigger a mandatory four-year license revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: A second DWI conviction brings a mandatory four-year revocation when the earlier offense happened within three years of the current one.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: What prior-offense window makes a third DWI conviction result in mandatory permanent license revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: A third DWI conviction brings mandatory permanent revocation if at least one earlier conviction happened within the past five years.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: What license penalty hits on a fourth DWI conviction, and when does that fourth offense become a felony?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: A fourth DWI conviction brings mandatory permanent revocation, and it is a felony if the three earlier convictions all happened within the past seven years.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: Which three look-back windows govern the second-offense four-year loss, third-offense permanent loss, and fourth-offense felony?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Look-back windows differ by conviction: three years for the four-year second-offense revocation, five years for permanent revocation on a third, seven years for the felony fourth.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: Which two driving credentials receive a special blood alcohol concentration restriction after a DWI?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: A blood alcohol concentration restriction is placed on a license restored after a DWI suspension, or on a Limited Driving Privilege granted after a DWI conviction.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: What blood alcohol cap applies on a driver's first post-DWI license restoration versus a second or later restoration?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.memory_hook: First point zero four, then zero
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: The restriction is zero point zero four on the first restoration and zero point zero zero on the second or any later restoration.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: How does the blood alcohol restriction shift once a driver moves past their first DWI license restoration?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: The restored-license BAC restriction is zero point zero four the first time and zero point zero zero for every later restoration.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: Which three convictions trigger a zero point zero zero blood alcohol restriction right from the first restoration?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: The restriction is also zero point zero zero after a DWI conviction in a commercial motor vehicle, a conviction for driving under twenty-one after consuming alcohol or drugs, or felony death by vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: Which two DWI circumstances require installing an ignition interlock device on your vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.memory_hook: Point one five or seven-year prior
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: A DWI conviction with a BAC of zero point one five or more, or with another conviction in the past seven years, requires an ignition interlock device on the vehicle.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: How does the seven-year prior rule for an ignition interlock differ from the seven-year prior rule for felony DWI?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: The ignition interlock is triggered by a BAC of zero point one five or more or a prior conviction within seven years, while a fourth conviction becomes a felony when three priors fall within seven years.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: What can a court do to your car if you catch a new DWI while already revoked for an earlier DWI?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: If you are convicted of DWI while already revoked for an earlier DWI, the court may order your vehicle seized and sold.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: What is the minimum legal age to buy any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina, and does merely trying under age break the law?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: The legal age to buy any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina is twenty-one, and anyone younger who buys or tries to buy alcohol breaks the law.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: What license penalty hits an underage person convicted of buying, attempting to buy, or helping another minor get alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: An underage person convicted of buying or trying to buy alcohol, or of helping another underage person do so, faces a one-year license revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: What happens to an underage person's license if convicted of using or trying to use a fake or borrowed ID for alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: An underage person convicted of using, or trying to use, a fake license or ID or someone else's license or ID to get alcohol faces a one-year revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: What license penalty applies to anyone convicted of lending an ID to a minor for alcohol or giving alcohol to someone underage?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Any person convicted of letting an underage person use their license or ID to buy alcohol, or of giving alcohol to an underage person, also faces a one-year revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: How does an adult supplier's or ID lender's license revocation compare with the underage buyer's revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: An adult who lends an ID to an underage buyer or gives alcohol to an underage person faces the same one-year revocation as the underage buyer.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: What license consequence hits a driver under twenty-one convicted of driving with any alcohol or drugs in their body?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: A driver under twenty-one convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body loses their license for one year.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: How long is the driver license revocation when someone younger than twenty-one is convicted of driving with any alcohol or drugs present?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: A driver younger than twenty-one who is convicted of driving with any amount of alcohol or drugs in their body faces a one-year driver license revocation.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: What event places driver license points onto your North Carolina driving record?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Being convicted of certain motor vehicle violations in North Carolina puts driver license points on your driving record.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: At what point total may DMV assign you to a driver improvement clinic, and what fee does that clinic charge?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Once you reach seven points, DMV may send you to a driver improvement clinic, and the clinic costs eighty-three dollars and fifty cents.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: How many points are deducted from your driving record when you satisfactorily complete a driver improvement clinic?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: Finishing the driver improvement clinic satisfactorily takes three points off your record.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Accumulating how many points within a three-year window can suspend your North Carolina driver license?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: Collecting twelve points within three years can get your license suspended.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: Once your license is reinstated after a suspension, how many points within three years can trigger a second suspension?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: After your license is reinstated, gathering eight points within the next three years can bring a second suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: Which three point totals mark the driver improvement clinic threshold, a first suspension, and a post-reinstatement suspension?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: Seven points can send you to a driver improvement clinic, while twelve points within three years can cost you the license; after reinstatement only eight points within three years can bring a second suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: How long do a first, second, and third point-system license suspension each last?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: A point-system suspension lasts sixty days the first time, six months the second time and twelve months the third time.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: What three escalating durations make up North Carolina's adult point-system suspension ladder?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: The adult point-system ladder runs sixty days, then six months, then twelve months for the first, second and third suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: When your driving privilege is reinstated, what happens to prior driver license points versus insurance points?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: When your privilege is reinstated, every earlier driver license point is wiped out, but insurance points are not affected.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How does point removal from a driver improvement clinic differ from point removal upon post-suspension reinstatement?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: Completing the clinic removes three points, whereas reinstatement after a suspension cancels every earlier license point.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: Why can your auto insurance bill stay high even after reinstatement cancels every prior driver license point?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Reinstating your driving privilege cancels every prior driver license point, though insurance points are not canceled by that reinstatement.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: Who runs the separate point system used to set auto insurance rates, and who can explain how it affects you?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: Insurance companies set rates with their own separate point system, and your insurance agent can answer questions about it.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: Which two violations carry five points—the highest value on North Carolina's regular vehicle point schedule?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: In a regular vehicle, passing a stopped school bus and aggressive driving each carry five points, the highest values on the regular schedule.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: How many points attach to illegal passing, reckless driving, tailgating, property-damage hit-and-run, or wrong-side driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: Illegal passing, reckless driving, tailgating (following too closely), a property-damage-only hit and run, and driving on the wrong side of the road each carry four points.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: How many license points are assessed for failing to yield to a pedestrian, bicycle, motor scooter, or motorcycle?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Failing to yield to a pedestrian under the cited statute, or to a bicycle, motor scooter or motorcycle, carries four points.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: How many points attach to running a stop sign, running a red light, failing to yield, or speeding above fifty-five?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Running a stop sign, running a red light, failing to yield right of way, and speeding faster than fifty-five miles per hour each carry three points.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: How many points apply to driving unlicensed or expired over a year, ignoring a siren, entering a safety zone, or lacking insurance?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Driving with no license or one expired over a year, ignoring a siren, driving through a safety zone, and having no liability insurance each carry three points.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: How many points do you receive for skipping a required crash report or speeding above a posted school-zone limit?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: Failing to file a required accident report and speeding above a posted school zone limit each carry three points.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: How many points apply to failing to restrain a child properly—and to any other unlisted moving violation?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Not properly restraining a child in a child restraint or seat belt carries two points, the same as any other moving violation not listed.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: How many license points are added for littering when a motor vehicle is involved?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Littering that involves the use of a motor vehicle carries one point.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: How many points are assessed for passing a stopped school bus while driving a commercial motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: While operating a commercial motor vehicle, passing a stopped school bus carries eight points.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: Which two violations carry six points when committed in a commercial motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: In a commercial motor vehicle, a rail-highway crossing violation and aggressive driving each carry six points.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: In a commercial motor vehicle, how many points attach to reckless driving, running a red light, and other moving violations?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: In a commercial motor vehicle, reckless driving carries five points, running a red light four points and any other moving violation three points.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: How many license points attach to having any alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Having an alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle carries four points.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: How do the top commercial schedule values—passing a stopped school bus and rail violations—compare with vehicle littering?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: On the commercial schedule, passing a stopped school bus carries eight points and a rail-highway crossing violation six, yet littering with a vehicle still carries only one point.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: How many driver license points are added for illegal parking or vehicle overload, overlength, overwidth, and overheight convictions?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Overload, overlength, overwidth and overheight convictions add no points, and neither does illegal parking.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: How many license points attach to plate, registration, muffler, emblem, inspection, or concealed-weapon convictions?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Plate, registration, muffler, emblem and inspection-certificate offenses, and carrying a concealed weapon, add no points.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: How high can the fine or statutory penalty climb when a point-carrying offense is committed in a commercial motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: A point-carrying offense committed in a commercial motor vehicle may be charged double any fine or penalty the statute authorizes.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: Alongside criminal court penalties, what else can certain traffic convictions strip away?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: On top of any criminal penalty from the court, conviction of certain traffic offenses takes away your driving privilege.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Which two twelve-month combinations involving speeding over fifty-five allow DMV to suspend your license?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: DMV can suspend your license for two over-fifty-five miles per hour speeding convictions within twelve months, or one over-fifty-five speeding conviction plus one reckless driving conviction within a year.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Does willful racing against another car have to be arranged beforehand for DMV to suspend your license?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: A conviction for willful racing against another vehicle, planned ahead or not, lets DMV suspend your license.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: Under what court-sentence rule or extreme highway speed threshold can DMV also suspend your license?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: DMV can also suspend when a court sentence orders you not to drive for a set time, and in certain cases after a conviction for speeding over seventy-five miles per hour

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: What license revocation follows driving more than fifteen miles per hour over the limit while going faster than fifty-five?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: Driving more than fifteen miles per hour over the limit while going faster than fifty-five miles per hour brings a revocation of at least thirty days.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: Which two situations push that high-speed license revocation up to sixty days?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: The revocation is sixty days for a second over-fifty-five, more-than-fifteen-over speeding charge within one year, or for speeding together with reckless driving on the same occasion.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How does a thirty-day high-speed revocation differ from a sixty-day high-speed revocation?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.memory_hook: First thirty, repeat or reckless sixty
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: Speeding more than fifteen miles per hour over the limit above fifty-five miles per hour means at least thirty days, but a second such charge within a year, or speeding plus reckless driving on one occasion, means sixty days.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: How long is the suspension for manslaughter, death by vehicle, or vehicle assault—and how does impaired manslaughter differ?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: Manslaughter, death by vehicle and assault with a motor vehicle each bring a one-year suspension, while manslaughter while impaired brings a permanent one.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: How does impairment change the license suspension length for vehicular manslaughter?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: Manslaughter brings a one-year suspension, while manslaughter under the influence of an impairing substance brings a permanent one.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: What suspension duration applies to failing to stop and render aid after a crash or willfully refusing an alcohol test?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: Failing to stop and give aid after a crash, and willfully refusing a blood or breath alcohol test, each bring a one-year suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: What license suspension hits when a driver speeds above fifty-five and at least fifteen over the limit to avoid arrest?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: Speeding over fifty-five miles per hour and at least fifteen miles per hour over the limit while trying to avoid arrest brings a one-year suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: What suspension applies to two reckless driving charges in twelve months or seeking a permit or license by fraud?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: Two reckless driving charges within twelve months, or trying to get a license or learner permit under false pretenses, each bring a one-year suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: What license penalty and vehicle consequence apply to prearranged highway racing—including watching, betting, or lending a car?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: Prearranged highway racing, and watching, betting on or lending a car for it, carry a three-year suspension, and the officer seizes the car, which a court may order sold at public auction after conviction.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: How does the suspension length for prearranged highway racing compare with most other major table offenses?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Prearranged racing and helping with it carry three years, three times the one-year period for most other offenses in the same table.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.front: What suspension and fine follow failing to yield at an intersection or work zone when it causes serious bodily injury?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.expected_back: Failing to yield in the listed situations, such as entering an intersection or at a highway construction or maintenance area, when the offense causes serious bodily injury brings ninety days and five hundred dollars.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: How soon can DMV suspend after receiving a court conviction report, and where may a revoked driver hold a hearing right?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: DMV may suspend your privilege as soon as it receives the conviction report from the court, and a revoked driver may have a right to a hearing in the judicial district where they live.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: If a DMV hearing does not go your way, how quickly—and to which court—may you appeal?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: If the hearing does not help, you may appeal the DMV decision within thirty days to the Superior Court of your home county.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: What exact two-step sequence applies when a revoked driver challenges a DMV revocation?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: A revoked driver first asks DMV for a hearing; only if that fails is the appeal taken to the county Superior Court within thirty days.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.front: How can a traffic conviction in another state affect your North Carolina license, and what notice must DMV send?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.expected_back: A conviction in another state can lead to suspension or revocation of your North Carolina license as though it happened here, and DMV must notify you in writing of the effective date.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.front: What happens to your license if you miss court or leave a traffic fine unpaid, and how long does that hold last?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.expected_back: If you miss court or do not pay a fine for a citation, DMV sets a revocation date that takes effect unless the fine is paid or waived first, and it lasts until the court reports payment or waiver.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.front: Does paying off your overdue traffic citation erase the underlying conviction consequences for the offense itself?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.expected_back: Taking care of the citation does not cancel the consequences of the offense itself if you are convicted.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.front: What form and process can you use if you cannot afford to pay a traffic ticket, and what options does the judge have?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.expected_back: If you cannot afford a ticket, you file the Motion for Relief form with the clerk in the county where you got the ticket and ask for a hearing, where the judge may lower the amount, set a payment plan or waive it.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.front: How do you stop an unpaid-ticket suspension when you are able to pay the full amount?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.expected_back: If you can pay in full, you contact the clerk in that county, pay the whole amount, and the court tells DMV, which stops the suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: How do the cannot-pay route and the pay-in-full route differ—and what final step do both routes share?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: A driver who cannot pay files a Motion for Relief and asks the judge for relief, while a driver who can pay calls the clerk and pays everything; in both routes the court notifies DMV.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.front: What license suspension hits a provisional licensee under eighteen upon a second moving violation conviction within twelve months?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.expected_back: A provisional licensee under eighteen faces a thirty-day suspension for a second moving violation conviction within twelve months.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.front: What suspensions apply when a provisional licensee racks up a third or fourth moving violation conviction within twelve months?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.memory_hook: Ninety days third, six months fourth
sec05-card-sec05-F45.expected_back: A provisional licensee faces ninety days for a third and six months for a fourth moving violation conviction within twelve months.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: What is the complete three-step suspension ladder for a provisional licensee's repeat moving violations within twelve months?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: For a provisional licensee the ladder runs thirty days, ninety days and six months, counted from the second, third and fourth moving violation within twelve months.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.front: How much is North Carolina's standard restoration fee after a suspension or revocation, and what is the one exception?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.expected_back: Clearing a suspension or revocation requires a restoration fee of eighty-three dollars and fifty cents, except when the license was taken for medical reasons after a medical evaluation.

sec05-card-sec05-F47.front: What restoration fee applies after a DWI revocation, and how can you avoid the extra fifty-dollar service fee?
sec05-card-sec05-F47.expected_back: Restoring after a DWI revocation costs one hundred sixty-seven dollars and twenty-five cents, and a fifty dollars service fee also applies unless you surrendered the license to the court or mailed it to DMV before the effective date.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: How does the ordinary restoration fee compare with the DWI restoration fee, and when is the fifty-dollar service fee waived?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: The ordinary restoration fee is eighty-three dollars and fifty cents and the DWI restoration fee is one hundred sixty-seven dollars and twenty-five cents, while the separate fifty dollars service fee is skipped if the license was surrendered or mailed in before the effective date.

sec05-card-sec05-F48.front: What steps must you complete at a driver license office to restore your driving privilege after a suspension?
sec05-card-sec05-F48.expected_back: To get your privilege back you go to a driver license office, prove identity, pay the fees, reapply, take any required tests, show insurance if required and pay for the new license.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: Why does the distance behind farm machinery shrink much faster than drivers expect?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Because farm equipment moves so slowly, the gap closes much faster than you expect as you come up behind it.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: On which North Carolina roadways is farm equipment legally prohibited?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: Farm equipment is allowed by law on most North Carolina roads, but not on interstates.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Which lights must every vehicle participating in a funeral procession turn on?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Every vehicle in a funeral procession must drive with headlights on, and with hazard flashers on as well if it has them.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: How does the lead car of a funeral procession handle signals, and when may following cars continue without stopping?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: The lead vehicle of a procession obeys all signals, but once it has crossed lawfully, or when an officer or funeral director directs it, or a police vehicle leads, the rest may go through the intersection without stopping, using extra care.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: Where on the roadway and at what spacing do vehicles inside a funeral procession travel?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Procession vehicles keep to the right side of the road and follow the car ahead as closely as is reasonable and prudent.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: Must oncoming traffic yield to a funeral procession, and how must you act if you choose to yield?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: An oncoming driver may choose to yield to a procession, and if so must either slow down or stop fully off the roadway so other oncoming traffic can stay in its lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: When is a driver traveling in the same direction allowed to pass a funeral procession?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: A driver going the same way as a procession must not pass it, unless the road is marked with two or more lanes moving in the procession's direction.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: How do funeral-procession rules differ between oncoming drivers and same-direction drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Oncoming drivers may choose to yield to a funeral procession, while drivers going the same way are forbidden to pass it unless there are two or more lanes in its direction.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: What two intersection and gap mistakes must outside drivers avoid around a funeral procession?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Never knowingly drive between vehicles in a procession, and when it goes through a red light, do not enter the intersection on your green unless you can do so safely without crossing its path.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: Who continues and who waits when a funeral procession is still crossing an intersection after the light changes?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: Procession cars may continue through an intersection behind a lead car that crossed lawfully, while an outside driver facing green must not cut across the procession's path.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: Which side of the road must you drive on by law, and when is the left half legal?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: The law requires driving on the right side of the road; the left side is legal only in cases such as one-way streets and passing.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Which lane must you use on a multi-lane highway when driving slower than the posted speed limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: On a multi-lane highway, if you are going slower than the posted limit, use the far right lane except when passing, turning left or avoiding an obstruction.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: How do legal left-side exceptions pair with multi-lane positioning for slower drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Driving on the left is lawful only in situations such as one-way streets and passing, while slower traffic on a multi-lane highway belongs in the far right lane.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: Which two factors combine to determine total stopping distance, and how does higher speed affect both?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: Your speed and your reaction time together set your stopping distance, and higher speed lengthens both the distance covered while reacting and the braking distance.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: Roughly how many feet does a car traveling fifty-five miles per hour need to stop under ideal conditions?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: Even in ideal conditions a vehicle going fifty-five miles per hour needs about two hundred eleven feet to come to a complete stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: What does every added mile per hour do to vehicle control and crash survival odds?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: Every extra mile per hour reduces your control of the vehicle, and higher speed raises the chance that a crash will cause serious injury or death.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: How must your forward sight distance adjust as your travel speed climbs?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: The faster you travel, the farther ahead you need to see so that you have room to stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Is creeping far below the speed limit safe, and what sign must slow drivers still obey?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Driving well below the limit is also dangerous; if you must go slowly, still keep to any posted minimum speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: At which two road features is driving very slowly especially dangerous?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Very slow driving is especially risky just over the top of a hill or around a curve, where faster traffic may hit you before it can slow down.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What wise move should you make when a queue of vehicles builds up behind your slower pace?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: If a line of traffic builds behind you, it is wise to pull to the side, stop and let the vehicles go by.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: What do traffic studies cited in the handbook reveal about cars moving far below the posted speed limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: The handbook cites studies finding that a vehicle going well under the posted limit is far more likely to cause or be in a crash than one moving at normal speed.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: Given the dangers of both speeding and crawling, how should you choose your travel speed?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: Speeding reduces control and raises injury risk, yet driving well under the limit is also linked to more crashes, so the goal is a speed suited to conditions within the posted range.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: Which two ceilings may your driving speed never exceed?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: Never go faster than the posted limit, or faster than is reasonable and wise for the conditions at the time.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Does safe driving ever call for going below the posted limit—or above it?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Safe driving often means going slower than the posted limit, but never faster.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What is North Carolina's unposted default speed limit inside cities and towns?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: Unless a sign says otherwise, the speed limit in cities and towns is thirty-five miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: How does the maximum speed for a regular school bus compare with a school activity bus?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: The maximum speed is forty-five miles per hour for school buses and fifty-five miles per hour for school activity buses.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: What are North Carolina's maximum speeds outside municipalities and on interstate highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: The maximum speed is fifty-five miles per hour outside cities and towns and seventy miles per hour on interstates.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: How does the default town speed limit compare with North Carolina's top interstate limit?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: The default limit inside cities and towns is thirty-five miles per hour unless posted otherwise, while interstates allow up to seventy miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: Which two categories share the fifty-five-mile-per-hour maximum, and which bus stays ten slower?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: The fifty-five miles per hour figure is both the maximum outside cities and towns and the maximum for school activity buses, while a regular school bus is held to forty-five miles per hour

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: When do you slow for a curve, and what do you do with the gas through the bend?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: For a curve, slow down before you enter so you need not brake in it, then gradually add speed through the curve to keep traction and control.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: How should you apply the brake pedal if you have no choice but to brake inside a curve?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: If braking in a curve cannot be avoided, press the brakes gradually until you are sure steady pressure is safe.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: Why does curve slowing belong before the bend rather than by braking inside it?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: On a curve, the speed reduction happens before the curve, and the speed is then gradually increased through it rather than reduced by braking inside it.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: At what point do you begin steering for a curve, and where in your lane do you stay?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: Start steering just before the point where the road begins to bend, and stay on your own side as far right as you can.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: How do gravity, gear choice, and brake timing change when approaching a downhill curve?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: For a downhill curve, allow for gravity, shift to a lower gear before the descent, and brake earlier and slower than you would on level ground.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: When must downshifting and initial braking happen on a downhill curve compared with flat road?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: On a downhill curve you shift to a lower gear before the descent and start braking earlier than on flat road, not once you are in the bend.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Where should you position your vehicle and how should you pace speed through a right turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: On a right turn, keep close to the right edge so no vehicle can squeeze in between you and the curb; slow before turning and then speed up slightly.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: Which two road users are hardest to spot during turns, making signaling and scanning vital?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: Motorcycles and bicycles are particularly hard to see while you turn, so always signal and look before turning.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: Why is tailgating dangerous, and what space benchmark applies on the open highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: Following too closely is a leading cause of crashes; on the open road, leave enough space ahead that a passing vehicle could safely move into it.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: How do you count out North Carolina's two-second following-distance rule?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: The two-second rule means leaving two seconds between the moment the vehicle ahead passes a fixed point and the moment you reach that point.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: How does the two-second rule's purpose differ from scanning farther ahead as speed climbs?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: The two-second rule governs the gap to the car ahead, while seeing farther ahead is what you need as speed rises, because stopping distance grows.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: On a highway with three or more lanes, which extra lane must you check before changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: On a highway with several lanes, check both the lane you are moving into and the lane beyond it, in case another driver is heading for the same space.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What four-step sequence completes a safe lane change?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: To change lanes, check the side and rear-view mirrors, look over your shoulder to clear the blind spot, signal ahead of time, and then move over.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: Why isn't checking only your target lane enough on a multi-lane road?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: A lane change on a multi-lane road needs a check of the lane beyond your target lane too, because a driver there may be moving into the same space.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: What three checks and warnings come in order before you pull out to pass another vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: To pass, first look ahead and behind to judge whether it is safe, then signal to the drivers around you, then sound the horn to alert the driver ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: What legal duty does sounding your horn place on the driver you are starting to pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Your horn signal puts the driver you are passing under a legal duty to help you get by.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: What space, pace, and sightline conditions must exist before starting any pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: Pass only with plenty of room and a steady speed, and only if you can see far enough to get back into your lane before meeting oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: At least how far to the left must a passing vehicle stay from the vehicle being overtaken?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: The law requires the passing driver to stay at least two feet to the left of the vehicle being passed.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: At which three crossing or junction types is passing never safe and generally illegal?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Railroad crossings, town and city intersections, and marked intersections in the countryside are places where passing is never safe and is usually against the law.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: What minimum forward sight distance is required to pass on a curve or hill?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Do not pass on a curve or hill where you cannot see at least five hundred feet ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: Which yellow pavement-line setups prohibit passing?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: Do not pass where a solid yellow line is in your lane or where there is a double solid yellow line.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: How does legal side clearance while passing compare with minimum sight distance on hills and curves?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Passing clearance is at least two feet to the left of the passed vehicle, while the sight distance needed to pass on a curve or hill is at least five hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: How must you cooperate when another driver signals with the horn and passes you?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: When someone is passing you, you must help: move toward the right edge if they sound the horn, and never speed up.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: When does speeding up and refusing to yield to a passing vehicle become a criminal misdemeanor?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: Speeding up and failing to give way to a passing vehicle is a misdemeanor if it leads to a crash with injury or property damage.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: How do the passing driver's horn-and-signal duties pair with the overtaken driver's response?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: When passing, you signal your intention and blow the horn to alert the driver ahead; when being passed, you must help by moving to the right edge of the road if the passing driver blows the horn, and you must never increase your speed.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Why does North Carolina generally ban passing on the right?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Passing on the right is illegal except where specifically allowed, because it puts you on the other driver's blind side, where that car might turn right or pull over.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: In which four roadway or lane situations is passing on the right permitted?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Passing on the right is allowed on highways with two or more lanes each way, on one-way streets, around a car in a left-turn lane, and when you are in a lane reserved for right turns.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: When may you pass in the middle lane of a three-lane highway, and what blocks it?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: On a three-lane highway you may pass only in the center lane where it is marked for passing your way, unless the car in the center lane is turning left.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: Is passing on the right always illegal, or which specific exceptions apply?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Passing on the right is generally illegal, but it is allowed on roads with two or more lanes each way, on one-way streets, beside a left-turning car, and from a right-turn lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: On which side of a two-way street must you always park, and what street type is the exception?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Park on the right-hand side of the street at all times, unless it is a one-way street.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: What check and turn signal are required before pulling out of a right-curb parallel space—and when isn't left signaled?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: When pulling out of a parallel space, look for approaching traffic and signal a left turn first; the signal is not needed when parked on the left of a one-way street.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: Which five everyday street or crossing locations completely forbid parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Do not park at an intersection, in front of a driveway, or on a crosswalk, sidewalk or bridge.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: How far back must you park from a cross-street curb line versus curbless intersecting right-of-way lines?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Do not park within twenty-five feet of the curb line of a cross street, or within fifteen feet of the intersecting right of way lines where there is no curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: Within how many feet is parking prohibited near a fire hydrant or fire-station entrance?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Do not park within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant or of a fire station entrance.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: How does the fire-hydrant no-parking distance compare with curbed and uncurbed cross-street corners?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: The no-parking distance is fifteen feet from a fire hydrant but twenty-five feet from the curb line of a cross street, and fifteen feet from the right of way lines where there is no curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: May you park on highway pavement, and what visibility distance makes shoulder parking legal?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Never park on the paved travel part of a highway, and parking on the shoulder is illegal unless drivers from both directions can see your vehicle for at least two hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: How far away from a fire or fire truck must you park inside city limits versus outside town?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Keep at least one block away from a fire or fire truck inside city limits, and at least four hundred feet away outside a city, when parking.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How do city and rural fire-parking buffers contrast with the highway-shoulder visibility requirement?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: Near a fire or fire truck the parking buffer is one block inside city limits but four hundred feet outside a city, while a parked car on a shoulder must be visible for two hundred feet both ways.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: When is parking allowed anywhere within an interstate right of way?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Parking is not allowed anywhere in an interstate right of way, except in designated areas or in an emergency.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: What must a vehicle display to legally use a disabled parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Disabled parking spaces may be used only by a vehicle showing a disability license plate or placard.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: What check should you make outside the car before climbing in to back up?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: Before getting in to back up, check behind the vehicle for children or small objects, which are hard to see from the driver's seat.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: Which hand steers and where should you look while backing a vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: When backing, steer with your left hand and look over your right shoulder through the rear window instead of relying only on the mirrors or side window.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: What is the top safe speed when backing up, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: Back up very slowly, at no more than ten miles per hour, because a vehicle is harder to control and stop in reverse.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: Which speed cap and viewing habit work together whenever you reverse?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: The backing speed limit of no more than ten miles per hour pairs with the rule to look over the right shoulder through the rear window, not just in the mirrors.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Where do crashes happen most frequently, and what share of fatal wrecks occur there?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Intersections are where crashes happen most often, and over one-third of fatal motor vehicle crashes occur there.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: How wide must a median be on a four-lane divided highway for each roadway crossing to count as a separate intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: On a four-lane highway divided by a median wider than thirty feet, each crossing counts as a separate intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: What speed adjustment does North Carolina law require approaching an intersection—even when right of way is yours?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: The law requires you to slow down as you approach an intersection, even when you have the right of way.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: Does holding the right of way excuse you from slowing for an intersection or avoiding a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Having the right of way still requires you to slow down approaching the intersection and to avoid hitting anyone.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: At an intersection without signs or signals, how does a car already inside compare with an approaching car?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: At an intersection with no signs or signals, a vehicle already inside the intersection goes before one that has not entered.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the exact same moment, who holds the right of way?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: When vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same moment, the vehicle on the right has the right of way.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: When two opposing vehicles arrive together and one signals a left turn, who goes first?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: When two facing vehicles arrive together and one wants to turn left, the turning driver must signal and wait, so the driver going straight has the right of way.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: How do first-in, tie-on-right, and straight-versus-left rules stack at an uncontrolled intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection the car already inside goes first, and when two arrive together the car on the right goes first; facing cars split straight-versus-left, with the left turner waiting.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: Is changing lanes permitted while driving straight through an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: Never change lanes while driving straight through an intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: What two actions are mandatory at every stop sign before proceeding or turning?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: At a stop sign you must stop completely and yield to traffic on the through street before moving on or turning.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: How should you exit a private driveway, and how do you handle a blind unmarked intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: When coming out of a private driveway, stop and yield to every vehicle and pedestrian, and at a blind unmarked intersection stop and then creep forward carefully.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: How does a single-point interchange organize ramps and traffic signals?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: A single-point interchange merges two intersections into one above or below a free-flowing road, run by a single set of traffic signals.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: How does a modern roundabout compare in size and speed with an older traffic circle?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: A modern roundabout is much smaller than an older traffic circle and keeps speeds low, about fifteen to twenty miles per hour, which makes it safer.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: Which direction do cars flow in a traffic circle, and from which lane must you exit multi-lane circles?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: In a traffic circle all vehicles travel counterclockwise to the right and leave by turning right; with more than one lane, get into the outside lane before your exit and never turn right from an inside lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.front: How many intersections does a traffic circle count as, and which vehicles hold right of way?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.expected_back: A whole traffic circle counts as one intersection, and vehicles already in the circle have the right of way.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: In a traffic circle, how do entry priority and exit-lane rules work together?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: In a traffic circle the vehicles already circulating have the right of way, and you exit only by turning right from the outside lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.front: What does a yellow roundabout-ahead warning sign tell you, and to whom do you yield at entry?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.expected_back: A yellow roundabout-ahead sign tells you to slow down, and on entry you yield to any vehicles or bicyclists already circulating.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.front: Do drivers circulating inside a roundabout stop for entering cars, and what two steps apply when exiting?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.expected_back: Vehicles inside a roundabout do not yield to those approaching; signal when you exit and yield to pedestrians in the roundabout crosswalk.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: How do yielding duties differ between drivers entering a roundabout and drivers exiting one?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Entering roundabout traffic yields to vehicles and bicyclists already inside, while circulating traffic does not yield to approaching cars but does yield to pedestrians when exiting.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.front: How far around a single-lane roundabout do you travel for a right turn, straight path, left turn, or U-turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.expected_back: In a single-lane roundabout you go a quarter of the way around to turn right, halfway to go straight, three-quarters to turn left, and all the way around for a U-turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.front: When and how do you pick lanes for a multi-lane roundabout, and may you switch lanes inside?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.expected_back: In a multi-lane roundabout, choose your lane from signs and markings before entering: usually the right lane to exit right and the left lane to go straight, turn left or make a U-turn, with no lane changes inside.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: How does making a left turn work in a single-lane roundabout versus a multi-lane roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: In a single-lane roundabout three-quarters of the way around replaces a left turn, while in a multi-lane roundabout the left lane is typically used for straight, left and U-turn movements.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.front: How should you respond to an emergency vehicle at a roundabout before entering versus once already inside?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.expected_back: Never enter a roundabout while an emergency vehicle with lights and siren is going through; if you are already inside, exit first and then pull over.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.front: How should drivers treat bicyclists inside a roundabout, and where must pedestrians cross?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.expected_back: Drivers should not pass a bicyclist inside a roundabout, and pedestrians should use the marked crosswalks around the outside rather than cutting through the middle.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: What must you hold to legally drive on North Carolina public streets and highways, and how does the law view driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: In North Carolina it is illegal to drive a motor vehicle on public streets and highways unless you hold a valid driver license; driving is a legal privilege that comes with responsibility.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: Even without driving down the road, which two behind-the-wheel actions are illegal if you lack a valid license?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Without a valid license you also may not sit behind the wheel while the engine is running, or steer a vehicle while another vehicle pushes or tows it.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: Who is eligible by age to get a regular North Carolina learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: A regular learner permit is available to anyone who is eighteen years old or older.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: Which vehicles may a learner permit holder operate, and what possession rule applies every time they drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: A learner permit lets its holder drive the type or class of vehicle it names, but only while the permit is in the holder's possession.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: Who must ride along when a learner permit holder drives on the highway, and which seat must they occupy?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: When a permit holder drives on the highway, a person licensed for that vehicle must ride in the seat beside them.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: What two conditions must your highway companion meet whenever you drive on a learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: While driving a motor vehicle on the highways, a learner permit holder must be accompanied by a person licensed to operate that vehicle who is seated beside the permit holder.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: Which three checks or exams must you pass to earn a North Carolina learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: To get a learner permit you must pass a vision check, a traffic signs test and a test on motor vehicle laws.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Which four areas may an applicant for any original North Carolina driver license be tested on?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: Applicants for any original driver license may be tested on vision, motor vehicle law knowledge, traffic signs, and driving skill in an on-road test.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: How are North Carolina driver license tests scored — can acing one exam offset failing another?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: Every driver license test is scored on its own, so you must pass each one separately.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How does the test lineup for an original driver license go beyond the three learner permit tests?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: The learner permit tests are vision, signs and motor vehicle law knowledge, while an original license can also require the on-road driving skill test.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: How must you identify each sign on the traffic signs test, and where can every tested sign be found?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: On the signs test you must recognize each traffic sign by its color and shape and say what it means; every sign on that test appears in the handbook.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: What two subjects does the knowledge test cover, and what accommodation is available if reading is difficult?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: The knowledge test covers traffic laws and safe driving practices, and an audio version can be requested by applicants who struggle with reading.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: What separates the traffic signs test from the knowledge test at the license office?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The signs test and the knowledge test are not the same test: the signs test asks you to identify signs by color and shape and give their meaning, while the knowledge test covers traffic laws and safe driving practices.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: During which in-person licensing visits does North Carolina check your vision?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Your vision is checked whenever you apply in person, whether for a learner permit, an original license or a renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: If you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision check, what goes on your license and when must you wear them?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: If you need glasses or contacts to meet the vision standard, you must wear them every time you drive, and your license will carry a corrective-lens restriction.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: How severely does North Carolina punish driving without the corrective lenses required on your license?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Driving without the corrective lenses your license requires is punished the same way as driving with no license at all.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Why is violating a corrective-lens restriction far worse than a minor equipment ticket?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: A corrective-lens restriction is not a suggestion: driving without the required lenses is treated like driving unlicensed, not like a minor equipment fault.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: How do mental or physical conditions affect licensing — when is a license denied versus issued with restrictions?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: A person whose mental or physical condition could make driving unsafe may be denied a license, while a person with a disability can get a restricted license if the condition does not prevent safe driving.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Does having a disability automatically bar someone from getting a North Carolina license?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: A disability does not automatically bar licensing: the deciding question is whether the condition keeps the person from driving safely, and a restricted license is possible when it does not.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Where does the on-road driving test fall in the testing sequence, and how does it apply to permits, first licenses, and renewals?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: The on-road driving test comes last, after every other test is passed; it is required for a first license, may be required at renewal, and is never required for a learner permit.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: Compare whether an on-road test is required for a learner permit, a first license, and a license renewal?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.memory_hook: Permit never, first yes, renewal maybe
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: The road test is the final step for a first license, but it is not required for a learner permit, and it may or may not be required at renewal.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What is the general rule on taking the on-road test for original license applicants, and is it absolute?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: Original license applicants must take the on-road test, although the handbook notes some cases where it may not be required.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: What two broad abilities do you demonstrate to the examiner during the on-road driving test?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: During the road test you show that you can perform basic driving patterns and drive safely in traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: From intersections and quick stops to posture and turnabouts, which driving skills and habits do road-test examiners grade?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: Road-test examiners grade how you approach intersections, stop signs and signals; quick stops on command; backing; stopping, starting and parking; clutch use in a manual car; turn signals and horn; turning; lane use; following; passing and being passed; yielding to pedestrians and vehicles; posture; and the three-point turnabout.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What kind of vehicle must you bring and drive for your driving skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: You must take the driving skills test in a vehicle that represents the license class you are applying for.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: Starting at the far right edge, what actions make up step one of a three-point turnabout?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: Three-point turnabout, step one: from the far right edge of the road, check for traffic, signal left, creep forward turning the wheel left, and stop several inches from the left curb or edge.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: Which way do you move and turn the wheel during step two of a three-point turnabout, and where do you stop?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: Three-point turnabout, step two: back up slowly while turning the wheel right, and stop several inches from the right curb or edge.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: How do you complete step three of a three-point turnabout?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: Three-point turnabout, step three: move forward slowly with the wheel turned left to complete the turnabout.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: Across all three moves of a three-point turnabout, which direction does the steering wheel turn on each leg?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: In the three-point turnabout the wheel goes left on both forward moves and right on the backward move.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: What two broad license categories does North Carolina issue, and what determines the class you need?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: North Carolina issues both a regular driver license and a commercial driver license, and the vehicle you will drive decides which class you need.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: Which regular license class covers everyday personal cars and small trucks for most North Carolina drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: Most drivers only need a regular Class C license for personal cars and small trucks.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: What weight ratings and driver age rule define the vehicles covered by a regular Class C license?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: A regular Class C license covers a noncommercial single vehicle rated under twenty-six thousand one pounds, and a towing combination rated under twenty-six thousand one pounds combined when the driver is at least eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: Since both regular and commercial licenses use Classes A, B, and C, which specific credential is the ordinary everyday car license?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: Regular license classes and commercial license classes share the letters A, B and C, but a regular Class C is the ordinary noncommercial license that most car and small-truck drivers need.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: Which CDL-exempt vehicle combination requires a regular Class A license?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: A regular Class A license covers a CDL-exempt vehicle combination whose towed unit has a gross vehicle weight rating of ten thousand one pounds or more.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: What CDL-exempt single vehicle — and optional towed weight — falls under a regular Class B license?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: A regular Class B license covers a CDL-exempt single vehicle rated at twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, including when it tows a vehicle rated no more than ten thousand pounds.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: How does the weight threshold that triggers a regular Class A license differ from the one for regular Class B?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: The regular Class A threshold is about the towed unit, rated ten thousand one pounds or more, while the regular Class B threshold is about a single vehicle rated twenty-six thousand one pounds or more.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Which separate handbooks must commercial license applicants and motorcycle applicants study?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: CDL Class A, B or C applicants study the CDL Handbook, and motorcycle endorsement or motorcycle permit applicants study the Motorcycle Handbook.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: Does being an unpaid volunteer excuse a driver from holding a commercial driver license for listed passenger or property vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: A commercial driver license is required for paid or volunteer drivers of the listed vehicle types that are built or used to carry passengers or property.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: What two minimum weight ratings define a commercial Class A combination vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: A commercial Class A vehicle is a combination with a combined weight rating of at least twenty-six thousand one pounds whose towed unit is rated at least ten thousand one pounds.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: Which single vehicles or towing combinations count as commercial Class B vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: A commercial Class B vehicle is a single vehicle rated at least twenty-six thousand one pounds, or a combination whose towing unit is rated at least twenty-six thousand one pounds while the towed unit is rated under ten thousand one pounds.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: Outside Classes A and B, what two passenger or cargo features make a vehicle commercial Class C?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: A commercial Class C vehicle is one outside Classes A and B that is built to carry sixteen or more people counting the driver, or that carries hazardous materials requiring placards.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: Why isn't a commercial Class C vehicle defined by heavy weight alone?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: A commercial Class C vehicle is defined by what it carries, sixteen or more people counting the driver or placarded hazardous materials, not by weight alone.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: Which four vehicle categories are exempt from needing a CDL, and what license must their drivers still hold?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: No CDL is needed for recreational vehicles, military equipment, fire or emergency equipment, or certain farm vehicles, but a regular license of the right class is always required.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: Which license allows on-duty volunteer fire, rescue, or EMS members to operate Class A, B, or C emergency vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: On-duty volunteer fire, rescue or EMS members may drive Class A, B or C fire-fighting, rescue or EMS vehicles while holding only a regular A, B or C license.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: Which five commercial hauling or passenger operations each require a special CDL endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: Hauling hazardous materials, carrying passengers, driving school or activity buses, pulling double trailers and driving tank vehicles each require a special CDL endorsement.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: What two credential options legally allow someone to ride a motorcycle on North Carolina public roads?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: To operate a motorcycle on public roads, a person needs a motorcycle learner permit or a regular or commercial license carrying a motorcycle endorsement.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: What existing license — and signature if under eighteen — must an applicant already have to get a motorcycle learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: A motorcycle learner permit applicant aged sixteen to seventeen must already hold a full provisional license and have a parent or guardian sign; an applicant eighteen or older must already hold a license from the division.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How does a motorcycle endorsement differ structurally from a motorcycle learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: A motorcycle endorsement is added to an existing regular or commercial license, while a motorcycle learner permit is a separate permit; either one allows motorcycle operation on public roads.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: What age, experience, CDL, and certificate rules apply to school bus drivers, and how do activity bus drivers differ?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: A school bus driver must be at least eighteen, have at least six months of driving experience, and hold a Class B or C CDL with S and P endorsements plus a School Bus Driver's Certificate; activity bus drivers meet the same terms without the certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: What single credential requirement separates a regular school bus driver from a school activity bus driver?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: A school bus driver needs a School Bus Driver's Certificate on top of the CDL endorsements, while a school activity bus driver meets the same requirements without that certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.front: Who is permanently barred by North Carolina statute from receiving or renewing a CDL with a P or S endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.expected_back: Under G.S. twenty-thirty-seven.14A, the division will not issue or renew a CDL with a P or S endorsement for anyone who must register as a sex offender.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.front: What two visual features let you recognize highway signs instantly, and what are the three sign groups?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.expected_back: Shape and color let you identify the kinds of highway signs at a glance, and traffic signs are divided into three types: regulatory, warning, and guide or informational.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.front: Which single traffic sign uses an eight-sided octagon, and what colors appear on it?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.expected_back: The eight-sided octagon is used only for stop signs, which show white STOP lettering on a red background.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.front: How far ahead of an intersection does a stop sign typically stand, and what must you do?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.expected_back: A stop sign is usually placed six to fifty feet before the intersection, and the law requires a full stop there.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.front: Once you make a complete stop at a stop sign, when may you pull forward?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.expected_back: After stopping at a stop sign, do not move again until you are certain the way is clear.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.front: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt when a required stop has no painted line or crosswalk?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.expected_back: When a sign or signal requires a stop, stop at the marked stop line; with no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection at a point where you can see the cross street.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.front: What colors and shape identify a yield sign, and what action does it require?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.expected_back: The yield sign is a red and white triangle pointing down, and it requires you to slow down and give the right of way.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.front: When are you required to come to a complete stop at a yield sign?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.expected_back: At a yield sign, whether you must stop depends on cross traffic; if needed to avoid interfering with it, stop and wait until it passes.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.front: How does your legal obligation at a stop sign differ from your obligation at a yield sign?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.expected_back: A stop sign always demands a full stop, while a yield sign demands slowing and yielding, with a stop only when cross traffic requires it.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.front: Which distinct geometric outlines belong exclusively to stop signs versus yield signs?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.expected_back: The octagon belongs to the stop sign alone, while the downward-pointing triangle belongs to the yield sign.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.front: What colors and messages appear on rectangular or square regulatory signs, and what if you ignore one?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.expected_back: Rectangular and square regulatory signs, usually black and white or red and white, show speed limits and rules such as NO U-TURN, and disobeying them is a traffic violation.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.front: Who is legally allowed to park in a stall marked by a handicap parking sign?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.expected_back: A handicap parking sign reserves the space for qualifying people who display a handicap license plate or dashboard placard.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.front: Which side of the highway holds the yellow pennant sign, and what zone does it mark?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.expected_back: The yellow pennant-shaped sign sits on the left side of the road and marks the start of a no-passing zone, reinforcing the rectangular DO NOT PASS sign.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.front: How does the yellow left-side pennant work alongside the rectangular DO NOT PASS sign?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.expected_back: The yellow pennant on the left marks where a no-passing zone begins, while the rectangular DO NOT PASS sign states the rule itself.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.front: What message type and standard color scheme belong to diamond-shaped signs?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.expected_back: Diamond-shaped signs give cautions or warnings and are normally black on yellow.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.front: What hazard ahead is signaled by a diamond sign painted black on orange?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.expected_back: A diamond sign in black on orange warns of a construction or maintenance area, so drive with extra care.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.front: What changes in meaning when a warning diamond shifts from yellow to orange?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.expected_back: A diamond in black on yellow is an ordinary warning, while a diamond in black on orange warns of a construction or maintenance area.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.front: Why do highway crews place a STOP AHEAD warning sign well upstream of certain intersections?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.expected_back: The STOP AHEAD warning sign is placed well before a stop sign whose view is blocked by a curve or other objects.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.front: What does a round yellow sign bearing a black X and RR warn you to do?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.expected_back: A round yellow sign with a black X and the letters RR warns of a railroad crossing ahead, so slow down and stop if needed to cross safely.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.front: What colors and exact words appear on the crossbuck standing right at railroad tracks?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.expected_back: The crossbuck at the tracks reads RAILROAD CROSSING in black on white crosspieces.
