sec15-card-sec15-R05.front: How do the round yellow RR sign and the white crossbuck differ in where they stand?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.expected_back: The round yellow RR sign gives advance warning before the crossing, while the white crossbuck stands at the crossing itself.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.front: After stopping for a train signal, lowered gate, or flagger, when is it legal to cross?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.expected_back: Once stopped for a train signal, gate or flagger, stay stopped until the gate rises or the signal or flagger shows it is safe.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.front: How many times should you look each way before driving across railroad tracks?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.expected_back: Before crossing railroad tracks, look twice in each direction.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.front: What absolute rule does the DO NOT STOP ON TRACKS reminder enforce?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.expected_back: The DO NOT STOP ON TRACKS sign reminds drivers never to stop on a railroad track for any reason.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.front: What zone or crossing does a five-sided pentagon sign warn about?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.expected_back: The five-sided pentagon sign warns of a school zone or school crossing, where you should watch especially for children.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.front: How do speed limits typically change inside many school zones?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.expected_back: In many school zones the speed limit is lowered during certain school hours.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.front: Which two school areas use the five-sided pentagon, and whom must you watch for?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.expected_back: The five-sided pentagon sign warns of a school zone or a school crossing, where drivers should be especially watchful for children.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.front: What four kinds of helpful travel details do guide and informational signs provide?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.expected_back: Guide and informational signs give directions, routes, distances and the locations of services.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.front: Which compass directions generally match odd-numbered highways versus even-numbered highways?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.expected_back: Odd-numbered highways generally run north and south, and even-numbered highways generally run east and west.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.front: How can you tell a north-south highway from an east-west highway by its route number?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.expected_back: Odd-numbered highways generally run north to south, whereas even-numbered highways generally run east to west.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.front: How does the shape of a U.S. highway marker differ from a North Carolina state route marker?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.expected_back: U.S. highway route markers are shield shaped, while North Carolina route markers are diamond shaped.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.front: What shape marks North Carolina secondary roads, and what emblem marks interstate highways?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.expected_back: North Carolina secondary road signs are rectangular, and interstate highways use a red, white and blue shield.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.front: How do U.S. routes, interstates, and North Carolina state routes differ in shape and color?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.expected_back: U.S. route markers are shields, interstate markers are red, white and blue shields, and North Carolina route markers are diamonds.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.front: Which three emergency or help locations can blue-and-white roadside signs point toward?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.expected_back: Blue and white signs point to a nearby hospital, Highway Patrol station or telephone.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.front: Which three background colors are used on rectangular guide signs showing directions and distances?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.expected_back: Rectangular guide signs may be green, brown or blue and give directions and distances.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.front: What should you do instead of stopping in a travel lane to puzzle over a road sign?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.expected_back: Never stop in the middle of the road to read a sign; when safe, pull onto the shoulder and work out your route there.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.front: How do yellow pavement lines and white pavement lines differ in the traffic directions they separate?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.expected_back: Yellow lines divide lanes going in opposite directions, and white lines divide lanes going the same direction.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.front: Which lane-line color separates opposing traffic, and which separates traffic moving together?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.expected_back: Yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic, while white lines separate traffic moving the same way.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.front: What passing rule applies along a single broken yellow center line on a two-lane, two-way road?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.expected_back: A broken yellow center line on a two-lane, two-way road means careful passing is allowed in both directions.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.front: What passing rule applies across double solid yellow center lines?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.expected_back: Double solid yellow center lines may not be crossed to pass from either direction.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.front: When a broken yellow stripe pairs with a solid yellow stripe, when may you pass with care?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.expected_back: On a two-lane road you may pass with care when the broken yellow line is on your side.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.front: How does a broken yellow line on your side differ from double solid yellow lines?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.expected_back: A broken yellow line on your side lets you pass with care, but double solid yellow lines forbid passing from either side.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.front: Which edge of a divided highway gets a solid white stripe, and which edge gets a solid yellow stripe?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.expected_back: A single solid white line marks the right edge of the road, and a single solid yellow line marks the left edge on a divided highway.

sec15-card-sec15-F33.front: What does it mean if you look down and see the white edge line on your left and yellow on your right?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.expected_back: If the white edge line is on your left and the yellow edge line on your right, you are going the wrong way.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.front: What is a center two-way left-turn lane strictly reserved for, and what two moves are banned in it?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.expected_back: A center two-way left-turn lane on some multi-lane highways is only for left turns from either direction, never for passing or merging.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.front: How do white and yellow reflective road markers help on wet nights, and what do red ones warn?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.expected_back: White and yellow reflective pavement markers make lane lines easier to see on wet roads at night, while red markers warn that you are going the wrong way.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.front: What do raised blue reflective markers in the pavement point out?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.expected_back: In some areas, blue reflective markers in the road show where fire hydrants or water supplies are for firefighters.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.front: How does the meaning of red reflective pavement markers differ from blue ones?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.expected_back: Red pavement markers warn of wrong-way travel, while blue markers show the location of fire hydrants or water supplies.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.front: Whose instructions must you follow when a traffic officer directs an intersection that has working lights or signs?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.expected_back: When a traffic officer is directing traffic, obey the officer's hand signals instead of the usual signals or signs.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.front: What hand gestures and whistle blasts does an officer typically use for stop versus go?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.expected_back: An officer usually signals stop with a raised palm facing the vehicle and a long whistle blast, and signals go with a hand motion and a series of short blasts.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.front: What tool may a traffic officer use to direct drivers after dark?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.expected_back: At night, a traffic officer may give signals with a flashlight.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: When North Carolina law requires a railroad-crossing stop, within what distance range from the nearest rail must you halt?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Stopping inside that thirty-five-foot safety band keeps your front bumper clear of overhanging boxcars while preserving track sightlines.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Which active crossing devices or personnel legally trigger a mandatory railroad stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Any electric flasher, mechanical warning, dropped arm, or human flagger means steel wheels are already closing on the grade.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: Even without gates, which two train-approach situations require you to stop at a crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Passive rural crossings lack gates, so a locomotive horn within roughly fifteen hundred feet or a close visible engine demands braking.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: What counts as stopping too close versus stopping too far back at a railroad crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Creeping inside fifteen feet risks getting clipped by wide rail equipment, while halting past fifty feet blocks clear track scanning.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: How does North Carolina's audible train-horn distance compare in scale with your bumper's stopping zone?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Test writers love swapping fifteen hundred feet with fifty feet, so keep the distant horn trigger separate from your rail stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: May drivers or pedestrians go around, under, or through a crossing gate that is closed or moving?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Zigzagging around a descending or lowered barrier gambles your life against a locomotive closing faster than human eyes judge.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: How should vehicles position themselves while waiting at a railroad crossing, and when are two lines legal?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Doubling up on a two-lane road blocks opposing lanes unless pavement markings provide four or more total lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: How is breaking North Carolina's railroad signal law classified, and when does an employer face penalties too?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Dispatchers or companies that knowingly let commercial drivers run railroad warnings face both an infraction and civil fines.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: What does a yellow-and-black advance RR sign tell you to do as you approach?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Spotting the round yellow disc early lets you quiet the cabin, scan both directions down the rails, and cover the brake.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: Who holds the right of way over every road user—even police, fire, and ambulances—and what if a stop sign is posted?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Locomotives cannot swerve or brake like rubber-tired emergency rigs, and any posted crossing octagon requires a complete stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: Roughly how much distance does a train traveling fifty-five miles per hour need to come to a stop?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Even if an engineer slams emergency brakes the instant they spot your car, steel momentum carries past eighteen football fields.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: How should you approach and depart a railroad crossing sign, and what rule applies to stopping on the tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Wait until space clears completely on the far side because halting on the rails for any reason risks catastrophic impact.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What shape marks the crossing itself, and what does a smaller plaque mounted beneath it indicate?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Noticing a multiple-track number plaque warns you that a hidden second train can arrive right behind the first.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.question_text: When crossing warning lights activate, when must you stop—and is driving through lowered gates ever lawful?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.teaching_text: Trying to beat descending gate arms is illegal and risks getting struck before you clear the far rail.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.question_text: Why is driving along or across railroad tracks anywhere outside an official grade crossing illegal?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.teaching_text: Railroad corridors are private rights-of-way where ungraded ballast and high-speed trains trap off-road shortcuts.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.question_text: What is your legal duty toward an approaching train at a rural crossing marked only by a bare crossbuck?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.teaching_text: Lack of flashing bulbs or gates never shifts priority away from an oncoming locomotive.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.question_text: Which intersection signal rule matches flashing red lights mounted on a railroad crossbuck?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.teaching_text: Flashing red lenses carry identical mandatory stop authority whether hanging over asphalt or flanking steel rails.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.question_text: How does your duty at a crossbuck with flashing red lights compare with a bare crossbuck lacking lights or gates?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.teaching_text: Active red flashers command an immediate stop, whereas an unlit passive crossbuck functions like a yield sign toward trains.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.question_text: Why must you wait until red lights stop flashing instead of rolling forward the instant a caboose clears?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.teaching_text: Departing boxcars hide fast opposing trains on parallel tracks until the warning flashers shut off completely.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.question_text: Which four commercial or transit vehicle types should you expect to stop at railroad crossings even without a train?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.teaching_text: Leaving extra following space behind buses and placarded tankers prevents rear-ending them when they make mandatory track checks.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.question_text: What should you do if warning lights start flashing or gates begin lowering while your car is already on the tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.teaching_text: Signal timing builds in clearance seconds before train arrival, whereas braking or shifting into reverse traps you mid-track.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.question_text: Can a lowering crossing gate physically trap your car on the tracks if it drops ahead of you?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.teaching_text: Lightweight fiberglass arms are engineered to snap or flex harmlessly rather than let hesitant drivers stall on live rails.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.question_text: Even though flexible gates cannot trap you, what everyday traffic mistake easily pins cars onto railroad tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.teaching_text: Following a bumper onto the crossing before room opens beyond leaves nowhere to go when a red light halts the line.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.question_text: How does your crossing response flip depending on whether signals start before you enter or while you are on the rails?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.teaching_text: Stopping belongs strictly outside the gate line, while commitment forward clears the danger zone once tires touch the crossing.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.question_text: What three pieces of emergency information appear on the Blue Sign posted at every North Carolina highway-rail crossing?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.teaching_text: Every approach direction displays that blue Emergency Notification plaque so callers pinpoint the exact crossing in seconds.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.question_text: What is the quickest way to halt an approaching train during a track emergency, and how is your location identified?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.teaching_text: Phoning the railroad dispatch desk directly with the unique federal crossing identifier alerts nearby train crews faster than local relays.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.question_text: What immediate action must everyone take if your vehicle stalls on or right beside railroad tracks?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.teaching_text: Abandoning the cabin at once and moving quickly down the roadway keeps flying collision debris away from passengers.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: When a car stalls on the tracks, which step comes first—calling the Blue Sign number or getting everyone out?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Dialing from inside a dead vehicle wastes survival seconds if a silent train rounds the curve before dispatch answers.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.question_text: Who handles active crossing emergencies via the Blue Sign versus reports of damaged or missing signs?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.teaching_text: Live track hazards go straight to the railroad's dispatch number, while sign maintenance issues go to the Federal Railroad Administration.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.question_text: Why must right-turning city drivers watch carefully for a bicyclist riding straight through the intersection?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.teaching_text: Turning right across a straight-moving cyclist's curbside path causes classic right-hook intersection crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.question_text: What is the safe move if you realize too late that you are in the wrong lane for a city turn?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.teaching_text: Cutting abruptly across crowded city lanes triggers side-swipes when circling the next intersection costs under a minute.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.question_text: Which visual clue on the car ahead warns that you are cruising inside its driver's blind spot?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.teaching_text: If the forward driver's rearview mirror is hidden from your angle, their mirror cannot reflect your headlights either.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.question_text: Beside avoiding lane weaving, how should you divide through travel versus turns on a multi-lane one-way street?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.teaching_text: Holding middle lanes for straight travel leaves left and right curb lanes clear for turning traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.question_text: Which three physical factors often make rural roads deadlier than congested city streets?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.teaching_text: Higher cruising speeds combined with narrow unlit shoulders turn minor rural drift into severe high-energy crashes.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.question_text: Why are primary-highway cruising speeds unsafe on secondary country roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.teaching_text: Tighter bends and blind hill crests hide farm equipment or stopped cars inside your highway braking distance.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.question_text: Which design features make interstate highways statistically safer than conventional roads?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.teaching_text: Dividing opposing traffic while eliminating rail crossings, sharp bends, stop signs, and traffic lights removes angle-crash points.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.question_text: How should you use the acceleration lane when merging onto an interstate highway?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.teaching_text: Entering mainline lanes sluggishly forces fast highway traffic to slam brakes or swerve across lanes.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.question_text: Which interstate lanes are for cruising versus passing, and what following rule helps prevent common rear-end crashes?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.teaching_text: Rear-end collisions top interstate crash charts whenever drivers camp close behind bumpers instead of holding a two-second gap.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.question_text: How often does North Carolina recommend stopping at interstate rest areas, and where must you never halt?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.teaching_text: Highway hypnosis dulls reaction times over long stretches, while stopping inside a live travel lane invites fatal rear impacts.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.question_text: After pulling well off the interstate for a breakdown, how do you signal distress by day and at night?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.teaching_text: A white cloth on the antenna or left handle plus an open hood alerts patrols by day, and flashers mark you after dark.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.question_text: How does proper interstate breakdown procedure reinforce the rule against stopping in travel lanes?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.teaching_text: Coasting far onto the shoulder before raising the hood and tying a white cloth keeps disabled metal out of live traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.question_text: When should you signal and begin braking as you take an interstate exit?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.teaching_text: Holding mainline speed until your tires enter the deceleration lane protects trailing highway traffic from sudden braking.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.question_text: How do speed changes in an acceleration lane contrast with speed changes in a deceleration lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.teaching_text: Both auxiliary lanes shield mainline traffic from speed mismatches—building speed before merging in and shedding speed after moving out.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.question_text: Why is driving far below the posted speed limit hazardous on an interstate, and how should you pace yourself?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.teaching_text: Large speed gaps create rolling chicanes that trigger sudden lane changes, provided matching flow stays within the speed limit.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.question_text: What three moves are forbidden if you miss your interstate exit, and what must you do instead?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.teaching_text: Reversing on a freeway shoulder or cutting across gore grass causes deadly high-speed broadsides.

sec10-card-sec10-F39.question_text: What immediate steps must you take if you accidentally enter an interstate ramp going the wrong way?
sec10-card-sec10-F39.teaching_text: Getting onto the right-side edge immediately pulls you out of head-on lanes until a gap lets you turn around safely.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.question_text: Why do you keep driving forward after a missed exit yet stop immediately on the right shoulder after a wrong-way entry?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.teaching_text: Continuing with legal flow reaches the next interchange safely, whereas wrong-way travel faces oncoming traffic head-on.

sec10-card-sec10-F40.question_text: From how many feet away at night should high beams versus low beams reveal a person ahead?
sec10-card-sec10-F40.teaching_text: Notice how low beams illuminate barely a third of high-beam reach, limiting safe nighttime city speeds.

sec10-card-sec10-F41.question_text: Which two mechanical or loading factors knock headlights out of alignment and blind oncoming drivers?
sec10-card-sec10-F41.teaching_text: Packing heavy gear into the trunk squats the rear suspension and tilts low beams straight into opposing windshields.

sec10-card-sec10-F42.question_text: What color and visibility distance apply to taillights, and what color and distance apply to the license-plate lamp?
sec10-card-sec10-F42.teaching_text: Bright red rear lamps warn trailing traffic five hundred feet back while a crisp white bulb illuminates plate numbers at fifty.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.question_text: Can you pair all four North Carolina night-lighting distances—high beams, low beams, taillights, and license plate?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.teaching_text: Keep seeing-ahead benchmarks separate from being-seen rear requirements so exam distractors never scramble those four numbers.

sec13-card-sec13-F01.question_text: What three immediate steps should you take right after hitting an animal or spotting an injured one?
sec13-card-sec13-F01.teaching_text: Staying locked inside off the travel lane keeps both passing cars and panicked wildlife from hurting you.

sec13-card-sec13-F02.question_text: Why should you never walk up to an animal that your vehicle has struck?
sec13-card-sec13-F02.teaching_text: Wounded, terrified wildlife can lash out unpredictably and seriously injure anyone who steps close.

sec13-card-sec13-F04.question_text: What is North Carolina's number-one rule in any sudden driving emergency?
sec13-card-sec13-F04.teaching_text: Freezing up or jerking controls in panic turns a recoverable roadside scare into a severe wreck.

sec13-card-sec13-F05.question_text: What three steps slow a manual-transmission car when the regular brakes fail?
sec13-card-sec13-F05.teaching_text: Engine compression starts scrubbing speed immediately before the parking brake adds extra stopping force.

sec13-card-sec13-F06.question_text: What two controls should you use if the brakes fail in an automatic car?
sec13-card-sec13-F06.teaching_text: Combining the emergency brake with low gear gives you mechanical drag when hydraulic brakes quit.

sec13-card-sec13-R01.question_text: How does handling brake failure in a manual car differ from handling it in an automatic?
sec13-card-sec13-R01.teaching_text: Knowledge checks test sequence: stick-shift drivers engage a lower gear and clutch before pulling the emergency brake.

sec13-card-sec13-F07.question_text: Why should you still force low gear and the emergency brake during brake failure despite possible wear?
sec13-card-sec13-F07.teaching_text: Worn transmission gears or brake cables can be repaired at a shop, whereas a runaway crash cannot.

sec13-card-sec13-F08.question_text: How do you dry wet brakes safely after driving through water?
sec13-card-sec13-F08.teaching_text: Gentle pedal pressure over a short stretch creates just enough warmth to evaporate moisture off the pads.

sec13-card-sec13-F09.question_text: How and when should you set up your speed control for a long or steep downhill grade?
sec13-card-sec13-F09.teaching_text: Riding the brake pedal all the way down a mountain overheats linings and causes dangerous brake fade.

sec13-card-sec13-R02.question_text: When do you drag light brake pressure briefly, and when do you rely on a lower gear instead?
sec13-card-sec13-R02.teaching_text: Mixing these up is dangerous because dragging brakes down a long grade overheats them instead of helping.

sec13-card-sec13-F10.question_text: What steps should you follow if your accelerator sticks down while driving?
sec13-card-sec13-F10.teaching_text: Popping the transmission into neutral disconnects engine power from the wheels so steady braking can stop you.

sec13-card-sec13-R03.question_text: How does your gear choice for a stuck gas pedal differ from your gear choice for failed brakes?
sec13-card-sec13-R03.teaching_text: Downshifting a roaring stuck engine keeps driving the wheels forward, whereas neutral cuts power right away.

sec13-card-sec13-F11.question_text: What ride change tells you to stop and inspect your tires, and how does a sudden blowout feel?
sec13-card-sec13-F11.teaching_text: Catching an odd vibration early lets you pull over before the tire bursts with a loud bang.

sec13-card-sec13-F19.question_text: What should you do with the steering wheel and gas pedal the instant a tire blows out?
sec13-card-sec13-F19.teaching_text: Holding your lane while easing off the gas keeps weight balanced when a blown tire tugs hard.

sec13-card-sec13-F20.question_text: When is it safe to touch the brake pedal and pull off the road after a tire blowout?
sec13-card-sec13-F20.teaching_text: Stomping the brake right after a tire bursts pitches weight forward and spins the car out.

sec13-card-sec13-F12.question_text: What three setup steps come before you start changing a flat tire?
sec13-card-sec13-F12.teaching_text: Getting completely out of live lanes and locking the parking brake keeps the jack from tipping.

sec13-card-sec13-R04.question_text: How do your actions while rolling through a blowout differ from starting a roadside flat change?
sec13-card-sec13-R04.teaching_text: Surviving the rolling emergency comes first; wrenching on a spare waits until you sit clear of traffic.

sec13-card-sec13-F13.question_text: How must passengers exit during a tire change, and where must they never stand?
sec13-card-sec13-F13.teaching_text: Stepping out away from traffic and staying clear of bumpers protects riders if another car clips yours.

sec13-card-sec13-F14.question_text: Which lights should run and how do you stop the vehicle from rolling during a tire change?
sec13-card-sec13-F14.teaching_text: Chocking the grounded tires keeps the car from creeping off the jack while lights warn approaching drivers.

sec13-card-sec13-F15.question_text: What should you do instead of trying to fix a disabled car right next to passing traffic?
sec13-card-sec13-F15.teaching_text: Kneeling beside fast-moving lanes for DIY repairs puts your life inches from distracted highway drivers.

sec13-card-sec13-F16.question_text: Where should the car sit and where should everyone wait after a roadside breakdown?
sec13-card-sec13-F16.teaching_text: Drifting drivers often strike stalled shoulder vehicles from behind, making front and rear bumper zones deadly.

sec13-card-sec13-F17.question_text: How do you signal that your broken-down car needs help by day and after dark?
sec13-card-sec13-F17.teaching_text: A raised hood and white cloth on the left handle or antenna alert troopers without standing in lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-R05.question_text: Which visual markers ask for breakdown help, and which doors must everyone use to get out?
sec13-card-sec13-R05.teaching_text: Notice the sides: the white cloth goes on the traffic-side handle or antenna while people exit curbside.

sec13-card-sec13-F18.question_text: Which night-visibility items should stay in your vehicle at all times for emergencies?
sec13-card-sec13-F18.teaching_text: Nighttime breakdowns happen without warning, and having light ready makes you visible to oncoming cars.

sec13-card-sec13-F21.question_text: What two immediate warnings and speed steps come first if an oncoming car crosses the center line?
sec13-card-sec13-F21.teaching_text: Shedding speed buys time and cuts impact energy while the horn can snap a drowsy driver awake.

sec13-card-sec13-F22.question_text: Which direction must you steer if an oncoming vehicle enters your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-F22.teaching_text: Swinging left risks meeting the other driver head-on when they wake up and swerve back into their own lane.

sec13-card-sec13-F23.question_text: What two panic moves must you avoid if your wheels drop off the pavement edge onto the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-F23.teaching_text: Catching a raised pavement lip at speed with a sharp tug spins or flips the vehicle across lanes.

sec13-card-sec13-F24.question_text: How do you safely bring your car back onto the pavement after dropping onto the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-F24.teaching_text: Waiting until you are nearly stopped with clear lanes lets tires climb the pavement edge without snapping sideways.

sec13-card-sec13-R06.question_text: How does recovering from a dropped wheel differ from escaping an oncoming car in your lane?
sec13-card-sec13-R06.teaching_text: Both emergencies punish panic left jerks: hold straight and slow on shoulders, and steer right from head-on threats.

sec13-card-sec13-F25.question_text: Which three slick road surfaces raise skid risk, and how should you adjust speed on them?
sec13-card-sec13-F25.teaching_text: Sudden throttle or brake changes break tire grip instantly on rain-slick pavement, ice, or packed snow.

sec13-card-sec13-F26.question_text: How should you brake to prevent a skid in an ABS car compared with a non-ABS car?
sec13-card-sec13-F26.teaching_text: Anti-lock computers pulse the brakes for you only while you hold steady pressure, whereas standard brakes need gentle pumping.

sec13-card-sec13-R08.question_text: What is the key pedal difference when trying to avoid a skid with ABS versus without ABS?
sec13-card-sec13-R08.teaching_text: Test questions swap these constantly: pumping defeats anti-lock brakes, while locking steady without ABS triggers a slide.

sec13-card-sec13-F27.question_text: What should you do with the gas pedal and steering wheel once a skid starts?
sec13-card-sec13-F27.teaching_text: Turning toward the sliding rear aligns the front tires with your travel path so grip can return.

sec13-card-sec13-F28.question_text: What steering adjustment is needed right as your skidding car begins to straighten out?
sec13-card-sec13-F28.teaching_text: Holding the first turn angle too long snaps the tail into an opposite spin across the roadway.

sec13-card-sec13-R07.question_text: In what exact order do the two steering moves happen during skid recovery?
sec13-card-sec13-R07.teaching_text: Catching the slide first and unwinding as the nose straightens keeps one skid from becoming two.

sec13-card-sec13-F29.question_text: What should you do if an oncoming collision looks unavoidable?
sec13-card-sec13-F29.teaching_text: Brushing bushes or rolling into an open field on the right beats a deadly head-on impact every time.

sec13-card-sec13-F30.question_text: How should you respond if a car is about to rear-end you and the lane ahead is open?
sec13-card-sec13-F30.teaching_text: Moving forward gives the trailing car extra stopping feet while pressing against the headrest limits whiplash.

sec13-card-sec13-R09.question_text: Which two protective actions go together when a rear-end hit is coming and space ahead is open?
sec13-card-sec13-R09.teaching_text: Adding space softens the blow, and bracing your skull flat against the support protects your neck.

sec13-card-sec13-F32.question_text: How should you hold the steering wheel when a collision is about to strike your car?
sec13-card-sec13-F32.teaching_text: Keeping a firm hold helps stop the impact from wrenching the wheel and sending you into secondary hits.

sec13-card-sec13-F33.question_text: Along with staying ready to steer, what last-resort move shields you right before glass shatters?
sec13-card-sec13-F33.teaching_text: Covering your eyes and face with your arms at the final split second guards against flying glass.

sec13-card-sec13-F31.question_text: How does North Carolina law treat bystanders who stop to help crash victims, and what is excluded?
sec13-card-sec13-F31.teaching_text: Legal protection encourages motorists to render aid without fear, provided they avoid unruly or intentional misconduct.

sec13-card-sec13-F34.question_text: What is every driver legally required to do immediately when involved in any crash?
sec13-card-sec13-F34.teaching_text: Leaving the scene of an accident—even a minor one—turns a traffic mishap into a hit-and-run offense.

sec13-card-sec13-F35.question_text: Once stopped at a crash scene, what three priorities must be handled right away?
sec13-card-sec13-F35.teaching_text: Securing the scene, helping hurt people, and alerting officers keeps one wreck from escalating.

sec13-card-sec13-F36.question_text: When should crash vehicles on a highway lane, ramp, or shoulder be moved onto the shoulder?
sec13-card-sec13-F36.teaching_text: Getting drivable cars out of live highway lanes when nobody is hurt or killed prevents deadly secondary collisions.

sec13-card-sec13-F37.question_text: Which injuries or apparent property-damage total require immediate reporting to the nearest law enforcement agency?
sec13-card-sec13-F37.teaching_text: Notice North Carolina's dollar threshold: one thousand dollars in total apparent damage makes immediate police notice mandatory.

sec13-card-sec13-F38.question_text: What two penalties can follow if you fail to report a legally reportable crash?
sec13-card-sec13-F38.teaching_text: Walking away without notifying police on a reportable wreck exposes you to criminal prosecution and license suspension.

sec13-card-sec13-F39.question_text: Beyond police, whom should you notify after any crash, and what DMV paperwork can follow?
sec13-card-sec13-F39.teaching_text: Alerting your carrier early protects your coverage and prepares you if DMV requests liability proof forms.

sec13-card-sec13-R10.question_text: How does the threshold for mandatory police reporting differ from notifying your insurance company?
sec13-card-sec13-R10.teaching_text: Police notice kicks in for injury, death, or thousand-dollar damage, whereas your insurer should hear about every crash.

sec13-card-sec13-F40.question_text: Which five pieces of driver, vehicle, and coverage information must be exchanged at a crash?
sec13-card-sec13-F40.teaching_text: Forgetting registration numbers or insurance names at the roadside stalls claims and violates exchange duties.

sec13-card-sec13-F41.question_text: What must you do if you cannot identify the other occupants or the owner of damaged property?
sec13-card-sec13-F41.teaching_text: Recording every available fact and delivering it to the nearest officer satisfies your legal duty when owners aren't there.

sec14-card-sec14-F01.question_text: Which two roadway locations use traffic signals to control both drivers and pedestrians?
sec14-card-sec14-F01.teaching_text: Drivers scanning only street corners can miss overhead lights protecting walkers halfway down a busy block.

sec14-card-sec14-F02.question_text: What movements does a circular green light allow, and who gets the right of way when you turn?
sec14-card-sec14-F02.teaching_text: A round green ball never clears your turn path—oncoming cars and crossing walkers still go first.

sec14-card-sec14-F03.question_text: What does a steady circular yellow light warn, and how should you decide whether to stop?
sec14-card-sec14-F03.teaching_text: Brake smoothly whenever stopping distance allows, continuing cautiously only when slamming brakes right at the line is unsafe.

sec14-card-sec14-F04.question_text: Why must you never press the gas to beat a yellow light before red appears?
sec14-card-sec14-F04.teaching_text: Accelerating late into changing intersections causes high-speed T-bone crashes with cross traffic or left turners.

sec14-card-sec14-F05.question_text: Under what two conditions may you turn right at a steady circular red light?
sec14-card-sec14-F05.teaching_text: Rolling past the line without stopping completely or ignoring a posted prohibition triggers an instant red-light ticket.

sec14-card-sec14-F06.question_text: Whom must you yield to after stopping before making a permitted right turn on red?
sec14-card-sec14-F06.teaching_text: Staring left for approaching cars makes drivers overlook pedestrians stepping off the right-hand curb directly ahead.

sec14-card-sec14-F07.question_text: What fine range applies if you fail to yield to a pedestrian while turning right on red?
sec14-card-sec14-F07.teaching_text: North Carolina backs crosswalk protection on right-on-red turns with a steep hundred-to-five-hundred-dollar fine.

sec14-card-sec14-F08.question_text: What type of movement does a lit green arrow grant in the direction it points?
sec14-card-sec14-F08.teaching_text: Conflicting streams are held by red lights, though entering carefully still guards against stragglers clearing the box.

sec14-card-sec14-R01.question_text: How does turning on a circular green differ from turning on a green arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-R01.teaching_text: Confusing a solid round green for a green arrow causes classic left-turn crashes into oncoming traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F09.question_text: Who must yield when a U-turn driver and an opposing right-turn driver both have green arrows?
sec14-card-sec14-F09.teaching_text: Both lanes aim for the same exit lane, and North Carolina puts the yield duty on the U-turning car.

sec14-card-sec14-F10.question_text: What must drivers turning in the direction of a steady red arrow do?
sec14-card-sec14-F10.teaching_text: Unlike a round red light, a red arrow forbids turning in its direction until the display changes.

sec14-card-sec14-R03.question_text: How does a steady circular red differ from a steady red arrow when you want to turn?
sec14-card-sec14-R03.teaching_text: Making a right-on-red against a lit red right arrow is an easy trap that earns a violation.

sec14-card-sec14-F11.question_text: What is ending when a yellow arrow lights up, and what three displays might follow it?
sec14-card-sec14-F11.teaching_text: Protected right of way is expiring, shifting next to a round green, round red, or red arrow.

sec14-card-sec14-R02.question_text: How does the meaning of a circular yellow light differ from a yellow arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-R02.teaching_text: Round yellow precedes a full red stop, whereas a yellow arrow may transition into an unprotected round green.

sec14-card-sec14-F12.question_text: On a combined arrow-and-circle signal head, what controls turning cars when no arrow is lit?
sec14-card-sec14-F12.teaching_text: Once the arrow lamp goes dark, turning drivers obey the circular lens and must yield on round green.

sec14-card-sec14-F13.question_text: When both arrows and circular lights shine together on a signal, which controls turns and which controls straight traffic?
sec14-card-sec14-F13.teaching_text: Reading the lens matched to your lane movement keeps you from running a red turn arrow on green through.

sec14-card-sec14-F14.question_text: How must you treat an intersection when its traffic light is completely dark or malfunctioning?
sec14-card-sec14-F14.teaching_text: Blowing through a dead intersection during a storm outage causes severe broadside crashes when cross drivers assume right-of-way.

sec14-card-sec14-F15.question_text: When does the all-way-stop rule NOT apply at a broken or dark traffic light?
sec14-card-sec14-F15.teaching_text: Stopping on your own when an officer waves your lane forward creates confusion and gridlock.

sec14-card-sec14-R06.question_text: What is the default rule at a dark traffic light, and what two situations override it?
sec14-card-sec14-R06.teaching_text: Default to four-way stop etiquette unless a live traffic director or backup control device is actively running.

sec14-card-sec14-F16.question_text: Which roadside control matches a flashing red light, and when may you enter?
sec14-card-sec14-F16.teaching_text: Make a full stop first and stay put until entering will not interfere with cross traffic.

sec14-card-sec14-F17.question_text: Which roadside control matches a flashing yellow light, and how should you drive through it?
sec14-card-sec14-F17.teaching_text: Cross traffic typically faces a stop or flashing red, yet slowing down guards against anyone pulling out misjudged.

sec14-card-sec14-R04.question_text: How does your duty at a flashing red light compare with your duty at a flashing yellow light?
sec14-card-sec14-R04.teaching_text: Stopping unnecessarily under flashing yellow invites rear-enders, while rolling flashing red causes intersection T-bones.

sec14-card-sec14-F18.question_text: What does a flashing yellow arrow allow, and what must you do before completing the turn?
sec14-card-sec14-F18.teaching_text: Oncoming lanes still have green, so wait for a safe gap and clear crosswalks before turning.

sec14-card-sec14-F19.question_text: On a flashing-yellow-arrow head, what do the solid red arrow and solid yellow arrow tell you?
sec14-card-sec14-F19.teaching_text: Once the arrow turns solid yellow, your turn window is closing and a solid red stop arrow comes next.

sec14-card-sec14-R05.question_text: How does a flashing yellow arrow differ from a solid yellow arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-R05.teaching_text: Flashing yellow invites a yielded turn, while solid yellow warns that turning permission is ending.

sec14-card-sec14-F20.question_text: What does a solid green arrow allow on a flashing-yellow-arrow signal head?
sec14-card-sec14-F20.teaching_text: Opposing traffic and crosswalks are held so you can turn without yielding, while still scanning attentively.

sec14-card-sec14-F21.question_text: What display may a right-turn signal head show at the top instead of a red arrow?
sec14-card-sec14-F21.teaching_text: Using a steady circular red rather than a red arrow allows legal right-on-red turns after stopping when unsigned.

sec14-card-sec14-F22.question_text: What stream of traffic does a freeway ramp meter regulate?
sec14-card-sec14-F22.teaching_text: Spacing incoming cars one by one breaks up platoons so highway merging stays smooth.

sec14-card-sec14-F23.question_text: What do steady red and steady green mean when you pull up to a ramp meter?
sec14-card-sec14-F23.teaching_text: Hold at the ramp line on red, then accelerate smoothly down the ramp to merge once green lights.

sec14-card-sec14-F24.question_text: What should you do when an entrance ramp meter is dark with neither red nor green lit?
sec14-card-sec14-F24.teaching_text: Ramp meters often switch off outside rush hour, so stopping at an unlit ramp meter risks getting rear-ended.

sec14-card-sec14-R07.question_text: How does your response to a red ramp meter differ from a dark ramp meter?
sec14-card-sec14-R07.teaching_text: Unlike intersection outages that become four-way stops, a dark freeway ramp meter simply means merge without stopping.

sec14-card-sec14-F25.question_text: Where are hybrid beacons installed, and how do they look before someone triggers them?
sec14-card-sec14-F25.teaching_text: Expect unlit overhead beacons at mid-block walkways and firehouse driveways to wake up suddenly on button press.

sec14-card-sec14-F26.question_text: In what three-step light sequence does a hybrid beacon wake up once activated?
sec14-card-sec14-F26.teaching_text: Two yellow stages alert approaching drivers smoothly before the solid red stop indication locks in.

sec14-card-sec14-F27.question_text: What must drivers do while a hybrid beacon displays steady red?
sec14-card-sec14-F27.teaching_text: Remain completely stopped while walkers cross the roadway or emergency rigs roll out of their bay.

sec14-card-sec14-F28.question_text: When may you drive through a hybrid beacon after it switches from steady red to flashing red?
sec14-card-sec14-F28.teaching_text: Once walkers or emergency trucks finish clearing your path, treat the alternating flashing red like a stop sign.

sec14-card-sec14-R08.question_text: At a hybrid beacon, how does steady red differ from flashing red?
sec14-card-sec14-R08.teaching_text: Never creep through steady red even if the walkway looks empty; rolling resumes only on clear flashing red.

sec14-card-sec14-F29.question_text: What display does a hybrid beacon return to once its crossing cycle finishes?
sec14-card-sec14-F29.teaching_text: Unlike standard traffic lights, a resting dark hybrid beacon lets normal traffic flow without stopping.

sec14-card-sec14-R09.question_text: How do a hybrid beacon's warning stages differ from the colors shown on a ramp meter?
sec14-card-sec14-R09.teaching_text: Mainline roadway speeds need flashing and steady yellow warnings, whereas low-speed ramp meters toggle straight between red and green.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.question_text: For vehicles built since nineteen fifty-five, what lamp colors and daylight visibility distance apply to brake and turn lights?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.teaching_text: Bright daytime sunlight washes out weak bulbs, so brake and turn lamps must read clearly a hundred feet back.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.question_text: Must brake and turn-signal lamps sit inside the taillight housing, or may they be mounted separately?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.teaching_text: North Carolina inspects whether the lamps shine clearly on cue rather than forcing one specific lens layout.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.question_text: Can you pair North Carolina's daylight visibility distance with the mounting rule for brake and turn lamps?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.teaching_text: Whether integrated into taillights or housed alone, every brake and turn signal needs full hundred-foot daytime reach.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.question_text: Why is keeping signal lenses clean and bulbs working critical once daylight fades?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.teaching_text: Road grime dims electric bulbs right when darkness makes driver arm signals nearly invisible to trailing traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.question_text: When should you adjust your mirrors, and what exact view should the inside and side mirrors frame?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.teaching_text: Framing straight behind inside while barely grazing your own rear fenders outside pushes side coverage wider toward adjacent lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.question_text: Which three core capabilities must the brakes provide on any motor vehicle driven on public roads?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.teaching_text: Slowing down in motion means little if weak parking hardware lets the car roll away on a steep grade.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.question_text: How many independent ways of applying the brakes should well-maintained factory brake systems provide?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.teaching_text: Keeping a separate mechanical parking or emergency system gives you backup stopping power if hydraulic pressure fails.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.question_text: Under full foot pressure, how high above the floorboard must a healthy brake pedal remain?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.teaching_text: Dropping closer than one-third from the carpet leaves almost zero reserve travel during a hard panic stop.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.question_text: What mechanical trouble does a slowly sinking brake pedal point to, and what should you do about brake squeaks?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.teaching_text: A pedal creeping downward under steady foot pressure warns of internal fluid leaks before complete brake loss strikes.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.question_text: Which three emergency-braking advantages do anti-lock brakes help deliver?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.teaching_text: Preventing wheel lockup keeps front tires rolling so you can steer around hazards instead of skidding straight into them.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.question_text: What foot technique maximizes anti-lock braking, and what habit weakens it?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.teaching_text: Letting up or pumping overrides the computer's rapid valve pulses just when you need maximum controlled grip.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.question_text: Why is pumping the brake pedal the exact wrong instinct in an ABS-equipped car?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.teaching_text: Old-school pedal pumping belonged to non-ABS cars, whereas lifting off an ABS pedal interrupts automated anti-skid modulation.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.question_text: What simple step should you take every time you walk away from an unattended vehicle to prevent theft?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.teaching_text: Even a thirty-second convenience-store dash invites opportunistic joyriders when keys stay dangling in the column.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.question_text: Which structural defects or minimum tread measurement make a tire legally unsafe in North Carolina?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.teaching_text: Visible fabric plies, separating rubber chunks, or bald grooves shallower than one-sixteenth inch fail inspection and invite blowouts.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.question_text: What specific damage or grip problems come from under-inflated tires compared with over-inflated tires?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.teaching_text: Flexing soft sidewalls builds blowout heat, while ballooned over-inflated centers shrink the contact patch and wear down the middle.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.question_text: How do tire failure modes flip when air pressure drops too low versus climbs too high?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.teaching_text: Exam questions pair blowout heat with low pressure and slippery center-strip wear with excess pressure.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.question_text: Can you match North Carolina's legal fraction for minimum tire tread with the fraction for brake-pedal height?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.teaching_text: Keep tiny tread fractions separate from tall pedal fractions so inspection questions never trip you up.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.question_text: How often and under what tire-temperature condition should you check tire pressure against manufacturer specs?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.teaching_text: Highway friction heats trapped air and skews gauge readings upward, so cold morning checks match factory door-jamb numbers.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.question_text: Which vehicles are legally allowed to mount emergency lights or sirens in North Carolina?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.teaching_text: Restricting sirens and emergency beacons to official responders keeps right-of-way authority unmistakable in traffic.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.question_text: From how far away must a licensed vehicle's horn be audible, and what tone quality is forbidden?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.teaching_text: A legal horn must carry two hundred feet down the road without blasting an unreasonably loud or startling racket.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.question_text: Under what circumstance should you tap your horn, and how promptly must a dead horn be repaired?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.teaching_text: Saving the horn strictly for genuine safety alerts keeps its warning sharp, and broken horns leave you voiceless in blind spots.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.question_text: What floor and ceiling apply simultaneously to a legal vehicle horn in North Carolina?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.teaching_text: Your horn fails the statute if it is too weak to reach two hundred feet or modified to shriek harshly.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.question_text: What two emissions or sound outputs does a required working muffler hold down?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.teaching_text: Driving with a rusted-out or bypassed muffler fills lanes with deafening exhaust roar and visible fumes.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.question_text: What deadly hazard comes from an exhaust leak, and what simple window habit does the handbook recommend?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.teaching_text: Odorless carbon monoxide brings drowsiness, blackout, and death before you smell danger, so cracking glass one inch brings fresh air.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.question_text: Which three body-motion symptoms warn of bad suspension that could trigger a loss of control?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.teaching_text: Worn shocks and struts let tires hop off rough pavement during curves or emergency swerves, demanding immediate repair.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.question_text: Which bulbs blink when emergency flashers activate, and who may switch them on?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.teaching_text: Flashing every corner signal at once lets any everyday driver mark a roadside breakdown or sudden hazard ahead.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.question_text: Who may use four-way hazard flashers compared with emergency beacons and sirens?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.teaching_text: Four-way flashers warn of a stopped civilian hazard, whereas sirens and emergency strobes belong strictly to police and rescue.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.question_text: Roughly how much extra per gallon can fuel cost climb for every five miles per hour driven above sixty?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.teaching_text: Wind drag rises sharply past sixty miles per hour, burning noticeably more gas on every highway trip.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.question_text: By up to what percentage can aggressive starts and hard braking raise fuel consumption?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.teaching_text: Flooring the throttle only to slam the brakes converts expensive gasoline straight into wasted brake-pad heat.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.question_text: When should you shut off a waiting engine, and where is the speed crossover between open windows and air conditioning?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.teaching_text: Open windows create aerodynamic drag above forty miles per hour that costs more fuel than running air conditioning.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.question_text: How much fuel economy or gasoline can a dirty air filter and a loose gas cap cost you?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.teaching_text: Choked intake air cuts efficiency about ten percent while unsealed filler necks let thirty gallons evaporate yearly.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.question_text: How many seconds—and roughly what urban distance—ahead should defensive drivers scan?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.teaching_text: Reading traffic a full city block early eliminates panic braking and sudden last-second swerves.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.question_text: About how often should you flick your eyes across the mirrors to catch tailgaters?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.teaching_text: Brief split-second checks track closing traffic behind you without starving your forward view.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.question_text: How does your forward scanning lead-time compare with how often you check your mirrors?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.teaching_text: Keep those two ten-based habits distinct—scanning ten to fifteen seconds downrange while checking mirrors every ten seconds.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.question_text: During which four driving situations should you check behind your vehicle and scan blind spots?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.teaching_text: Long downhill grades bring heavy fast-closing trucks from behind just as surely as lane shifts, braking, or reversing.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.question_text: Where do vehicle blind spots sit, and how must you verify they are empty before moving sideways?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.teaching_text: Glass reflections miss adjacent cars tucked beside your rear quarters until a quick shoulder turn checks the lane directly.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.question_text: Why are properly aimed mirrors still not enough by themselves right before changing lanes?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.teaching_text: Relying on mirrors alone misses cars riding next to your rear quarter panels during lateral moves.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.question_text: When parked cars, bushes, buildings, glare, or dirty glass hide cross traffic, how should you clear the corner?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.teaching_text: Creeping out inch by inch lets you peek past curbside obstructions before committing your hood into live lanes.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.question_text: Which five maneuvers call for signaling—even on a seemingly empty street—and what comes before signaling?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.teaching_text: Signaling warns unseen cyclists or pedestrians you missed, though a blinking bulb never grants priority before checking safety.

sec11-card-sec11-F32.question_text: Although electric turn signals legally replace hand signals, what sky condition can hide whether they are blinking?
sec11-card-sec11-F32.teaching_text: Direct sunrise or sunset glare reflecting off plastic housings makes flashing filaments nearly impossible for nearby drivers to distinguish.

sec11-card-sec11-F33.question_text: How far ahead must you signal normally versus when the speed limit is forty-five miles per hour or higher?
sec11-card-sec11-F33.teaching_text: Higher speeds eat up a hundred feet in barely a second, so North Carolina doubles warning distance starting at forty-five.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.question_text: At what posted speed limit does North Carolina's required turn-signal distance jump from one hundred to two hundred feet?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.teaching_text: Watch that exact forty-five cutoff on the permit test—not fifty or fifty-five—whenever picking your turn-signal distance.

sec11-card-sec11-F34.question_text: How do you position your left arm and fingers out the window to signal a left turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F34.teaching_text: Extending your arm horizontally points directly toward the lane or street you plan to enter.

sec11-card-sec11-F35.question_text: How do you hold your left forearm, hand, and palm to signal a right turn?
sec11-card-sec11-F35.teaching_text: Holding the palm flat forward creates a crisp upright silhouette trailing drivers recognize immediately.

sec11-card-sec11-F36.question_text: Which arm angle and palm direction tell drivers behind you that you are slowing or stopping?
sec11-card-sec11-F36.teaching_text: Facing your open palm rearward toward trailing bumpers reinforces a clear slow-down gesture when brake bulbs fail.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.question_text: Can you match straight out, forearm up, and pointed down to their three hand-signal meanings?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.teaching_text: Every hand signal uses the driver's left window, relying purely on elbow angle to separate all three maneuvers.
sec11-card-sec11-R10.must_match_memory_hook: Straight left, up right, down stop

visual_sync.text_span: Straight left, up right, down stop

sec11-card-sec11-F37.question_text: How should you clear a tailgater behind you, and where within your lane should you normally ride?
sec11-card-sec11-F37.teaching_text: Letting aggressive bumpers pass removes rear-end risk while riding centered keeps equal cushion on both sides.

sec11-card-sec11-F38.question_text: When trapped between two simultaneous hazards of unequal severity—like oncoming cars and a child on a bike—who gets wider margin?
sec11-card-sec11-F38.teaching_text: Unprotected riders wobble unpredictably and have zero crash steel around them, so cushion the child far wider than cars.

sec11-card-sec11-F39.question_text: How do you handle two equally serious hazards—such as parked cars on one side and oncoming traffic on the other?
sec11-card-sec11-F39.teaching_text: Eliminating one hazard completely by waiting turns a tight two-sided squeeze into an easy single-clearance pass.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.question_text: How does defensive strategy shift between two unequal dangers and two equally serious dangers?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.teaching_text: When you cannot stop out of unequal risks you favor the vulnerable party, whereas stopping splits equal risks apart.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: Is exceeding the posted speed limit inside a North Carolina highway work zone ever lawful?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Even when crews appear out of sight behind jersey barriers, posted work-zone speed caps carry full statutory force.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Where does a North Carolina highway work zone legally begin and end?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: Speed and penalty rules stay active all the way until you pass the final END ROAD WORK marker.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: When a sign at the start of a work zone lists a speeding penalty, how does it apply to your ticket?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Work-zone surcharges do not replace standard court fines—they stack directly on top of your underlying speeding conviction.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How do the start and end signs of a work zone relate to whether the extra speeding penalty applies?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Every work zone runs sign to sign, while the extra surcharge triggers specifically when an entry plaque posts it.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: What single road environment reserves orange signs with black lettering on the approach and inside?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Seeing black-on-orange diamonds instantly tells your brain temporary roadwork geometry and crews lie ahead.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: Who is stationed ahead when you pass a Flagger warning sign, and how should you prepare?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Crews in high-visibility orange vests flip STOP and SLOW paddles manually as heavy equipment crosses single lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: Why should you act promptly on black-on-orange advance lane-closure signs instead of waiting until the cones?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Advance signs sit far upstream so traffic blends smoothly before barricades pinch away shoulder room.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Why is driving noticeably slower than surrounding work-zone traffic a leading cause of rear-end crashes?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Concrete barriers and tight drums strip away shoulder escape routes when gawkers brake unexpectedly below flow speed.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: Which four physical devices or personnel guide vehicles safely through highway work zones?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Following the continuous line of orange drums, cones, barricades, and paddle flaggers keeps tires out of open trenches.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: During which clock window and visibility threshold does North Carolina law require headlights?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Memorize four hundred feet as North Carolina's daytime fog, smoke, or storm sightline trigger alongside sunset-to-sunrise darkness.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: Can North Carolina's headlight statute trigger in the middle of the afternoon—and at what exact distance?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Thick afternoon fog, dust, or downpours dropping visibility to four hundred feet or less mandate full headlights.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: What equipment switch must accompany your windshield wipers whenever bad weather hits in North Carolina?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Turning on full headlights—not merely daytime running lamps—lights your red taillights through heavy highway spray.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: When should you select low beams versus high beams during nighttime driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Streetlit town blocks call for low beams, while open country roads allow brights until oncoming or leading cars appear.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: Which three visibility and human factors make driving after dark riskier than daytime travel?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Shrinking sightlines collide with late-night fatigue, impaired motorists, and blinding opposing headlights.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: How should you respond if an approaching driver leaves high beams blazing in your face?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: One quick flash reminds forgetful drivers gently, whereas retaliating with brights leaves two blinded drivers closing fast.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: If your single high-beam reminder fails to make an oncoming car dim, why must your switch stay on low?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Flipping your own high beams back at them doubles head-on crash risk by blinding the only driver who could still see.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes—and how should you adjust speed—when oncoming headlights glare at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Tracking the white pavement edge keeps your lane position steady without burning out your night-adapted retinas.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: What rule caps how fast you may safely drive on a dark road at night?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Cruising faster than your stopping distance fits inside your headlight cone guarantees hitting dark obstacles before halting.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: Which lights go on and which switch off when you park beside a highway after dark?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Leaving full headlights burning on a shoulder disorients oncoming drivers or lures tired motorists straight into your bumper.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: What two in-car tools fight low sun glare, and what is your backup move if glare still blinds you?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: When horizon glare overwhelms tinted lenses and a flipped visor, waiting ten minutes off-road beats driving blind.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: Which two vehicle switches and what speed adjustment apply whenever rain falls?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Rain cuts tire friction and obscures mirrors simultaneously, requiring clear glass, lit lamps, and gentler pace.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: How many times farther can stopping take on slick pavement, and how much following distance should you leave?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Because wet or icy asphalt multiplies braking distance up to tenfold, doubling your dry following cushion is the bare minimum.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: How does North Carolina's slippery-road stopping multiplier connect to its wet following-distance rule?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Exam options love confusing two-to-ten-times stopping distance with at-least-double following distance, so lock each phrase cleanly.
sec12-card-sec12-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Up to tenfold stop, double gap

visual_sync.text_span: Up to tenfold stop, double gap

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: During which exact minutes of a rainfall are roads slickest, and what makes them so greasy?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Light early raindrops float weeks of dripped engine oil, rubber dust, and road grime before heavy downpours rinse asphalt.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: At minimum, how many miles per hour slower than dry conditions should you drive on wet pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Trimming five to ten miles per hour gives tire grooves time to channel water away beneath each footprint.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: Why must cruise control stay switched off both during and after rain?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: If tires float onto standing water, automated throttle keeps spinning wheels while you lose precious split-seconds canceling cruise.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: Once rain stops falling, why is re-engaging cruise control still dangerous on wet roads?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Runoff puddles linger across highway ruts after skies clear, where active cruise delays throttle lift during a sudden hydroplane.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: At how low a speed and in how thin a film of water can tires lift into a hydroplane?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Drivers assume hydroplaning takes freeway speeds, yet thirty miles per hour over barely an eighth-inch puddle floats rubber.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: What exact pedal and steering actions recover grip when your car begins hydroplaning?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Hitting the brakes locks floating wheels instantly, whereas easing off throttle smoothly lets speed drop until tread bites asphalt.
sec12-card-sec12-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Ease off gas, skip brakes, straight

visual_sync.text_span: Ease off gas, skip brakes, straight

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: Can you pair the onset speed and water depth of hydroplaning with the correct foot response?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: Even shallow puddles at city speeds float tires, and lifting smoothly off the gas without braking restores contact.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: How do tread depth and inflation pressure affect hydroplaning risk and skid control?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Open deep grooves pump water away while keeping pressure near the top of the maker's range sharpens skid stability.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: Which four visual, sound, or steering cues warn that standing water sits on the pavement?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Feeling steering suddenly go light alongside slushing spray and surface dimples tells you tires are nearing liftoff.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: How long after a storm ends can leftover roadside puddles still trigger hydroplaning?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Shaded dips and clogged storm drains trap deep wheel-rut pools long after sunshine dries surrounding lanes.

sec12-card-sec12-F27.question_text: Since nineteen seventy, what share of North Carolina tropical-weather deaths came from inland flooding—and how many involved flooded roads?
sec12-card-sec12-F27.teaching_text: Inland creeks and submerged roads kill far more storm victims than coastal wind, especially drivers bypassing flood warnings.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: Why must you never drive through standing water covering a roadway?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Murky floodwater hides collapsed culverts and missing asphalt where a seemingly shallow puddle drops three feet straight down.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: What depth of fast-moving water sweeps a car sideways, and what depth floats or rolls it?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Water barely reaching your lower tire sidewalls pushes tons of metal sideways before ankle-to-shin flow flips cabins.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: How do six inches and twelve inches of rushing floodwater differ in what they do to a passenger car?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Half a foot knocks tires sideways off the crown, and one full foot buoys the chassis until currents roll it.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: What full sequence of steps keeps you alive when fog grows so thick you can barely see?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Securing the car with flashers and exiting out the passenger door moves your body clear of blind highway drift.
sec12-card-sec12-F31.must_match_memory_hook: Pull far off, flashers, exit right

visual_sync.text_span: Pull far off, flashers, exit right

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: Which headlight beam, speed habit, and traffic checks apply when you must drive through lighter fog?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Low beams cut beneath mist glare while watching taillights ahead and mirrors behind guards against chain-reaction pileups.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: How does your fog game-plan switch between blinding zero-visibility fog and passable mist?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Knowing when to abandon the shoulder via the passenger door versus creeping on low beams prevents multi-car fog crashes.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: Which three roadway spots freeze over before regular ground-supported asphalt as temperatures drop?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Cold wind chills elevated bridge decks from both above and below while tree shade blocks warming winter sunlight.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: Besides running wipers and low beams in snow, how drastically should you cut speed on packed snow versus glare ice?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Packed snow steals more than half your grip, and mirror-smooth ice demands creeping at a bare walking crawl.

sec12-card-sec12-F35.question_text: How should you accelerate and test grip on snow or ice, including in a manual-transmission car?
sec12-card-sec12-F35.teaching_text: Starting a stick-shift in second gear with a slow clutch softens wheel torque so tires roll instead of spinning.

sec12-card-sec12-F36.question_text: How much extra stopping distance should you leave on snow or ice, and what slows the car best?
sec12-card-sec12-F36.teaching_text: Leaving three times normal space lets engine compression decelerate rolling tires gently without brake-pedal lockup.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: Why does North Carolina pair triple stopping distance on snow and ice with staying off the brake pedal?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Sharp brake pressure breaks fragile winter traction instantly, whereas early throttle lift uses engine drag smoothly.

sec12-card-sec12-F37.question_text: Do tire chains and snow tires let you start, stop, or steer briskly on packed snow and ice?
sec12-card-sec12-F37.teaching_text: Winter hardware adds extra bite for gentle climbs yet still skids sideways if you yank the wheel or stab brakes.

sec12-card-sec12-F38.question_text: What two driving habits cut down wildlife strikes, especially around twilight and night?
sec12-card-sec12-F38.teaching_text: Spotting glowing eyes along ditch lines early gives you extra yards to brake before deer bound onto pavement.

sec12-card-sec12-F39.question_text: How does hitting a deer at thirty-five miles per hour compare with striking one at fifty-five or faster?
sec12-card-sec12-F39.teaching_text: Kinetic crash energy more than doubles by fifty-five, turning a survivable thirty-five strike into a deadly windshield impact.

sec12-card-sec12-F40.question_text: During which daily hours and yearly seasons must drivers watch hardest for crossing animals?
sec12-card-sec12-F40.teaching_text: Twilight feeding hours combined with spring dispersal and autumn mating migrations put peak deer numbers across highways.

sec12-card-sec12-F41.question_text: When should you use high beams in animal country—and why switch them off when an animal stands ahead?
sec12-card-sec12-F41.teaching_text: Blinding high-beam glare stuns deer motionless right in the center of your travel lane instead of letting them bolt.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: Why must you drop out of high beams even with zero oncoming cars once an animal appears on the road?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Dipping to low beams breaks the hypnotic glare spell so the animal can clear the asphalt.

sec12-card-sec12-F42.question_text: Once a single deer darts across your lane, what should you immediately expect?
sec12-card-sec12-F42.teaching_text: Deer travel in family groups, so accelerating as soon as the lead animal clears walks straight into trailing fawns.

sec12-card-sec12-F43.question_text: How should you steer, brake, and warn if an animal steps directly into your roadway?
sec12-card-sec12-F43.teaching_text: Swerving off-road into trees or oncoming trucks kills far more drivers than braking straight in your own lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: Which two sides of your health shape how you drive, and what health standard does holding a driver license require?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Mental stress or physical illness both degrade judgment and steering control long before you realize your focus slipped.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: How can a short-term illness like a cold, headache, or flu affect you behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Dismissing a bad cold or pounding headache ignores how everyday symptoms dull alertness and stretch braking reaction times.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, how fast does a car cover a football field—making even a brief nod-off deadly?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: Closing your eyes for three point seven seconds at highway speed sends your car blind down an entire football field.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: How severe are drowsy-driving crashes typically, and where and under what cabin condition do they happen most often?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: High speeds with nobody awake beside you to spot lane drift make solo rural highway trips prime fatigue traps.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: What warning signs tell you that drowsiness is taking over while you drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Forgetting the last few miles or buzzing a shoulder rumble strip means microsleeps are already threatening your lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: What should you do when you grow tired behind the wheel, and how much does a short nap with caffeine help?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Fifteen to forty-five minutes of sleep plus coffee buys only short-term alertness rather than replacing real rest.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: How often should you stop on a long road trip, and what should you do during each break?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Getting out to stretch and walk briskly every two hours restores circulation before highway hypnosis sets in.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: What daily mileage ceiling and medication precaution does the handbook recommend for road trips?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Pushing past four hundred miles in a single day—or taking drowsy medication—stacks heavy fatigue onto late-day highway hours.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: How does the emergency nap-and-caffeine tactic differ from the standard long-trip break rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Treat naps and coffee as short-lived emergency patches while scheduling brisk walking stops every two hours from the start.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: How does the North Carolina handbook define distracted driving?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Even legal cabin habits count as distracted driving the moment they steal attention from scanning and steering.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: Beyond texting and phone calls, what everyday cabin activities does the handbook list as common driving distractions?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Unwrapping food, checking navigation screens, or adjusting audio knobs pulls eyes off traffic just as fast as a phone.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: How does distraction hurt your reaction speed and hazard detection on the road?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Looking away for a beat makes you late spotting brake lights, side-street pullouts, crossing walkers, or road debris.
