sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: What physical control problem makes many distractions especially dangerous during a sudden emergency?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Holding a drink or phone leaves one hand on the rim when evasive steering demands firm two-handed control.

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Under what narrow circumstances—and timing—does the handbook advise using a phone on a trip?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Saving phone contact for emergencies or reaching a parent, guardian, or spouse—at a safe spot—protects your road margin.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: What three practical phone habits does the handbook recommend before and during a drive?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Letting passengers dial, sending rings to voicemail, and stowing loose phones stops cabin distractions and flying crash projectiles.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: Which cell-phone actions are illegal for every driver on North Carolina streets, highways, and public vehicular areas?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Parking lots and public vehicular areas carry the exact same ban on typing texts or emails as open highways.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: What cell-phone rule applies to a driver under eighteen while the vehicle is moving, and what is the lone exception?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Hands-free speakerphone or parent calls still break teen law while moving—only calling nine one one is permitted.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How does North Carolina's cell-phone ban for all drivers differ from the stricter ban for drivers under eighteen?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Test questions trap teens with parent-call answers that are legal for adults yet banned under eighteen while rolling.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: What mobile-device rule applies to anyone operating a school bus on a public road or vehicular area?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Carrying dozens of student passengers leaves zero room for cell-phone or mobile-device use behind a school-bus wheel.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How do the texting and under-eighteen phone rules differ legally from the handbook's family-call advice?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Do not confuse general handbook safety tips about limiting family calls with the statutory bans on texting and teen phone use.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: Which categories of medicine can impair driving, and what two precautions should you take when using them?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Store-shelf allergy or cold tablets can sedate you just like prescriptions, so learn your reaction and limit trips.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Roughly what percentage of all traffic deaths involve alcohol, according to the North Carolina handbook?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Nearly two out of every five fatal crashes trace back to alcohol impairment on the road.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: What category of drug is alcohol, and how does it change brain speed behind the wheel?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: People mistake an early social buzz for stimulation when alcohol actually depresses central nervous processing.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: How does alcohol distort a driver's sense of speed, distance, and personal risk?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Misjudging gaps while feeling invincible is the exact combination that pushes impaired drivers into high-speed gambles.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: Why do impaired drivers often miss signals, side-street cars, or walkers while concentrating on steering—and what else suffers?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Safe driving demands juggling lane tracking and hazard scanning together, yet alcohol narrows focus to one chore while causing drowsiness.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: What is the single thing that sobers up a drinker—and which three popular remedies fail?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Hot coffee, heavy food, or a cold shower only leaves you wide-awake and wet while your blood alcohol stays high.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: Why will drinking coffee, eating a large meal, or taking a cold shower never make an impaired person safe to drive?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Your liver metabolizes alcohol on a fixed clock that no meal, shower, or espresso shot can speed up.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: What practical alternatives does the handbook suggest so nobody ever drinks and drives?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Locking in a sober driver, transit, shared cab, or overnight stay before the first drink removes impaired temptation.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: Across a typical driving lifetime, what are the approximate odds of suffering serious injury or death in a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: One-in-three lifetime odds prove serious crashes are a realistic risk for everyday drivers, never just rare bad luck.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Who must wear a properly fastened seat belt whenever a belt-equipped vehicle moves forward on a North Carolina road?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: Rear-seat adult riders are covered just like front-seat occupants the moment the vehicle rolls forward.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: How do air bags or automatic shoulder harnesses affect your legal duty to fasten seat belts and lap belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Automatic shoulder straps without a fastened lap belt let occupants submarine forward under crash forces.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: Why is riding unbuckled illegal even when your car features both air bags and motorized shoulder harnesses?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Exam questions test that supplemental airbags and motorized chest straps never replace fastening the manual lap belt.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: When does a medical, physical, or psychological condition exempt someone from North Carolina's seat-belt mandate?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Personal discomfort never excuses an unbuckled noncommercial rider unless a real medical barrier or certified phobia prevents restraint.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: Which two groups of on-duty delivery carriers are exempted from wearing seat belts along their routes?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Constant mailbox-to-mailbox stops exempt on-duty rural postal carriers and route newspaper deliverers while actively delivering.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Under what speed ceiling are frequent-stop delivery drivers or passengers exempt from fastening seat belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Once a delivery van accelerates past twenty miles per hour between stops, everyone inside must click their belt.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: What exact speed limit keeps the frequent-delivery seat-belt exemption legal between stops?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Exceeding twenty miles per hour even briefly between delivery drops cancels the belt exemption immediately.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: Which three farming, vehicle-equipment, or full-seating situations are exempt from the North Carolina seat-belt law?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Remember all three narrow carve-outs covering in-state farm cargo trucks, vintage cars exempt from belts, and cabins once every belted spot is occupied.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: Who can ride unbuckled in a motor home, and what living-facility count must that motor home meet?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Drivers and front passengers in an RV must always buckle up even when rear living quarters meet the four-facility test.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: Out of every ten children killed while riding unrestrained, how many could properly used safety seats save?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Properly harnessed child restraints prevent seventy percent of fatalities among unrestrained young crash victims.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: What defines the best child safety seat, and where can families find affordable rental programs?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Local health departments, hospitals, and community groups rent proper seats cheaply so cost never leaves a child unbuckled.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: Up to what passenger age is the driver legally responsible for securing young riders in federally compliant restraints or belts?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: When an unbuckled fifteen-year-old rides in your car, the two-point citation and responsibility land directly on you as driver.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: Which age and weight combination requires a child to ride in a weight-appropriate child passenger restraint?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Until a child reaches either age eight or eighty pounds, an adult belt alone does not replace a weight-matched restraint.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: When a vehicle has an active front passenger airbag and a rear seat, which children must ride in back?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Front airbag blast forces endanger small frames unless the restraint is specifically engineered for front-airbag use.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How do the age-and-weight thresholds differ between the child-restraint rule and the front-airbag rear-seat rule?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Pair eight with eighty for child restraints and five with forty for keeping small kids behind active front airbags.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: When may a child under eight weighing forty to eighty pounds be secured with a properly fitted lap belt alone?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: Only when every available seating position lacks a lap-and-shoulder combo for the booster may forty-to-eighty-pound kids use lap-only.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: What seating condition must be true before a forty-to-eighty-pound child under eight may legally use a lap belt alone?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: If even one open seat offers a shoulder-and-lap belt for the restraint, choosing lap-only breaks the rule.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: How long should children stay in a booster seat after outgrowing harnessed seats, and how must an adult belt fit?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Moving out of a booster too early lets the lap strap ride onto soft stomach organs and the chest strap cut the throat.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: At up to what speed does an airbag burst from the dashboard during a crash?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: Inflating faster than an eyeblink at two hundred miles per hour hits hard if an occupant sits too close.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.question_text: Where does the handbook say children aged twelve and younger should ride?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.teaching_text: Keeping kids twelve and under buckled in the back row shields developing bones from front-seat airbag impact.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.question_text: Where must an infant in a rear-facing safety seat never be placed?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.teaching_text: A rear-facing shell rests inches from the dash where an inflating airbag strikes the back of the infant's head.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.question_text: Where across your body should the lap belt and shoulder belt rest to work safely alongside airbags?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.teaching_text: Anchoring straps across strong pelvic and chest bones prevents internal organ injury during sudden deceleration.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.question_text: How should the driver and front passenger seats be positioned relative to the dashboard, especially for shorter riders?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.teaching_text: Maximizing space from the steering wheel and dash gives front airbags room to inflate before cushioning you.

sec06-card-sec06-F45.question_text: Who must wear a safety helmet on a motorcycle or moped, and which federal standard must that helmet meet?
sec06-card-sec06-F45.teaching_text: Both operators and passengers on motorcycles and mopeds need certified impact protection under Federal Standard two hundred eighteen.

sec06-card-sec06-F46.question_text: What liner feature and manufacturer marking identify a compliant motorcycle helmet—and what about aftermarket stickers?
sec06-card-sec06-F46.teaching_text: Novelty shells with slap-on decals crush on impact because they lack the one-inch polystyrene core and permanent factory mark.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: Why does slapping a separately purchased DOT sticker onto a helmet fail to make it legal?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Only a permanent DOT emblem applied by the helmet manufacturer certifies tested crash protection.

sec06-card-sec06-F47.question_text: Which age group is barred from riding in the open cargo bed of a pickup truck, and who bears responsibility?
sec06-card-sec06-F47.teaching_text: Open cargo beds have zero belts or rollover protection, and the pickup driver gets cited unless a statutory exemption applies.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: How does the age guideline for riding in a car's rear seat compare with the age ban for open pickup beds?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Exam questions mix those two ages up since back-row seating at twelve is safety advice while open-bed riding under sixteen is illegal.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Which four situations exempt children from North Carolina's ban on riding in an open pickup bed?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Outside farm duties, parades, emergencies, or an adult riding in the cargo bed, kids belong belted inside the cab.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: What fine and record impact come with violating the child pickup-bed rule?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: DMV distractors love adding court costs or insurance hikes, yet this infraction carries only a flat twenty-five-dollar fine.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: How much hotter than outside air can a sunny parked car climb, even with a window cracked?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Cracking a window barely slows cabin heat buildup, turning a parked vehicle into a fatal heatstroke trap for kids or pets.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: Why is warming up a car dangerous when snow blocks the tailpipe?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Blocked exhaust forces odorless, invisible, tasteless carbon monoxide straight into the cabin before anyone realizes danger.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: Who holds the right of way in marked or unmarked crosswalks where no traffic signals exist?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Even without painted stripes, extending sidewalk lines across an unsignaled corner creates a legal crosswalk where drivers yield.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: Which lights govern pedestrians at signalized intersections without dedicated walk signals, and when shouldn't they start?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Stepping off the curb on yellow or red leaves walkers stranded mid-street just as cross traffic gets green.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: Who has the right of way when a pedestrian crosses on green and a vehicle turns across that path?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: A green ball lets you turn only after clearing pedestrians crossing lawfully on that same green phase.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: How does a pedestrian's right to cross on green contrast with starting across on yellow or red?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Green grants walkers priority even over turning traffic, whereas yellow and red forbid starting off the curb.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: How must drivers act when a signal shifts to yellow or red with someone still mid-crosswalk?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: A fresh green light never gives permission to crowd or cut off someone still clearing the street.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: Which three mobility cues give a blind pedestrian special legal protection at an unsignaled intersection?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Spot an extended white cane, red-tipped cane, or guide dog and give full priority without honking impatiently.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Which signal rules pedestrians where Walk and Don't Walk lights operate, and what does Walk grant?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: Active pedestrian heads replace standard traffic balls for foot traffic, giving Walk crossers full green-light priority.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: When both regular traffic lights and Walk or Don't Walk signals are working, which governs pedestrians?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Dedicated pedestrian signals time safe crossing windows around turn arrows, so walkers follow them over green vehicle balls.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: How should you respond if you have a green light and a pedestrian steps out against red?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Alerting an inattentive pedestrian with your horn gives them a split second to freeze or step back safely.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: When must you sound your horn around pedestrians, and what if a walker keeps moving without right of way?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Having legal right of way never excuses hitting someone on foot; warn first and stop if they continue.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: What is the maximum legal speed for a regular North Carolina school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Expect yellow route buses to travel slower than highway traffic because state law caps them at forty-five.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: During which morning and afternoon time windows does the handbook urge extra caution for school buses?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Kids darting toward stops peak during morning pickup and afternoon drop-off windows across residential streets.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: What triggers a mandatory school-bus stop, and which three things must happen before you drive again?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Rolling forward the instant red lights blink off risks hitting a late-crossing child before the bus pulls away.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: May you proceed once children finish crossing in front of a stopped school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Test traps bait you into moving once kids reach the sidewalk, yet you must wait until the bus moves.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: Which directions of traffic must stop when a school bus halts for passengers on a two-lane road?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Children routinely cross both lanes of an undivided two-lane street right in front of the yellow bus.

sec07-card-sec07-F25.question_text: Who must stop for a school bus on a two-lane road that has a center turning lane?
sec07-card-sec07-F25.teaching_text: A painted center turn lane on a two-lane street does not count as a wide four-lane buffer.

sec07-card-sec07-F26.question_text: Who must stop for a school bus on a four-lane road that has no median separation?
sec07-card-sec07-F26.teaching_text: Without a center median or turn lane separating four lanes, oncoming drivers still must stop for the bus.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: On a highway having at least four travel lanes plus a center turn lane, who stops for a school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Five-lane corridors never send students walking across opposing lanes, so only drivers trailing the bus stop.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: When a median divides a highway with at least four lanes, which drivers stop for a school bus?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Physical median separation shields oncoming lanes from crossing students, requiring only traffic behind the bus to stop.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: Which multi-lane or turn-lane road setups stop both directions for a school bus versus following traffic only?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Two-lane center-turn and undivided four-lane roads stop everyone, whereas medians or four-plus lanes with turn lanes free oncoming cars.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: Which four emergency vehicle types always hold right of way when running flashing lights and sirens?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Seconds matter on emergency runs, so active lights and sirens override ordinary intersection and lane priority.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: How should you respond when an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches from ahead or behind?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: Stopping dead in a middle lane blocks responders; move smoothly to the right edge and stay stopped.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: Which drivers are exempt from pulling over and stopping for an approaching emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Only oncoming traffic across a center median on a four-lane limited-access highway may keep moving.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: On undivided or ordinary roads do both directions yield to emergency vehicles, and what is the lone exception?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Unless a center median divides a four-lane limited-access highway, oncoming traffic pulls right and stops too.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: How close to a responder vehicle halted at a wreck or roadside scene is parking forbidden?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: Sightseers parking close to a wreck choke ambulance access and create secondary collision hazards.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: How far back must you stay from fire trucks answering an alarm, and what must you never cross?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Driving over a pressurized fire hose can burst the line and cut water to firefighters inside a blaze.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: How does the crash-scene parking buffer compare with the distance kept from fire trucks answering an alarm?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Exam choices swap these two numbers constantly—pair one hundred feet with crash parking and one block with fire alarms.

sec07-card-sec07-F27.question_text: What does the move-over law require on a multi-lane road when a lit emergency or service rig sits within twelve feet?
sec07-card-sec07-F27.teaching_text: Giving roadside officers, tow operators, and medics an empty buffer lane prevents deadly highway sideswipes.

sec07-card-sec07-F28.question_text: What does the move-over law require when you have only one lane in your direction past a stopped emergency vehicle?
sec07-card-sec07-F28.teaching_text: When you cannot legally change lanes away from flashing roadside lights, drop to a reduced, controlled speed until past.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: How does your move-over duty change between two-plus lanes and a single lane in your direction?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Multi-lane drivers vacate the adjacent lane completely, while single-lane drivers slow down until clear of the emergency scene.

sec07-card-sec07-F29.question_text: What three immediate steps should you take when police lights or a siren come on behind your car?
sec07-card-sec07-F29.teaching_text: Blinking right and pulling smoothly onto the closest safe shoulder shows predictable, cooperative compliance.

sec07-card-sec07-F30.question_text: How do you acknowledge an officer behind you when there is no safe place to pull over right away?
sec07-card-sec07-F30.teaching_text: Four-way flashers and dropping roughly ten miles per hour tell the officer you are seeking a safe turnout, not fleeing.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: Should you stop directly inside an active travel lane if police signal you where no shoulder exists?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Halting inside a live traffic lane risks a high-speed rear-end crash; use flashers, slow ten, and reach a safe spot.

sec07-card-sec07-F31.question_text: What may you do before pulling over if you genuinely doubt whether an unmarked vehicle is real law enforcement?
sec07-card-sec07-F31.teaching_text: Dispatchers can instantly verify whether an actual officer is behind you while you proceed carefully toward a safe spot.

sec07-card-sec07-F32.question_text: Once pulled over for police, what do you do with gear, window, engine, electronics, and seat belts?
sec07-card-sec07-F32.teaching_text: Unbuckling early looks like reaching or exiting, so stay belted in Park with audio silenced until the officer speaks.

sec07-card-sec07-F33.question_text: Where should the driver, front passenger, and back-seat passengers keep their hands during a traffic stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F33.teaching_text: Visible hands on the wheel and front seatbacks reassure approaching officers that nobody is reaching into hidden spots.

sec07-card-sec07-F34.question_text: What does North Carolina law require you to give at a stop, and what about further questioning?
sec07-card-sec07-F34.teaching_text: Identifying yourself and handing over license and registration are mandatory, while answering extra questions afterward remains your choice.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: How does your legal duty to show license and registration compare with answering additional officer questions?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Withholding your identity or registration violates state law, whereas declining further investigative questions after that is lawful.

sec07-card-sec07-F35.question_text: How must weapons be stored without a permit, and what must a concealed-carry permit holder tell the officer?
sec07-card-sec07-F35.teaching_text: Never reach near any weapon, and concealed-permit holders must proactively inform the approaching officer that a weapon is aboard.

sec07-card-sec07-F36.question_text: During a traffic stop, when may occupants exit the car or search under seats and in the glove box?
sec07-card-sec07-F36.teaching_text: Jumping out uninvited or rummaging under seats before the officer arrives looks dangerous from outside the vehicle.

sec07-card-sec07-F37.question_text: Does signing a North Carolina traffic citation admit guilt, and where do you contest it?
sec07-card-sec07-F37.teaching_text: Your roadside signature only acknowledges receiving the citation, saving legal arguments for the courtroom.

sec07-card-sec07-F38.question_text: What charge grade applies if someone resists, delays, or obstructs law enforcement at a roadside stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F38.teaching_text: Turning a minor traffic citation into obstruction lands you with a criminal Class Two misdemeanor charge.

sec07-card-sec07-F39.question_text: What steps should you take if you believe an officer acted improperly during a stop?
sec07-card-sec07-F39.teaching_text: Record fresh details right after the stop and contact the law-enforcement agency printed on your ticket.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: What happens to a driver whose failure to signal forces a motorcyclist to switch lanes, leave the road, or crash?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Sudden unsignaled lane moves rob riders of escape space and bring legal charges and fines—even without contact.

sec07-card-sec07-F40.question_text: Under what weather, light, and pavement conditions—and in what crash types—do most farm-equipment wrecks happen?
sec07-card-sec07-F40.teaching_text: Good weather breeds overconfidence around slow tractors, producing daylight sideswipes and angle collisions on dry pavement.

sec07-card-sec07-F41.question_text: What misread maneuver frequently causes drivers to crash while trying to pass farm machinery?
sec07-card-sec07-F41.teaching_text: When a tractor slows and extends a left arm toward a field gate, impatient followers fatally misread it as wave-by.

sec07-card-sec07-F42.question_text: May you pass slow farm machinery in a no-passing zone, and what visual hazard hides from behind?
sec07-card-sec07-F42.teaching_text: Crossing solid yellow lines for a slow tractor is illegal, and wide blades or planters often jut beyond the tires.

sec07-card-sec07-F43.question_text: When is the only advisable moment to pass farm equipment on a public road?
sec07-card-sec07-F43.teaching_text: Waiting until the operator eases off at a practical wide spot eliminates left-turn and wide-implement surprises.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: How do no-passing zones and operator pull-offs govern passing farm machinery?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Never cross a no-passing line for slow machinery, and wait until the operator pulls off to let traffic clear.

sec07-card-sec07-F44.question_text: What front light and rear light—or reflector substitute—must farm equipment display?
sec07-card-sec07-F44.teaching_text: Look for one white front lamp plus either a five-hundred-foot rear red lamp or two four-inch red reflectors.

sec16-card-sec16-F01.question_text: How does North Carolina law classify bicycles, and do impaired-driving laws apply to cyclists?
sec16-card-sec16-F01.teaching_text: Because state law classifies bikes as vehicles, riders carry the same traffic rules and DWI rules as motorists.

sec16-card-sec16-F02.question_text: Where should motorists expect to encounter bicyclists, and when might a cyclist take the entire lane?
sec16-card-sec16-F02.teaching_text: Narrow lanes, potholes, or turn setups often make riding centered in the travel lane the safest legal move.

sec16-card-sec16-F03.question_text: Which three road spaces may cyclists use, and what three factors guide that choice?
sec16-card-sec16-F03.teaching_text: Broken glass on shoulders or right-turning car conflicts often push cyclists out of edge strips into travel lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-F04.question_text: Which three core roadway rules must bicyclists obey just like motor-vehicle drivers?
sec16-card-sec16-F04.teaching_text: Predictable right-side riding, full stops at red lights and stop signs, and hand signals keep traffic coordinated.

sec16-card-sec16-F05.question_text: When may you overtake a bicyclist, and what is the safest way to pass?
sec16-card-sec16-F05.teaching_text: Moving cleanly into the next lane beats squeezing past elbow-close inside the cyclist's own lane.

sec16-card-sec16-F06.question_text: Which passing statutes govern overtaking a bicycle on a North Carolina road?
sec16-card-sec16-F06.teaching_text: Treat passing a cyclist with the exact sight-distance and lane rules required for overtaking another car.

sec16-card-sec16-F07.question_text: Why must bicyclists always ride with the flow of traffic rather than facing it?
sec16-card-sec16-F07.teaching_text: Drivers pulling out of driveways scan left for approaching traffic and routinely miss wrong-way riders coming from the right.

sec16-card-sec16-F09.question_text: Where are bicycles allowed, and which three classic car-versus-bike crash patterns must you watch for?
sec16-card-sec16-F09.teaching_text: Turning left across a rider, nosing out of a side street, or cutting right across their path causes most collisions.

sec16-card-sec16-F08.question_text: What front and rear visibility distances are required on a bicycle ridden at night?
sec16-card-sec16-F08.teaching_text: Test questions frequently swap those nighttime visibility ranges because forward headlamps shine farther ahead than rear red markers.

sec16-card-sec16-R01.question_text: How does a bicycle's required nighttime front-light distance compare with its rear red visibility distance?
sec16-card-sec16-R01.teaching_text: Exam questions love swapping two hundred and three hundred feet—front reaches farther than rear.

sec16-card-sec16-F10.question_text: Which bicycle riders and passengers must wear an approved helmet and use a saddle seat?
sec16-card-sec16-F10.teaching_text: Every rider or passenger younger than sixteen needs both a certified helmet and a proper saddle seat.

sec16-card-sec16-F11.question_text: What weight or height cutoff requires a young bicycle passenger to ride in a restraining seat?
sec16-card-sec16-F11.teaching_text: Forty is the easy double number here—under forty pounds or forty inches demands a protective child bike seat.

sec16-card-sec16-R02.question_text: How does the age cutoff for bicycle helmets differ from the size cutoff for restraining seats?
sec16-card-sec16-R02.teaching_text: Pair age sixteen with helmets and forty pounds or inches with child restraining seats on test day.

sec16-card-sec16-F12.question_text: What share of crash deaths are pedestrians in cities compared with rural areas?
sec16-card-sec16-F12.teaching_text: Dense urban intersections push pedestrian fatalities to roughly two-fifths of city crash deaths versus one-tenth rural.

sec16-card-sec16-R04.question_text: How much higher is the pedestrian share of motor-vehicle deaths in cities than in rural areas?
sec16-card-sec16-R04.teaching_text: Heavy foot traffic and constant turns make city streets four times more pedestrian-heavy in crash statistics.

sec16-card-sec16-F13.question_text: Which three groups make up most pedestrians killed in traffic crashes?
sec16-card-sec16-F13.teaching_text: Darting kids, slower-moving seniors, and people who have been drinking need extra visual cushion from drivers.

sec16-card-sec16-F14.question_text: Which side of the road should pedestrians use, and what color helps drivers spot them?
sec16-card-sec16-F14.teaching_text: Facing oncoming headlights lets walkers see danger early while white clothing pops out against dark asphalt.

sec16-card-sec16-F15.question_text: What should you carry and stay ready to do when walking along a road after dark?
sec16-card-sec16-F15.teaching_text: Even careful drivers outrun low beams at night, so never assume an approaching car sees you on foot.

sec16-card-sec16-R03.question_text: How does the safe side of the road for a pedestrian differ from the legal side for a bicyclist?
sec16-card-sec16-R03.teaching_text: Flipping this classic pair costs easy test points: foot travelers face traffic on the left while bikes ride right.

sec16-card-sec16-F16.question_text: How do heavy trucks accelerate—especially uphill—and how can their sheer size trick your eyes?
sec16-card-sec16-F16.teaching_text: Large objects appear to move slower from afar, tempting cars to pull out in front of fast highway rigs.

sec16-card-sec16-F17.question_text: Why do big trucks swing wide on turns, and what must you check before passing one drifting left?
sec16-card-sec16-F17.teaching_text: A rig swinging left may actually be setting up a wide right turn that traps cars squeezing inside.

sec16-card-sec16-F18.question_text: What happens to a heavy truck's brakes on long downhill grades, and how does stopping change?
sec16-card-sec16-F18.teaching_text: Cutting tightly in front of a descending tractor-trailer leaves a heavy rig with overheated brakes nowhere to go.

sec16-card-sec16-F19.question_text: How can passing or riding beside a large truck affect your car's handling?
sec16-card-sec16-F19.teaching_text: Turbulent bow waves from big trailers buffet lighter cars sideways unless you leave generous lane cushion.

sec16-card-sec16-F20.question_text: Why is it dangerous to assume a truck driver sitting twice as high as you can see everything?
sec16-card-sec16-F20.teaching_text: Tall hoods and long trailers create massive blind zones right around the rig despite the elevated seat.

sec16-card-sec16-F21.question_text: How far do a tractor-trailer's blind no-zones stretch in front, beside, and behind the rig?
sec16-card-sec16-F21.teaching_text: Memorize twenty feet ahead of the bumper and two hundred feet behind the trailer doors, plus both sides.

sec16-card-sec16-R05.question_text: How many times longer is a truck's rear no-zone compared with its front no-zone?
sec16-card-sec16-R05.teaching_text: Ten times longer behind—two hundred feet versus twenty—means tailgating a trailer blinds both you and the trucker.

sec16-card-sec16-F22.question_text: Why must you never linger in a truck's no-zone, and what quick mirror check tells if you're visible?
sec16-card-sec16-F22.teaching_text: Camping beside a trailer blocks the trucker's escape lane; if you cannot spot their face in the mirror, move.

sec16-card-sec16-F23.question_text: How do recreational vehicles compare with passenger cars in size, acceleration, braking, and turns?
sec16-card-sec16-F23.teaching_text: Vacation drivers piloting heavy motorhomes need extra room to pick up speed, swing corners, and haul down.

sec16-card-sec16-F24.question_text: What happens to sightlines on both ends when you follow closely behind a recreational vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F24.teaching_text: Tucking behind a wide motorhome walls off your forward view while hiding your car inside giant RV blind spots.

sec16-card-sec16-F25.question_text: What two stability hazards should you anticipate around a vehicle pulling a trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-F25.teaching_text: Gusts or slick curves set trailers fishtailing, and hard braking can fold the trailer sideways across lanes.

sec16-card-sec16-F26.question_text: How much clear road ahead can it take to safely overtake a vehicle towing a trailer?
sec16-card-sec16-F26.teaching_text: Extra combined length stretches your time in the oncoming lane to as much as half a mile.

sec16-card-sec16-R07.question_text: What passing-distance and hard-braking facts go hand in hand around towed trailers?
sec16-card-sec16-R07.teaching_text: Never rush an overtake or cut sharply in front of a towed load that could fold under sudden braking.

sec16-card-sec16-F27.question_text: How much right-of-way respect do motorcycle and moped riders get compared with four-wheeled vehicles?
sec16-card-sec16-F27.teaching_text: Smaller size never shrinks priority at intersections—treat two-wheeled traffic with full driver courtesy.

sec16-card-sec16-F28.question_text: How much lane width belongs to a motorcycle, and how must you pass one?
sec16-card-sec16-F28.teaching_text: Riders shift left and right inside their lane to dodge potholes and oil streaks, so never share their lane.

sec16-card-sec16-F29.question_text: Where in the lane do mopeds ride, and what minimum clearance must you leave on their left?
sec16-card-sec16-F29.teaching_text: Crowding a slower moped along the right portion of the lane risks clipping handlebars with your mirror.

sec16-card-sec16-R06.question_text: How does passing a motorcycle legally differ from passing a moped in North Carolina?
sec16-card-sec16-R06.teaching_text: Test questions pit these two rules head-to-head: full lane change for motorcycles versus at least two feet left for mopeds.

sec16-card-sec16-F30.question_text: Why is generous side clearance critical whenever your car passes any two-wheeled rider?
sec16-card-sec16-F30.teaching_text: Even without touching handlebars, the air blast rolling off a close car can shove a light cycle off balance.

sec16-card-sec16-F31.question_text: Before which maneuvers—and one turn in particular—must you double-check blind spots for motorcycles and mopeds?
sec16-card-sec16-F31.teaching_text: Slim bike profiles hide easily behind windshield pillars or mirrors right as cars turn left across oncoming traffic.

sec16-card-sec16-F32.question_text: What share of North Carolina motorcycle crashes involve a car, and who is usually at fault?
sec16-card-sec16-F32.teaching_text: Roughly two out of three bike wrecks involve an automobile whose driver failed to spot the approaching rider.

sec16-card-sec16-F34.question_text: When do motorcycles stop faster than cars, and what two conditions make them stop slower?
sec16-card-sec16-F34.teaching_text: Extra passenger weight or slick pavement forces gentler braking so the rider does not lock a wheel and go down.

sec16-card-sec16-R09.question_text: Which two situations stretch out a motorcycle's stopping distance compared with dry solo riding?
sec16-card-sec16-R09.teaching_text: Tailgating a two-up rider or a bike on wet asphalt fails when either condition slows or destabilizes braking.

sec16-card-sec16-F35.question_text: Which four loose or wet road hazards threaten riders ahead, and what does wobbling tell you?
sec16-card-sec16-F35.teaching_text: Patches of sand, gravel, wet leaves, or puddles barely phase cars yet drop bikes—especially hesitant beginners.

sec16-card-sec16-F36.question_text: How should you adjust following distance behind a motorcycle or moped on slick pavement, and why?
sec16-card-sec16-F36.teaching_text: Two narrow tires lose balance far quicker than four wide tires, demanding extra stopping room behind them.

sec16-card-sec16-F37.question_text: At which three rough or metal roadway features should you give riders extra space?
sec16-card-sec16-F37.teaching_text: Angled tracks, potholes, and slick steel bridge gratings force riders to slow down and adjust line suddenly.

sec16-card-sec16-F33.question_text: What federal helmet standard and strap rule apply to every moped operator and passenger?
sec16-card-sec16-F33.teaching_text: An unbuckled or novelty shell fails inspection and crash impact—every moped occupant needs a strapped FMVSS 218 helmet.

sec16-card-sec16-F38.question_text: What wheel count, engine-size cap, and transmission rule define a moped in North Carolina?
sec16-card-sec16-F38.teaching_text: Exceeding fifty cubic centimeters or adding external gear shifting bumps a two- or three-wheeler out of moped class.

sec16-card-sec16-F39.question_text: What is the legal top speed of a moped, and are faster-built models allowed on North Carolina roads?
sec16-card-sec16-F39.teaching_text: Any scooter engineered to top thirty miles per hour cannot be operated legally as a moped in North Carolina.

sec16-card-sec16-F40.question_text: What minimum age and credential are required to ride a moped on public roads, and what about DWI?
sec16-card-sec16-F40.teaching_text: Public-road moped riders need age sixteen plus a valid state license or ID card, and DWI laws still apply.

sec16-card-sec16-R08.question_text: What are North Carolina's three headline numbers for moped engine size, top speed, and rider age?
sec16-card-sec16-R08.teaching_text: Locking fifty, thirty, and sixteen together nails three favorite moped exam questions in one breath.

sec16-card-sec16-F41.question_text: Where in the lane should moped riders stay, and what two lane-sharing moves must they avoid?
sec16-card-sec16-F41.teaching_text: Squeezing between parked cars and moving queues at corners puts mopeds straight into opening doors and right hooks.

sec16-card-sec16-F42.question_text: What clothing colors and turn signals should moped riders use to stay conspicuous?
sec16-card-sec16-F42.teaching_text: High-contrast clothing catches eyes early, and hand signals fill in whenever a moped lacks electric blinkers.

sec16-card-sec16-F43.question_text: Since July 2015, what DMV registration and plate rules apply to every North Carolina moped?
sec16-card-sec16-F43.teaching_text: Riding an unregistered moped without a visible rear license plate invites an immediate traffic stop.

sec16-card-sec16-F45.question_text: Which DMV form proves moped ownership when the owner lacks a manufacturer's certificate of origin?
sec16-card-sec16-F45.teaching_text: Older mopeds often lack factory origin papers, so a sworn affidavit of facts lets owners register legally.
sec16-card-sec16-F45.must_match_memory_hook: File affidavit M V R fifty-eight

visual_sync.text_span: File affidavit M V R fifty-eight

sec16-card-sec16-R10.question_text: When did moped registration become mandatory, and what backup form covers missing origin paperwork?
sec16-card-sec16-R10.teaching_text: DMV tied mandatory July 2015 registration with the affidavit fallback so owners without origin certificates could get plated.

sec16-card-sec16-F46.question_text: Who is held legally responsible when trash is tossed or blown out of a moving vehicle?
sec16-card-sec16-F46.teaching_text: Even if a passenger drops a wrapper or cargo blows out of a truck bed, the driver takes the citation.

sec16-card-sec16-R11.question_text: How does the fine range for a first littering conviction compare with a repeat offense within three years?
sec16-card-sec16-R11.teaching_text: Repeat littering within three years doubles both ends of the penalty—from two-fifty-to-a-thousand up to five-hundred-to-two-thousand.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.question_text: What license status applies to every North Carolina driver under eighteen, and why do special laws govern them?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.teaching_text: Much higher crash rates among younger drivers explain why North Carolina builds extra safety guardrails around every minor licensee.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.question_text: Which North Carolina residents by age and vehicle class qualify for a Level One Limited Learner Permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.teaching_text: Once you turn fifteen as a state resident aiming for Class C vehicles, graduated licensing opens with this first permit.
sec02-card-sec02-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Ages fifteen to seventeen, Class C

visual_sync.text_span: Ages fifteen to seventeen, Class C

sec02-card-sec02-F02.question_text: What driver education certificate — including minimum classroom and behind-the-wheel hours — must a teen present before taking the permit test?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.teaching_text: Showing up at the license office without both thirty classroom hours and six road hours completed blocks permit testing.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.question_text: When a driver is under eighteen, for which tests must they present that thirty-plus-six driver education certificate beforehand?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.teaching_text: Minors need that approved thirty-classroom and six-road hour certificate whether testing for a learner permit or a license.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.question_text: Which three tests must a Level One Limited Learner Permit applicant pass?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.teaching_text: Clearing written rules, road signs, and eyesight screening earns your starter permit without an on-road driving exam.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.question_text: Who must sign the application for a minor's learner permit or driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.teaching_text: No minor receives a North Carolina permit or license without an official signature from a parent or legal guardian.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.question_text: Who is allowed to serve as a Level One supervising driver, and how long must they have held a valid license?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.teaching_text: An older sibling or friend licensed only three years cannot supervise you even if your parent approves them.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.question_text: During the first six months with a Level One permit, what daily hours and supervision rule apply?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.teaching_text: Late-night practice after nine p.m. is off-limits during your opening six months, even with a parent beside you.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.question_text: Once you have held a Level One permit for six full months, how do your legal driving hours and supervision rules stand?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.teaching_text: Clocking six months unlocks late-night practice hours so you can log dark driving, yet solo trips remain illegal.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.question_text: Across both time phases of a Level One permit, what changes after month six and what never changes?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.teaching_text: Exam questions try to trick you into dropping supervision after month six, when only the nine p.m. curfew lifts.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.question_text: Under a Level One permit, what restraint rule covers every rider, and who is allowed in the front row?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.teaching_text: Keeping extra passengers out of the front row ensures your supervising driver has clear sightlines and immediate reach.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.question_text: Which graduated licensing stage restricts the front seat strictly to the teen driver and the supervising driver?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.teaching_text: Level One is the stage where nobody except the learner and the supervising adult may occupy front seating.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.question_text: Where is a Level One driver barred from using a cell phone or any connected cell-phone technology while driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.teaching_text: Hands-free Bluetooth or dashboard phone pairing still counts as banned connected cell-phone technology in streets or parking lots.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.question_text: Which specific recipients make up the only cell-phone exception for a North Carolina teen driver?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.teaching_text: Calling a friend because you are running late violates the ban, since only true emergency responders, medical care, or parents, guardians, and spouses qualify.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.question_text: How many months must a teen hold the Level One permit before applying for a Limited Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.teaching_text: Finishing your practice hours early never shortens the mandatory nine-month calendar wait before stepping up.

sec02-card-sec02-F07.question_text: How many total behind-the-wheel hours — and how many night hours — must appear on the Level One driving log?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.teaching_text: At least ten of your sixty supervised hours must happen in darkness so night glare is practiced before solo driving.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.question_text: How does the driving log define daytime driving versus night driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.teaching_text: Logging twilight minutes accurately matters because night credit starts only after sunset once daylight is gone.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.question_text: Who signs the Level One driving log, and when do you turn it in to the Division?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.teaching_text: Forgetting to have your supervising driver sign the completed log stalls your Limited Provisional License appointment at the counter.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.question_text: How do the calendar holding period and the driving-log hour rule work together before Level Two?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.teaching_text: Both hurdles apply independently, meaning sixty logged hours including ten at night still require nine full months held.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.question_text: Which three types of convictions must be completely absent for the previous six months to advance to Level Two?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.teaching_text: A single seat-belt, cell-phone, or moving violation conviction resets your six-month clean-record countdown toward advancement.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.question_text: What age range qualifies for the Level Two Limited Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.teaching_text: Even if you held a starter permit for nine months at fifteen, you must reach sixteen before stepping into Level Two.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.question_text: During which daily hours — and for which direct trips at any hour — may a Level Two driver drive alone?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.teaching_text: Outside five a.m. to nine p.m., solo trips are legal only straight to or from work or volunteer fire, rescue, or EMS duty.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.question_text: When is a Level Two holder allowed to drive without a supervisor on board?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.teaching_text: Stopping for food after a late shift breaks the direct-route rule that shields after-nine work or volunteer rescue trips.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.question_text: At Level Two, what restraint rule covers passengers, and where must a supervisor sit whenever supervision is required?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.teaching_text: During late-night non-work drives that still require supervision, your supervising adult must occupy the front seat beside you.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.question_text: When driving unsupervised at Level Two, how many under-twenty-one passengers from outside your household are allowed — and how do household riders differ?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.teaching_text: Peer distraction spikes teen crash risk, so unsupervised trips cap non-household riders under twenty-one unless everyone aboard lives at home.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.question_text: Under what single condition may an unsupervised Level Two driver carry one extra under-twenty-one passenger from outside the household?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.teaching_text: That bonus seat applies only while driving a student directly to or from school, never for weekend hangouts.

sec02-card-sec02-F21.question_text: When driving unsupervised at Level Two, how does the household-member rule change the moment a non-household rider under twenty-one gets in?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.teaching_text: You can drive all your younger siblings alone, yet bringing even one teen friend bars under-twenty-one household members from riding along.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.question_text: Which riders trigger the unsupervised Level Two passenger limit, and what mixing trap catches household riders?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.teaching_text: Passengers twenty-one or older are not capped, whereas outside riders under twenty-one trigger both the count and the household-mixing ban.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.question_text: How do cell-phone rules and exceptions at Level Two compare with Level One?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.teaching_text: Earning solo daytime driving privileges never relaxes North Carolina's ban on teen phone use behind the wheel.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.question_text: How long must a teen hold the Level Two license before applying for a Full Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.teaching_text: Six months of solo daytime experience builds independent judgment before nighttime and passenger caps come off.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.question_text: What minimum holding period separates a Level Two Limited Provisional License from a Full Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.teaching_text: Keep the two waits straight on test day because Level One takes nine months whereas Level Two takes six.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.question_text: What conviction-free record is required over the prior six months to move up to Level Three?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.teaching_text: Just like advancing earlier, any moving violation, seat-belt ticket, or cell-phone conviction within six months blocks your upgrade.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.question_text: How can an eligible driver upgrade to a Level Three Full Provisional License — or to a regular Class C license at age eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.teaching_text: Once your holding period and clean record qualify, you can complete either upgrade online without waiting in an office line.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.question_text: Which three graduated limits disappear once a teen earns a Full Provisional License?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.teaching_text: Reaching Full Provisional removes the nine p.m. curfew, late-night supervision requirement, and teen passenger count limits.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.question_text: If a Full Provisional licensee is still under eighteen, what cell-phone rule applies while driving?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.teaching_text: Until your eighteenth birthday arrives, cell phones stay illegal behind the wheel apart from listed emergency calls.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.question_text: After a Full Provisional License removes hour, supervision, and passenger caps, which restriction still binds drivers under eighteen?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.teaching_text: Many teens assume Full Provisional equals adult privileges, forgetting the under-eighteen cell-phone ban remains active.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.question_text: What should a new North Carolina resident aged fifteen to seventeen who already holds an out-of-state permit or license do?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.teaching_text: Checking with a local office clarifies which graduated stage matches your prior out-of-state holding time and driver education.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.question_text: How does the DMV monitor a provisional licensee's driving record compared with an adult's, and when might it reach out?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.teaching_text: Provisional records face tighter scrutiny, triggering DMV follow-up after qualifying crashes or traffic convictions.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.question_text: How much alcohol or drugs may a provisional licensee consume before or while driving, and what penalty hits upon conviction?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.teaching_text: Even a trace sip of alcohol or impairing drug triggers a mandatory one-year license revocation upon conviction.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.question_text: Why is thinking in terms of a blood-alcohol percentage wrong for a provisional licensee?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.teaching_text: Adult percentage thresholds do not shield minors because consuming any amount at all brings a one-year revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.question_text: Which specific phone, typing, and reading actions are illegal for a provisional licensee behind the wheel?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.teaching_text: Glancing at an incoming text or email at speed pulls teen eyes off traffic just as dangerously as typing.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.question_text: Who must have a seat belt properly fastened when a provisional licensee drives a moving vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.teaching_text: Whether riding up front or in the third row, every passenger in a provisional driver's moving car must buckle up.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.question_text: Which two school disciplinary actions lasting more than ten consecutive days cost a student their license, and for how long?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.teaching_text: Getting suspended or assigned to disciplinary alternative schooling past ten straight days strips driving privileges for twelve months.
sec02-card-sec02-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Over ten days, lose twelve months

visual_sync.text_span: Over ten days, lose twelve months

sec02-card-sec02-R09.question_text: Under North Carolina's Lose Control, Lose Your License law, what exact school-discipline threshold triggers a twelve-month suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.teaching_text: Ten days or fewer avoids the trigger, whereas crossing ten consecutive disciplinary days triggers a full twelve-month suspension.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.question_text: Give two examples of safety restrictions that can be placed on a North Carolina driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.teaching_text: Tailored restrictions let drivers operate legally so long as required eyewear or vehicle equipment is in place.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.question_text: How does the law treat a driver who operates outside the limits of a license restriction?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.teaching_text: Driving past the boundary of any restriction on your card carries the full weight of driving unlicensed.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.question_text: Why must you stay strictly inside every restriction printed on your driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.teaching_text: Your license is valid only inside its stated restriction limits, turning any violation into an unlicensed-driving offense.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.question_text: What may the DMV do to verify documents you bring in, and what happens to any altered document?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.teaching_text: Never cross out or tweak a form yourself because examiners copy or verify originals and reject anything showing alteration.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.question_text: Which three core identity, residence, and status facts must a first-time North Carolina applicant prove?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.teaching_text: Bring paperwork covering full name with birth date, state residence address, and Social Security number or U.S. legal presence.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.question_text: Beyond identity and residence documents, what coverage proof must a driver license applicant present?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.teaching_text: North Carolina verifies financial responsibility up front before putting a new driver license in your hands.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.question_text: Does the phrase Not for Federal Identification invalidate a North Carolina license, learner permit, or ID card for state purposes?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.teaching_text: That label only flags federal security limits while keeping your North Carolina driving or state ID privileges completely valid.

sec02-card-sec02-F42.question_text: Starting May seven, two thousand twenty-five, where do holders of a Not for Federal Identification card need extra documents?
sec02-card-sec02-F42.teaching_text: Boarding commercial planes or entering ID-checked federal sites, military bases, or nuclear plants requires supplemental documents without a star.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.question_text: Which three groups — homeless applicants, legally blind applicants, and older seniors — qualify for a free ID card, and what paperwork does each need?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.teaching_text: Homeless applicants bring a shelter letter and legally blind applicants bring a physician letter, while seniors seventy and up need no extra letter.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.question_text: Beyond homelessness, blindness, or age seventy, what two medical or disability records qualify someone for a free ID card?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.teaching_text: Either a driving-record medical cancellation or a primary care provider's letter documenting a developmental disability waives the ID fee.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.question_text: In what physical format must required automobile liability insurance proof be presented, and what phone shortcut is rejected?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.teaching_text: Showing a screenshot or photo of your insurance card on a phone screen gets turned away at the counter.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.question_text: Which three licensing or privilege situations require you to show proof of liability insurance?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.teaching_text: First-time or out-of-state transfers, post-suspension or revocation restorations, and court-granted Limited Driving Privileges all demand insurance proof.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.question_text: How many days after issuance do Form DL-one hundred twenty-three, insurance binders, and certificates stay valid?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.teaching_text: Waiting more than thirty days after your agent issues Form DL-one hundred twenty-three makes the form stale for licensing.

sec03-card-sec03-F08.question_text: What step with your insurance agent prevents delays before you head to the driver license office?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.teaching_text: Picking up that agent-issued insurance form ahead of time keeps your counter appointment moving without last-minute delays.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.question_text: Who signs Form DL-123A — the certification of insurance exemption — at the license office?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.teaching_text: Drivers with zero registered cars who never borrow private non-fleet vehicles sign that exemption form at the counter.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.question_text: What driving restriction comes with signing the insurance exemption, and what fee plus proof lifts it later?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.teaching_text: Dropping that fleet-only limit later requires bringing financial-responsibility proof and paying the duplicate fee shown in the handbook.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.question_text: How does Form DL-one hundred twenty-three differ in purpose and effect from Form DL-123A?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.teaching_text: Keep the letter A straight on exam day because DL-123A signs an exemption that restricts you to fleet vehicles.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.question_text: What did the two thousand five REAL ID Act change, and what federal rules does North Carolina's REAL ID satisfy?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.teaching_text: Federal standards tightened state credential checks so compliant North Carolina cards clear TSA checkpoints and federal buildings.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.question_text: What visual mark on a North Carolina license, learner permit, or ID card shows that it is a REAL ID?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.teaching_text: Checking the face of your license, permit, or ID for the star tells you instantly whether it is federally compliant.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.question_text: Which air travelers — including teens — and which facility visitors are affected by REAL ID rules?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.teaching_text: Domestic commercial flyers including unaccompanied minors under eighteen plus visitors to ID-checked military bases, prisons, or nuclear plants fall under these rules.

sec03-card-sec03-F12.question_text: If you do not hold a REAL ID, can you still enter ID-required federal sites or fly, and what should you do beforehand?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.teaching_text: Lacking the star never bans entry outright, provided you verify acceptable backup documents with the TSA or host agency ahead of time.

sec03-card-sec03-F13.question_text: What exact four-word notice must federal law print on the face of every non-REAL ID license or ID card?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.teaching_text: Any standard card issued without the star carries that mandatory federal notice printed right across its face.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.question_text: When did NCDMV start issuing REAL ID and non-REAL ID cards, and how much extra does a REAL ID cost?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.teaching_text: Getting the star adds zero surcharge beyond standard credential fees, which has been true since rollout in May two thousand seventeen.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.question_text: Compare a REAL ID and a non-REAL ID card on face markings, driving validity, and price?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.teaching_text: One shows a star while the other states Not for Federal Identification, yet both drive legally and cost identical fees.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.question_text: Once you establish residence in North Carolina, how many days do you have to get a state license or learner permit?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.teaching_text: Letting your old out-of-state card ride past sixty days after moving in leaves you driving past the statutory deadline.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.question_text: How fast must a new resident apply for and receive a North Carolina CDL to keep commercial driving privileges?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.teaching_text: Commercial drivers get only half the regular window, needing their North Carolina CDL within thirty days of residency.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.question_text: How does the new-resident licensing deadline differ between a regular North Carolina license and a CDL?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.teaching_text: Written questions love swapping thirty and sixty days between regular passenger newcomers and commercial drivers transferring in.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.question_text: If an applicant has lived in North Carolina less than twelve months, what search must DMV complete before issuing a card?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.teaching_text: Anyone with under a year of state residency undergoes a mandatory National Sex Offender Public Registry check before issuance.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.question_text: Which tests may a new resident applying for a Class C license have to take — and when is a road test added?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.teaching_text: Expect office checks on laws, vision, and signs, while an on-road drive happens only if the examiner deems it needed.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.question_text: Who counts as a nonresident under North Carolina licensing rules?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.teaching_text: Your legal home in another state, territory, jurisdiction, or foreign country keeps you classified as a nonresident.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.question_text: Which four common groups — from travelers and college students to military families — count as nonresidents?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.teaching_text: Out-of-state students and stationed service members planning to return home — plus nonresident military spouses — remain nonresidents.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.question_text: What separates a nonresident like a visiting college student from a new resident who must get a North Carolina license?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.teaching_text: Planning to return to an out-of-state home preserves nonresident status, whereas establishing state residence starts the licensing clock.

sec03-card-sec03-F22.question_text: How does North Carolina store customer photos and signatures, and what data feature sits on every license or ID?
sec03-card-sec03-F22.teaching_text: Central digital storage pairs with a machine-readable bar code on your card holding customer record data.

sec03-card-sec03-F23.question_text: Because cards are produced centrally, what sixty-day document lets you drive right away and when does your permanent card arrive?
sec03-card-sec03-F23.teaching_text: Local offices never print plastic licenses on the spot, issuing a sixty-day driving certificate while central production mails your card.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.question_text: How long is your temporary driving certificate valid, and why isn't your plastic license handed over at the counter?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.teaching_text: Both the temporary certificate window and central mail delivery run on the same sixty-day timeline.

sec03-card-sec03-F24.question_text: While waiting for your new card in the mail, what may you keep using for photo identification?
sec03-card-sec03-F24.teaching_text: Hang onto your existing license or ID card so you still have photo identification until the replacement arrives.

sec03-card-sec03-F25.question_text: What card orientation applies under twenty-one, and how do the colored birthday bars differ under eighteen versus eighteen to twenty?
sec03-card-sec03-F25.teaching_text: Under-eighteen vertical cards show red and yellow bars for eighteen and twenty-one, while ages eighteen to twenty show one red bar.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.question_text: Which age group gets both red and yellow birthday bars on a vertical card, and which gets only a single red bar?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.teaching_text: Once an applicant is already eighteen through twenty, the yellow eighteenth-birthday bar disappears, leaving only the twenty-first red bar.

sec03-card-sec03-F40.question_text: On what annual date does a North Carolina license expire, and how many years does it last by age at issuance?
sec03-card-sec03-F40.teaching_text: Cards issued from age eighteen through sixty-five run eight years to your birthday, dropping to five years at sixty-six and up.

sec03-card-sec03-R09.question_text: What exact age line decides whether a newly issued North Carolina license lasts eight years or five years?
sec03-card-sec03-R09.teaching_text: Your age on the issuance date sets the term, switching from eight years to five years right at age sixty-six.

sec03-card-sec03-F26.question_text: When does DMV mail a renewal reminder card, what does it tell you, and is bringing it mandatory?
sec03-card-sec03-F26.teaching_text: DMV sends that courtesy card roughly six months early showing your renewal length, though you can still renew without it.

sec03-card-sec03-F28.question_text: How many days before expiration may you renew a North Carolina driver license?
sec03-card-sec03-F28.teaching_text: Opening the renewal window one hundred eighty days early lets you handle your appointment well before your birthday rush.

sec03-card-sec03-F27.question_text: Which test is always required when you renew your license in person at a driver license office?
sec03-card-sec03-F27.teaching_text: Every counter renewal screens your eyesight to confirm you still meet safe driving vision standards.

sec03-card-sec03-F29.question_text: If you show up to renew without your current or expired license in hand, what must you show the examiner?
sec03-card-sec03-F29.teaching_text: Bringing two approved identification documents lets the examiner verify who you are when your old card is missing.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.question_text: How is your vision verified differently when renewing in person versus renewing by mail?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.teaching_text: Since a mail applicant cannot look into the counter machine, a licensed physician must sign a vision statement instead.

sec03-card-sec03-F30.question_text: How long must a resident be out of state continuously to renew by mail, and when does that temporary license end?
sec03-card-sec03-F30.teaching_text: After thirty continuous days out of state, the mailed temporary card expires sixty days after returning or on its printed date first.

sec03-card-sec03-F31.question_text: Beyond thirty continuous days away, what address, Class C expiration, photo age, record, vision, affidavit, age-cap, and cycle rules govern civilian mail renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-F31.teaching_text: Every box must pass, including Class C expired two years max, five-year photo, physician vision, offender affidavit, age seventy-two cap, and alternating cycles.

sec03-card-sec03-F32.question_text: How often may eligible drivers renew by mail, and which two license types can never use mail renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-F32.teaching_text: Mail renewal alternates every other cycle, and neither commercial licenses nor full provisional licenses ever qualify.

sec03-card-sec03-F33.question_text: What documents — and optional address option — let an active-duty service member stationed outside North Carolina renew by mail?
sec03-card-sec03-F33.teaching_text: Sending military orders plus a front-and-back military ID copy works even when using a host family address.

sec03-card-sec03-F34.question_text: With active-duty paperwork, how early before expiration can a military renewal happen, and how old may the DMV photo on file be?
sec03-card-sec03-F34.teaching_text: Deployment schedules earn extra flexibility, allowing renewals over a year early with a DMV photo up to eight years old.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.question_text: Compare the maximum age of the DMV photo on file for a civilian mail renewal versus a military mail renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.teaching_text: Civilians hit a five-year photo ceiling for mail renewal, whereas active-duty service members get up to eight years.

sec03-card-sec03-F35.question_text: How many times in a lifetime may a military-designation license be renewed by mail, and which family members also qualify?
sec03-card-sec03-F35.teaching_text: Military-designation mail renewals cap at two per lifetime, and both military spouses and dependents share mail-renewal access.

sec03-card-sec03-F36.question_text: Under what expiration condition can a military dependent holding a full provisional license upgrade to Class C at age eighteen?
sec03-card-sec03-F36.teaching_text: As long as that full provisional card has been expired one year or less, an eighteen-year-old military dependent can upgrade.

sec03-card-sec03-F37.question_text: When does a service member returning to North Carolina actually need to visit a driver license office?
sec03-card-sec03-F37.teaching_text: Returning home from duty triggers no extra office trip until your license reaches its normal renewal date.

sec03-card-sec03-F38.question_text: How can a qualified veteran add a VETERAN designation at their next renewal, and what extra fee applies?
sec03-card-sec03-F38.teaching_text: Bringing honorable discharge paperwork like Form DD-two hundred fourteen adds the designation free at your next renewal.

sec03-card-sec03-F39.question_text: What option and fee apply if a veteran wants the VETERAN designation added before their next scheduled renewal?
sec03-card-sec03-F39.teaching_text: Requesting an early replacement card before renewal prints the designation right away for the standard duplicate fee.

sec03-card-sec03-F41.question_text: What license-status rule governs getting a duplicate, and what two ways can you replace a lost or stolen license?
sec03-card-sec03-F41.teaching_text: Expired, suspended, or cancelled licenses cannot get duplicates, while active lost cards replace with two IDs or online using your number.

sec03-card-sec03-F42.question_text: What must you do within sixty days after changing your address, and what single address-change situation is exempt?
sec03-card-sec03-F42.teaching_text: Moving requires notifying the division and getting a duplicate within sixty days, unless government renumbering changed your address without moving.

sec03-card-sec03-F43.question_text: What sixty-day DMV steps follow a name change, and how far ahead should you update Social Security first?
sec03-card-sec03-F43.teaching_text: Updating your Social Security record a full day ahead lets DMV systems match when issuing your duplicate.

sec03-card-sec03-F44.question_text: Which official records or notarized form prove a legal name change, and which jurisdictions must have issued them?
sec03-card-sec03-F44.teaching_text: Bring certified marriage, court, or Register of Deeds records or notarized Form DL-one hundred one from the U.S., Puerto Rico, U.S. territories, or Canada.

sec03-card-sec03-R10.question_text: What deadline and card requirement do address changes and name changes share, and when is an address change not a violation?
sec03-card-sec03-R10.teaching_text: Both updates require division notice and a duplicate within sixty days, except when government action renames your street without a move.

sec04-card-sec04-F01.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration is every driver impaired—and can impairment start well below that mark?
sec04-card-sec04-F01.teaching_text: Waiting until you hit the per se cap ignores how alcohol degrades reaction and judgment at much lower concentrations.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.question_text: At what blood alcohol concentration does crash risk begin climbing, and what happens to fatal crash odds at zero point zero eight?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.teaching_text: Even before reaching the legal limit, your odds of triggering a deadly wreck are already climbing fast.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.question_text: How does the zero point zero five blood alcohol mark differ from the zero point zero eight mark for car drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.teaching_text: Test questions bait you into calling zero point zero five the per se car limit when it actually marks rising crash danger.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.question_text: How did the Safe Roads Act of nineteen eighty-three reshape North Carolina's impaired-driving laws?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.teaching_text: North Carolina consolidated older scattered statutes into a single Driving While Impaired charge so nobody slips through technicalities.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.question_text: How can prosecutors prove a DWI charge without relying on a specific blood alcohol number?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.teaching_text: Blowing under zero point zero eight will not save you if alcohol or drugs visibly dull your mental or physical control.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.question_text: Which blood alcohol concentrations automatically prove DWI for a regular vehicle driver versus a commercial vehicle driver?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.teaching_text: Heavy commercial rigs carry far greater kinetic force, so the law cuts their per se alcohol threshold in half.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.question_text: How does a commercial motor vehicle driver's per se DWI limit compare to an ordinary motorist's limit?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.teaching_text: Confusing those two thresholds is a classic exam trap whenever a question switches between passenger cars and commercial trucks.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.question_text: What roadside enforcement tool do North Carolina DWI statutes authorize officers to use?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.teaching_text: Officers do not need to spot a traffic violation first to screen drivers passing through an authorized sobriety checkpoint.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.question_text: What two types of chemical testing may an officer request after charging a driver with DWI?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.teaching_text: Driving on North Carolina roads carries implied consent obligations whenever an officer charges you with impaired driving.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.question_text: What immediate revocation and additional DMV revocation hit your license if you refuse a required chemical test?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.teaching_text: Refusing the breathalyzer never dodges losing your license because civil revocations trigger automatically even before trial.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.question_text: How much of a willful-refusal revocation must pass before a judge can ever consider granting a limited driving privilege?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.teaching_text: Refusing chemical testing locks you out of any work or school driving relief for at least half a year.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.question_text: What happens to your driving privilege right away if your chemical test hits zero point zero eight—or zero point zero four commercially?
