sec04-card-sec04-F07.teaching_text: Blowing at or over the threshold benches your license on the spot for at least a month before court finishes.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.question_text: How does the license revocation for refusing a chemical test compare with failing it at zero point zero eight?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.teaching_text: Trying to outsmart the test by refusing tacks at least twelve extra DMV revocation months onto the immediate thirty-day loss.
sec04-card-sec04-R03.must_match_memory_hook: Both thirty days, refusal adds year

visual_sync.text_span: Both thirty days, refusal adds year

sec04-card-sec04-F08.question_text: Can prosecutors introduce your chemical test reading—or your refusal to take the test—against you in court?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.teaching_text: Saying no at the breath machine gives prosecutors courtroom proof of refusal rather than hiding the stop from a judge.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.question_text: May a driver sip beer or any other alcoholic drink while operating a vehicle in North Carolina?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.teaching_text: Exam traps sometimes single out beer as milder than liquor, yet drinking any alcohol while driving breaks state law.

sec04-card-sec04-F13.question_text: What is North Carolina's rule on carrying an open container of alcohol inside a vehicle, including the passenger area?
sec04-card-sec04-F13.teaching_text: Even when the driver stays completely sober, an unsealed bottle in a passenger's cupholder violates open-container law.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.question_text: What rule governs open or unopened alcohol inside the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle on a public road?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.teaching_text: Even an unbroken factory-sealed bottle inside a truck cab triggers a violation on a public highway.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.question_text: How does the passenger-area alcohol container rule differ between a regular car and a commercial vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.teaching_text: Watch whether the test question names a family sedan or a commercial rig before picking an unopened-container answer.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.question_text: How are North Carolina DWI punishment levels structured, and what mandatory penalty hits on a second DWI conviction?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.teaching_text: Aggravating factors push sentences higher, and a repeat DWI conviction guarantees time behind bars.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.question_text: Alongside punishment, how do North Carolina DWI laws address potential alcohol problems for high-risk versus lower-BAC offenders?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.teaching_text: Stopping repeat crashes means pairing legal sanctions with alcohol safety classes or targeted substance evaluations.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.question_text: What evaluation must every driver convicted of DWI finish before DMV will reinstate driving privileges?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.teaching_text: Waiting out your revocation calendar still leaves you unlicensed until your mandatory substance abuse assessment is cleared.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.question_text: How long is the mandatory license revocation for a first DWI conviction in North Carolina?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.teaching_text: Even a first-time offense wipes out your full driver license for twelve straight months upon conviction.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.question_text: When does a second DWI conviction trigger a mandatory four-year license revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.teaching_text: Catching another DWI within three years quadruples the license loss compared with a first-time conviction.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.question_text: What prior-offense window makes a third DWI conviction result in mandatory permanent license revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.teaching_text: One prior conviction inside the five-year look-back window turns a third DWI into permanent license forfeiture.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.question_text: What license penalty hits on a fourth DWI conviction, and when does that fourth offense become a felony?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.teaching_text: Stacking three prior convictions inside seven years elevates a fourth DWI into a felony prosecution alongside permanent revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.question_text: Which three look-back windows govern the second-offense four-year loss, third-offense permanent loss, and fourth-offense felony?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.teaching_text: Memorizing that odd-number step pattern keeps you from mixing up look-back periods with revocation lengths on test day.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.question_text: Which two driving credentials receive a special blood alcohol concentration restriction after a DWI?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.teaching_text: Getting back on the road after a DWI means driving under tighter alcohol caps than ordinary motorists.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.question_text: What blood alcohol cap applies on a driver's first post-DWI license restoration versus a second or later restoration?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.teaching_text: Your first comeback halves the standard alcohol cap, and any second restoration drops your legal limit to zero.
sec04-card-sec04-F23.must_match_memory_hook: First point zero four, then zero

visual_sync.text_span: First point zero four, then zero

sec04-card-sec04-R04.question_text: How does the blood alcohol restriction shift once a driver moves past their first DWI license restoration?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.teaching_text: A repeat restoration erases the zero point zero four allowance completely, leaving zero tolerance for any measurable alcohol.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.question_text: Which three convictions trigger a zero point zero zero blood alcohol restriction right from the first restoration?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.teaching_text: Those high-severity or youth convictions skip the zero point zero four step and impose total alcohol abstinence immediately.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.question_text: Which two DWI circumstances require installing an ignition interlock device on your vehicle?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.teaching_text: Either an extreme breath reading or a repeat offense within seven years forces breath-test lockouts before your engine starts.
sec04-card-sec04-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Point one five or seven-year prior

visual_sync.text_span: Point one five or seven-year prior

sec04-card-sec04-R05.question_text: How does the seven-year prior rule for an ignition interlock differ from the seven-year prior rule for felony DWI?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.teaching_text: Both rules share a seven-year clock, yet just one earlier DWI mandates interlock while felony status requires three.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.question_text: What can a court do to your car if you catch a new DWI while already revoked for an earlier DWI?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.teaching_text: Driving impaired on a DWI-revoked license puts the vehicle itself on the auction block alongside criminal penalties.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.question_text: What is the minimum legal age to buy any alcoholic beverage in North Carolina, and does merely trying under age break the law?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.teaching_text: Getting turned down at the register still counts as an unlawful underage purchase attempt.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.question_text: What license penalty hits an underage person convicted of buying, attempting to buy, or helping another minor get alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.teaching_text: You do not even need to be near a car to lose your driver license for a year over underage alcohol purchases.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.question_text: What happens to an underage person's license if convicted of using or trying to use a fake or borrowed ID for alcohol?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.teaching_text: Flashing an older sibling's card or a fake ID at a store costs twelve months of driving privileges.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.question_text: What license penalty applies to anyone convicted of lending an ID to a minor for alcohol or giving alcohol to someone underage?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.teaching_text: Handing a younger friend your license or buying drinks for minors puts your own driving privilege under a one-year revocation.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.question_text: How does an adult supplier's or ID lender's license revocation compare with the underage buyer's revocation?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.teaching_text: North Carolina hits the adult enabler with the exact same twelve-month revocation imposed on the underage buyer.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.question_text: What license consequence hits a driver under twenty-one convicted of driving with any alcohol or drugs in their body?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.teaching_text: Drivers under twenty-one have zero legal allowance, so even a trace reading triggers a full one-year loss.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.question_text: How long is the driver license revocation when someone younger than twenty-one is convicted of driving with any alcohol or drugs present?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.teaching_text: Never wait for zero point zero eight under twenty-one because any detectable substance revokes your license for twelve months.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: What event places driver license points onto your North Carolina driving record?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Merely getting pulled over adds nothing until an actual conviction for a covered violation posts to your record.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: At what point total may DMV assign you to a driver improvement clinic, and what fee does that clinic charge?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Hitting seven points is your warning bell before twelve-point suspension territory, plus you pay eighty-three dollars and fifty cents.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: How many points are deducted from your driving record when you satisfactorily complete a driver improvement clinic?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Shaving three points off a seven-point record drops you back to four and creates breathing room against suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: Accumulating how many points within a three-year window can suspend your North Carolina driver license?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: A handful of three-point or four-point tickets across three years stacks up fast enough to bench your license.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Once your license is reinstated after a suspension, how many points within three years can trigger a second suspension?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Coming back from a suspension puts you on a tighter leash where just eight points instead of twelve suspends you again.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: Which three point totals mark the driver improvement clinic threshold, a first suspension, and a post-reinstatement suspension?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Keep those three milestones in exact order because test questions love swapping the twelve-point and eight-point caps.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: How long do a first, second, and third point-system license suspension each last?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Each repeat point suspension multiplies your time off the road, jumping from two months to half a year to twelve months.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: What three escalating durations make up North Carolina's adult point-system suspension ladder?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Do not confuse the adult sixty-day starter suspension with the thirty-day starter rule used for provisional teens.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: When your driving privilege is reinstated, what happens to prior driver license points versus insurance points?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Starting fresh at DMV does not erase the separate surcharge points your auto insurer tracks for premiums.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How does point removal from a driver improvement clinic differ from point removal upon post-suspension reinstatement?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: A clinic trims three points before suspension hits, whereas reinstatement clears every prior DMV point after serving a suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: Why can your auto insurance bill stay high even after reinstatement cancels every prior driver license point?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: DMV point cancellation only resets your state licensing ledger while insurance points remain untouched.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: Who runs the separate point system used to set auto insurance rates, and who can explain how it affects you?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: DMV clerks handle licensing records, so questions about policy surcharges belong with your insurance agent.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: Which two violations carry five points—the highest value on North Carolina's regular vehicle point schedule?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Passing a stopped school bus or driving aggressively puts five immediate points on your record in one ticket.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: How many points attach to illegal passing, reckless driving, tailgating, property-damage hit-and-run, or wrong-side driving?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Three convictions from that four-point tier inside three years reach the twelve-point suspension cap on their own.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: How many license points are assessed for failing to yield to a pedestrian, bicycle, motor scooter, or motorcycle?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Unprotected walkers and two-wheel riders face severe injury in collisions, so right-of-way failures carry a heavier four-point hit.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: How many points attach to running a stop sign, running a red light, failing to yield, or speeding above fifty-five?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Everyday intersection and highway speeding mistakes sit in the three-point bracket and stack up faster than drivers expect.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: How many points apply to driving unlicensed or expired over a year, ignoring a siren, entering a safety zone, or lacking insurance?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Skipping liability coverage or ignoring emergency sirens hits your license ledger just as hard as running a red light.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: How many points do you receive for skipping a required crash report or speeding above a posted school-zone limit?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Speeding past school-zone signs or failing to file required crash paperwork puts three points straight onto your record.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: How many points apply to failing to restrain a child properly—and to any other unlisted moving violation?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Even when a moving violation does not appear in the higher brackets, it still adds two baseline points.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: How many license points are added for littering when a motor vehicle is involved?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Tossing trash from a car window is not just a fine because North Carolina posts one license point too.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: How many points are assessed for passing a stopped school bus while driving a commercial motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Passing a stopped school bus in a heavy commercial rig carries eight points—the single highest hit on the schedule.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: Which two violations carry six points when committed in a commercial motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Railroad crossing errors in a long commercial rig risk catastrophic train derailments, earning six points right alongside aggressive driving.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: In a commercial motor vehicle, how many points attach to reckless driving, running a red light, and other moving violations?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Every commercial moving tier steps up one full point higher than the regular passenger-car point schedule.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: How many license points attach to having any alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Carrying even an unopened bottle in a commercial cab lands four license points on top of commercial alcohol bans.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: How do the top commercial schedule values—passing a stopped school bus and rail violations—compare with vehicle littering?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Commercial safety violations soar to eight and six points while vehicle littering stays anchored at one point.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: How many driver license points are added for illegal parking or vehicle overload, overlength, overwidth, and overheight convictions?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Weight-station and parking tickets still cost money, yet non-moving size and curb infractions add zero license points.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: How many license points attach to plate, registration, muffler, emblem, inspection, or concealed-weapon convictions?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Tag, inspection, muffler, and concealed-weapon offenses carry court penalties without adding moving-violation points to your license.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: How high can the fine or statutory penalty climb when a point-carrying offense is committed in a commercial motor vehicle?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Getting cited in a commercial vehicle hits twice as hard financially when courts double the authorized fine.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: Alongside criminal court penalties, what else can certain traffic convictions strip away?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Paying your court fine never shields your wallet from a separate loss of driving privileges at DMV.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Which two twelve-month combinations involving speeding over fifty-five allow DMV to suspend your license?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Even well below twelve total points, two over-fifty-five speeding convictions—or one plus reckless driving—within a year can suspend you.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Does willful racing against another car have to be arranged beforehand for DMV to suspend your license?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Impulse stoplight sprints trigger racing suspensions even when neither driver planned the race ahead of time.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: Under what court-sentence rule or extreme highway speed threshold can DMV also suspend your license?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: Pushing past seventy-five miles per hour or receiving a judge's no-driving condition exposes your license to suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: What license revocation follows driving more than fifteen miles per hour over the limit while going faster than fifty-five?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: One heavy highway ticket meeting both speed conditions revokes your license for at least thirty days on the first strike.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: Which two situations push that high-speed license revocation up to sixty days?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Repeating that high-speed offense inside twelve months—or pairing speeding with reckless driving at once—doubles revocation to sixty days.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: How does a thirty-day high-speed revocation differ from a sixty-day high-speed revocation?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Watch whether the question describes a single highway speeding charge or adds a repeat charge or reckless count.
sec05-card-sec05-R07.must_match_memory_hook: First thirty, repeat or reckless sixty

visual_sync.text_span: First thirty, repeat or reckless sixty

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: How long is the suspension for manslaughter, death by vehicle, or vehicle assault—and how does impaired manslaughter differ?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Adding an impairing substance to vehicular manslaughter escalates a one-year suspension into permanent license loss.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: How does impairment change the license suspension length for vehicular manslaughter?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: Test items contrast those two manslaughter outcomes directly to check that you spot impairment as the permanent trigger.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: What suspension duration applies to failing to stop and render aid after a crash or willfully refusing an alcohol test?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Fleeing an injury scene or refusing chemical testing each carries a full twelve-month suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: What license suspension hits when a driver speeds above fifty-five and at least fifteen over the limit to avoid arrest?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Running from blue lights at highway speed turns a thirty-day speeding issue into a full one-year suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: What suspension applies to two reckless driving charges in twelve months or seeking a permit or license by fraud?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Faking application facts at the counter carries the exact same one-year suspension as stacking two reckless charges.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: What license penalty and vehicle consequence apply to prearranged highway racing—including watching, betting, or lending a car?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Even lending your keys or betting at a planned street race risks a three-year suspension, and the raced car gets seized.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: How does the suspension length for prearranged highway racing compare with most other major table offenses?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Planned racing and helping stage it jump to three full years—triple the standard one-year table penalty.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: What suspension and fine follow failing to yield at an intersection or work zone when it causes serious bodily injury?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: Cutting off traffic in an intersection or construction zone and seriously hurting someone triggers ninety days off the road plus five hundred dollars.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: How soon can DMV suspend after receiving a court conviction report, and where may a revoked driver hold a hearing right?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: Action starts as soon as court records arrive, though eligible drivers can seek a DMV hearing in their home judicial district.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: If a DMV hearing does not go your way, how quickly—and to which court—may you appeal?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Waiting past the thirty-day deadline forfeits your right to challenge the DMV decision in home-county Superior Court.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: What exact two-step sequence applies when a revoked driver challenges a DMV revocation?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: You cannot jump straight into Superior Court without pursuing the administrative DMV hearing step first.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: How can a traffic conviction in another state affect your North Carolina license, and what notice must DMV send?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Crossing state lines never hides a serious ticket because North Carolina treats reported out-of-state convictions as local and mails your effective date.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.question_text: What happens to your license if you miss court or leave a traffic fine unpaid, and how long does that hold last?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: Ignoring a minor ticket snowballs into an indefinite license revocation until the court reports full payment or waiver.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.question_text: Does paying off your overdue traffic citation erase the underlying conviction consequences for the offense itself?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.teaching_text: Settling the clerk's bill lifts the failure-to-pay hold, yet any points or offense suspension from conviction still apply.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.question_text: What form and process can you use if you cannot afford to pay a traffic ticket, and what options does the judge have?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.teaching_text: Speaking up through the county clerk lets a judge reduce the bill, set payments, or waive it before revocation hits.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.question_text: How do you stop an unpaid-ticket suspension when you are able to pay the full amount?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.teaching_text: Paying the county clerk directly triggers an electronic court update to DMV that halts the pending suspension.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: How do the cannot-pay route and the pay-in-full route differ—and what final step do both routes share?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Whether a judge grants relief or you pay the clerk in full, DMV only clears your record once the court reports it.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.question_text: What license suspension hits a provisional licensee under eighteen upon a second moving violation conviction within twelve months?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.teaching_text: Teen provisional holders do not get a twelve-point cushion because two moving convictions in a year suspend them for a month.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.question_text: What suspensions apply when a provisional licensee racks up a third or fourth moving violation conviction within twelve months?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.teaching_text: Continuing to collect moving tickets under eighteen triples the penalty to ninety days and then doubles it to half a year.
sec05-card-sec05-F45.must_match_memory_hook: Ninety days third, six months fourth

visual_sync.text_span: Ninety days third, six months fourth

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: What is the complete three-step suspension ladder for a provisional licensee's repeat moving violations within twelve months?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Test questions try starting that teen suspension ladder on your first ticket, when North Carolina actually triggers it on your second moving conviction.

sec05-card-sec05-F46.question_text: How much is North Carolina's standard restoration fee after a suspension or revocation, and what is the one exception?
sec05-card-sec05-F46.teaching_text: Expect to pay eighty-three dollars and fifty cents to clear a suspension unless your license was pulled solely after a medical evaluation.

sec05-card-sec05-F47.question_text: What restoration fee applies after a DWI revocation, and how can you avoid the extra fifty-dollar service fee?
sec05-card-sec05-F47.teaching_text: Turning in or mailing your physical license before the revocation start date spares you the extra fifty-dollar service charge on top of restoration.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: How does the ordinary restoration fee compare with the DWI restoration fee, and when is the fifty-dollar service fee waived?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: DWI restoration roughly doubles the eighty-three-dollar-fifty-cent base charge, while timely license surrender avoids the fifty-dollar service add-on.

sec05-card-sec05-F48.question_text: What steps must you complete at a driver license office to restore your driving privilege after a suspension?
sec05-card-sec05-F48.teaching_text: Your privilege never switches back on automatically when time expires—you must reapply in person, pass required checks, and pay.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: Why does the distance behind farm machinery shrink much faster than drivers expect?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: At fifty-five miles per hour, you eat up hundreds of feet in seconds behind a fifteen-mile-per-hour tractor.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: On which North Carolina roadways is farm equipment legally prohibited?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: Expect legal farm tractors on rural highways and secondary roads, yet never on controlled-access interstates.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Which lights must every vehicle participating in a funeral procession turn on?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Shining headlights and four-way flashers mark every car in the cortege so cross traffic recognizes the continuous line.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: How does the lead car of a funeral procession handle signals, and when may following cars continue without stopping?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Once the lead car crosses legally—or police or a director guides it—trailing cars continue carefully even if lights turn red.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: Where on the roadway and at what spacing do vehicles inside a funeral procession travel?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Staying right and keeping a tight, prudent gap keeps outside drivers from mistaking a break for an opening.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Must oncoming traffic yield to a funeral procession, and how must you act if you choose to yield?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Stopping halfway in an oncoming lane traps drivers behind you; either slow gently or pull completely off the pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: When is a driver traveling in the same direction allowed to pass a funeral procession?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Passing a funeral line on a single-lane directional road is illegal; wait unless two marked lanes go its way.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: How do funeral-procession rules differ between oncoming drivers and same-direction drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Oncoming motorists choose whether to yield, whereas same-direction motorists cannot pass without at least two lanes their way.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: What two intersection and gap mistakes must outside drivers avoid around a funeral procession?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Even facing a green light, wait at the stop bar until the continuous funeral line clears your path.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: Who continues and who waits when a funeral procession is still crossing an intersection after the light changes?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: A fresh green light does not let cross traffic slice through a funeral line whose lead car entered legally.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: Which side of the road must you drive on by law, and when is the left half legal?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: Keeping right separates opposing streams of traffic except during legal passes or on designated one-way streets.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Which lane must you use on a multi-lane highway when driving slower than the posted speed limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Camping below the speed limit in left lanes triggers aggressive tailgating and risky right-side passes.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: How do legal left-side exceptions pair with multi-lane positioning for slower drivers?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Save the left side for passing or one-way streets, and tuck into the far-right lane whenever moving below posted speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: Which two factors combine to determine total stopping distance, and how does higher speed affect both?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: Going faster stretches both the ground covered before your foot hits the brake and the braking roll afterward.

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: Roughly how many feet does a car traveling fifty-five miles per hour need to stop under ideal conditions?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Two hundred eleven feet is over two-thirds of a football field—and wet pavement stretches it even farther.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: What does every added mile per hour do to vehicle control and crash survival odds?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Crash energy climbs rapidly with speed, shrinking steering margin while multiplying severe injury and death risk.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: How must your forward sight distance adjust as your travel speed climbs?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: Looking only at the bumper ahead leaves zero stopping room once highway speeds stretch your braking zone.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Is creeping far below the speed limit safe, and what sign must slow drivers still obey?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Crawling unexpectedly on fast highways invites rear-end collisions, so never dip below a posted minimum limit.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: At which two road features is driving very slowly especially dangerous?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Cresting a hill or rounding a blind bend at a crawl surprises full-speed drivers before they can brake.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What wise move should you make when a queue of vehicles builds up behind your slower pace?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Pulling safely off and stopping clears frustrated tailgaters before someone attempts a reckless blind pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: What do traffic studies cited in the handbook reveal about cars moving far below the posted speed limit?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Big speed gaps disrupt traffic flow, making extreme slowpokes far likelier to trigger or suffer collisions.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: Given the dangers of both speeding and crawling, how should you choose your travel speed?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Stay within posted bounds while tuning your exact pace to weather, visibility, and surrounding traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: Which two ceilings may your driving speed never exceed?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Driving the posted fifty-five during a blinding downpour still breaks the basic reasonable-and-wise speed rule.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Does safe driving ever call for going below the posted limit—or above it?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Rain, fog, or heavy traffic frequently demand dropping below the sign, while nothing justifies exceeding it.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: What is North Carolina's unposted default speed limit inside cities and towns?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: When no speed sign appears on a town street, hold thirty-five miles per hour or less.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: How does the maximum speed for a regular school bus compare with a school activity bus?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Test writers love swapping these two buses—yellow route buses cap at forty-five, while activity buses reach fifty-five.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: What are North Carolina's maximum speeds outside municipalities and on interstate highways?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Unposted country roads top out at fifty-five, while signed interstate corridors allow up to seventy.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: How does the default town speed limit compare with North Carolina's top interstate limit?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Interstates double the unposted thirty-five-mile-per-hour town limit because controlled ramps eliminate driveways and crosswalks.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: Which two categories share the fifty-five-mile-per-hour maximum, and which bus stays ten slower?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Pairing rural roads with activity buses at fifty-five keeps the forty-five-mile-per-hour route bus distinct on exam day.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: When do you slow for a curve, and what do you do with the gas through the bend?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Shedding speed on the straight approach avoids mid-curve braking skids, while gentle throttle keeps tires planted.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: How should you apply the brake pedal if you have no choice but to brake inside a curve?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Stabbing the brakes mid-bend unloads rear traction and spins the car; press gently before holding steady pressure.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Why does curve slowing belong before the bend rather than by braking inside it?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Tires turning hard already fight sideways force, so finish slowing early and feed gentle power through the arc.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: At what point do you begin steering for a curve, and where in your lane do you stay?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Starting your turn-in slightly early and hugging the right edge keeps you clear of oncoming centerline drifters.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: How do gravity, gear choice, and brake timing change when approaching a downhill curve?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Gravity pushes your car faster down the grade, so drop a gear beforehand and brake sooner and gentler than on flat pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: When must downshifting and initial braking happen on a downhill curve compared with flat road?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Waiting until you are already plunging into a downhill bend overheats brakes and overloads front-tire grip.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Where should you position your vehicle and how should you pace speed through a right turn?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Swinging wide left before turning right invites cyclists or impatient cars to wedge inside your right flank.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: Which two road users are hardest to spot during turns, making signaling and scanning vital?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Slim two-wheelers vanish behind windshield pillars and mirrors right when drivers cut across lanes or turn.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: Why is tailgating dangerous, and what space benchmark applies on the open highway?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Bumper-to-bumper packs trap overtaking cars in the oncoming lane; leave space so a passer can tuck in safely.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: How do you count out North Carolina's two-second following-distance rule?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Pick a shadow or sign ahead; reaching it fewer than two seconds after the lead bumper means you are tailgating.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: How does the two-second rule's purpose differ from scanning farther ahead as speed climbs?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Two seconds spaces you from the bumper directly ahead, while scanning farther downroad matches growing stopping distance.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: On a highway with three or more lanes, which extra lane must you check before changing lanes?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Two cars converging from opposite sides into the same middle lane collide unless someone checks two lanes over.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What four-step sequence completes a safe lane change?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Mirrors leave side blind spots wide enough to hide a sedan, so always glance over your shoulder before moving.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: Why isn't checking only your target lane enough on a multi-lane road?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Scanning one lane farther catches another driver diving toward that exact same empty pocket at the same instant.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: What three checks and warnings come in order before you pull out to pass another vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Skipping the mirror check, blinker, or horn tap surprises both trailing drivers and the car ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: What legal duty does sounding your horn place on the driver you are starting to pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Once you sound the horn to pass in North Carolina, state law requires the overtaken driver to help you clear.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: What space, pace, and sightline conditions must exist before starting any pass?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Never gamble on squeezing back in late; see enough open road to return cleanly before meeting oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: At least how far to the left must a passing vehicle stay from the vehicle being overtaken?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: Shaving closer than two feet risks mirror strikes or wind-buffet sideswipes if either car drifts slightly.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: At which three crossing or junction types is passing never safe and generally illegal?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Trains, cross-street cars, or sudden left turners at tracks and town or marked rural intersections trap passers.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: What minimum forward sight distance is required to pass on a curve or hill?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Oncoming highway traffic closes five hundred feet in mere seconds, turning blind crests and bends into head-on traps.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: Which yellow pavement-line setups prohibit passing?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Whether doubled across the center or paired with dashes opposite you, solid yellow in your lane forbids passing.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: How does legal side clearance while passing compare with minimum sight distance on hills and curves?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Pair two feet with lateral side buffer and five hundred feet with forward sightline so test numbers stay untangled.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: How must you cooperate when another driver signals with the horn and passes you?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Moving toward the right edge opens safe lane width, while accelerating traps the passer in oncoming danger.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: When does speeding up and refusing to yield to a passing vehicle become a criminal misdemeanor?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Racing someone trying to pass turns into a misdemeanor charge the moment injury or property damage results.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: How do the passing driver's horn-and-signal duties pair with the overtaken driver's response?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: One driver signals and taps the horn to announce the pass while the other eases right without accelerating.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Why does North Carolina generally ban passing on the right?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Drivers expect overtakes on the left and may suddenly turn right or pull onto the shoulder into you.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: In which four roadway or lane situations is passing on the right permitted?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Marked multi-lane corridors, one-way streets, waiting left turners, and dedicated right-turn lanes make right-side movement predictable.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: When may you pass in the middle lane of a three-lane highway, and what blocks it?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Use a three-lane road's center lane only where markings allow passing your direction and nobody sits turning left.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: Is passing on the right always illegal, or which specific exceptions apply?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Treat right-side passing as illegal everywhere except multi-lane highways, one-way streets, past left turners, or right-turn lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: On which side of a two-way street must you always park, and what street type is the exception?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: Parking facing backward on the left curb forces you to cross opposing traffic both arriving and leaving.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: What check and turn signal are required before pulling out of a right-curb parallel space—and when isn't left signaled?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Signal left after checking traffic when leaving a right curb, though left-curb parking on one-way streets skips left signaling.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: Which five everyday street or crossing locations completely forbid parking?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Blocking intersections, driveways, crosswalks, sidewalks, or narrow bridges traps pedestrians and chokes emergency sightlines.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: How far back must you park from a cross-street curb line versus curbless intersecting right-of-way lines?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Keep twenty-five feet clear of a cross-street curb—or fifteen feet from intersecting right-of-way lines where curbs are absent.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: Within how many feet is parking prohibited near a fire hydrant or fire-station entrance?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Fire crews need fifteen feet of open curb to hook heavy supply hoses and swing wide apparatus doors.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: How does the fire-hydrant no-parking distance compare with curbed and uncurbed cross-street corners?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Hydrants and curbless right-of-way corners share fifteen feet, while curbed cross streets stretch out to twenty-five feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: May you park on highway pavement, and what visibility distance makes shoulder parking legal?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Never park on paved travel lanes, and skip blind shoulders unless approaching drivers both ways see you from two hundred feet.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: How far away from a fire or fire truck must you park inside city limits versus outside town?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: City blocks mark urban fire perimeters cleanly, while rural roads lacking blocks enforce a four-hundred-foot buffer.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How do city and rural fire-parking buffers contrast with the highway-shoulder visibility requirement?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Keep four hundred feet for rural fires separate from the two-hundred-foot two-way sightline required on highway shoulders.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: When is parking allowed anywhere within an interstate right of way?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: High-speed interstate shoulders are breakdown lifelines, not rest stops for phone calls or map checks.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: What must a vehicle display to legally use a disabled parking space?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Even quick two-minute errands in accessible stalls are illegal without a valid disability plate or hanging placard.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: What check should you make outside the car before climbing in to back up?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Toddlers, pets, and low toys sit completely below rear-window sightlines once you settle into the driver's seat.

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: Which hand steers and where should you look while backing a vehicle?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Mirrors and side windows leave huge reverse blind zones; grip with your left hand and look out the back glass.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: What is the top safe speed when backing up, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Front-wheel steering geometry makes cars twitchy and harder to stop in reverse, capping safe backing at ten.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: Which speed cap and viewing habit work together whenever you reverse?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Keeping reverse at ten miles per hour or slower while turning over your right shoulder prevents driveway and lot collisions.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Where do crashes happen most frequently, and what share of fatal wrecks occur there?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Crossing paths and turning conflicts pack more than one-third of all fatal crashes into intersections.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: How wide must a median be on a four-lane divided highway for each roadway crossing to count as a separate intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Once a dividing median exceeds thirty feet wide, treat the second set of lanes as a brand-new intersection.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: What speed adjustment does North Carolina law require approaching an intersection—even when right of way is yours?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Easing off the gas before every cross street buys braking margin when another driver blows a sign.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: Does holding the right of way excuse you from slowing for an intersection or avoiding a crash?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Right of way decides order, never permission to plow ahead; slow down approaching corners and avoid hitting anyone.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: At an intersection without signs or signals, how does a car already inside compare with an approaching car?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Approaching an unmarked cross street never lets you crowd a driver who has already entered the intersection box.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: When two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the exact same moment, who holds the right of way?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Break simultaneous ties at unsigned corners by yielding to whichever driver sits on your right-hand side.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: When two opposing vehicles arrive together and one signals a left turn, who goes first?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Turning left cuts directly across oncoming lanes, so signal and wait until straight-through traffic clears.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: How do first-in, tie-on-right, and straight-versus-left rules stack at an uncontrolled intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Clear vehicles already inside first, yield simultaneous cross ties to the right, and hold left turns for oncoming straight cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: Is changing lanes permitted while driving straight through an intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Right-on-red turners and opposing drivers count on you holding your entry lane all the way across.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: What two actions are mandatory at every stop sign before proceeding or turning?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Stopping briefly is only half the rule; stay put until cross-street vehicles with priority pass safely.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: How should you exit a private driveway, and how do you handle a blind unmarked intersection?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: Emerging from driveways yields to every walker and car, while blind unmarked corners need a stop before creeping out.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: How does a single-point interchange organize ramps and traffic signals?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Combining both ramp junctions into one central deck above or below the freeway clears opposing left turns under one signal set.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: How does a modern roundabout compare in size and speed with an older traffic circle?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Tighter geometry holds circulating cars around fifteen to twenty miles per hour, slashing severe T-bone crash angles.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: Which direction do cars flow in a traffic circle, and from which lane must you exit multi-lane circles?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Cutting right toward an exit from an inner circle lane slices straight across drivers circulating beside you.

sec09-card-sec09-F37.question_text: How many intersections does a traffic circle count as, and which vehicles hold right of way?
sec09-card-sec09-F37.teaching_text: Treating the entire ring as one intersection keeps circulating traffic flowing while entry ramps wait for gaps.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: In a traffic circle, how do entry priority and exit-lane rules work together?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Wait for circulating cars before entering, then move into the outer ring early so you exit right cleanly.

sec09-card-sec09-F38.question_text: What does a yellow roundabout-ahead warning sign tell you, and to whom do you yield at entry?
sec09-card-sec09-F38.teaching_text: Ease off speed early and yield at the dashed entry line to both vehicles and bicyclists already circulating.

sec09-card-sec09-F39.question_text: Do drivers circulating inside a roundabout stop for entering cars, and what two steps apply when exiting?
sec09-card-sec09-F39.teaching_text: Stopping mid-ring causes rear-end pileups; keep circulating, signal your exit, and yield to crosswalk pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: How do yielding duties differ between drivers entering a roundabout and drivers exiting one?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Entering cars wait for circulating vehicles and bikes, while circulating cars keep priority until yielding to exit-crosswalk walkers.

sec09-card-sec09-F40.question_text: How far around a single-lane roundabout do you travel for a right turn, straight path, left turn, or U-turn?
sec09-card-sec09-F40.teaching_text: Picture a clock face counterclockwise—one-quarter turns right, halfway goes straight, three-quarters turns left, full loop U-turns.

sec09-card-sec09-F41.question_text: When and how do you pick lanes for a multi-lane roundabout, and may you switch lanes inside?
sec09-card-sec09-F41.teaching_text: Follow approach signs early—normally right lane for right turns, left lane for straight, left, or U-turns—and hold your lane.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: How does making a left turn work in a single-lane roundabout versus a multi-lane roundabout?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Single-lane loops carry you three-quarters around, while multi-lane setups typically start in the left entry lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F42.question_text: How should you respond to an emergency vehicle at a roundabout before entering versus once already inside?
sec09-card-sec09-F42.teaching_text: Stopping inside the narrow curved ring blocks fire trucks completely—finish exiting first, then pull right and stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F43.question_text: How should drivers treat bicyclists inside a roundabout, and where must pedestrians cross?
sec09-card-sec09-F43.teaching_text: Cyclists often take the full lane through narrow rings, and walkers belong on perimeter crosswalks—never across the center island.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.question_text: What must you hold to legally drive on North Carolina public streets and highways, and how does the law view driving?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.teaching_text: Treating driving like an automatic right instead of an earned legal privilege is the fastest way to lose your credential.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.question_text: Even without driving down the road, which two behind-the-wheel actions are illegal if you lack a valid license?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.teaching_text: Sitting in the driver seat with the motor idling or steering a pushed or towed car still counts as unlawful operation.

sec01-card-sec01-F05.question_text: Who is eligible by age to get a regular North Carolina learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.teaching_text: Applicants under eighteen follow graduated provisional rules instead, while adults eighteen and up qualify for a regular permit.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.question_text: Which vehicles may a learner permit holder operate, and what possession rule applies every time they drive?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.teaching_text: Leaving your permit at home makes the trip unlawful even if you passed every test for that vehicle class.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.question_text: Who must ride along when a learner permit holder drives on the highway, and which seat must they occupy?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.teaching_text: Tucking your licensed adult into the back seat violates permit supervision law because they cannot intervene quickly.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.question_text: What two conditions must your highway companion meet whenever you drive on a learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.teaching_text: Test questions try to trick you with a licensed rider in the rear row or someone licensed for a different class.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.question_text: Which three checks or exams must you pass to earn a North Carolina learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.teaching_text: Permit testing checks your eyesight, sign recognition, and traffic law knowledge before you ever practice on public roads.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.question_text: Which four areas may an applicant for any original North Carolina driver license be tested on?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.teaching_text: Moving from study to a full original license adds behind-the-wheel skill evaluation on top of the three office checks.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.question_text: How are North Carolina driver license tests scored — can acing one exam offset failing another?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.teaching_text: A perfect score on traffic laws will never rescue a failed road-sign check because each exam stands alone.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.question_text: How does the test lineup for an original driver license go beyond the three learner permit tests?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.teaching_text: Both applicants face vision, signs, and law checks, leaving the on-road driving skill test as the key separator.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.question_text: How must you identify each sign on the traffic signs test, and where can every tested sign be found?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.teaching_text: Words may be blanked out on sign prompts, so memorizing shapes and colors from the handbook is essential.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.question_text: What two subjects does the knowledge test cover, and what accommodation is available if reading is difficult?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.teaching_text: Struggling readers can ask for the spoken version so reading speed never blocks someone who knows safe driving rules.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.question_text: What separates the traffic signs test from the knowledge test at the license office?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.teaching_text: Mixing these two exams up leads applicants to study rules while ignoring blank sign shapes and colors.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.question_text: During which in-person licensing visits does North Carolina check your vision?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.teaching_text: Eyesight changes over time, so examiners screen vision at in-person permit, first-time license, and renewal appointments alike.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.question_text: If you need glasses or contacts to pass the vision check, what goes on your license and when must you wear them?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.teaching_text: Passing the eye chart with contacts or glasses locks a mandatory lens restriction onto every future trip you take.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.question_text: How severely does North Carolina punish driving without the corrective lenses required on your license?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.teaching_text: Leaving required glasses on your dresser is prosecuted just like driving with zero license at all.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.question_text: Why is violating a corrective-lens restriction far worse than a minor equipment ticket?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.teaching_text: Written tests love offering a minor fix-it ticket distractor, whereas the law treats unassisted driving as completely unlicensed.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.question_text: How do mental or physical conditions affect licensing — when is a license denied versus issued with restrictions?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.teaching_text: Examiners evaluate actual road safety rather than blanket labels, denying unsafe conditions while tailoring restricted licenses when safe.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.question_text: Does having a disability automatically bar someone from getting a North Carolina license?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.teaching_text: Only an inability to operate safely blocks licensing, whereas adaptive gear or tailored restrictions keep safe drivers mobile.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.question_text: Where does the on-road driving test fall in the testing sequence, and how does it apply to permits, first licenses, and renewals?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.teaching_text: You must clear vision, signs, and knowledge checks before an examiner ever rides along in traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.question_text: Compare whether an on-road test is required for a learner permit, a first license, and a license renewal?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.teaching_text: Sorting those three cases cleanly prevents test-day confusion between mandatory first-time road exams and discretionary renewal checks.
sec01-card-sec01-R04.must_match_memory_hook: Permit never, first yes, renewal maybe

visual_sync.text_span: Permit never, first yes, renewal maybe

sec01-card-sec01-F22.question_text: What is the general rule on taking the on-road test for original license applicants, and is it absolute?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.teaching_text: Expect to drive for an examiner on an original application unless your situation fits a specific handbook exception.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.question_text: What two broad abilities do you demonstrate to the examiner during the on-road driving test?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.teaching_text: Examiners watch both low-speed car control maneuvers and real-time judgment around live traffic.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.question_text: From intersections and quick stops to posture and turnabouts, which driving skills and habits do road-test examiners grade?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.teaching_text: Examiners score everyday habits like posture, horn or clutch control, lane discipline, and yielding alongside maneuvers like backing.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.question_text: What kind of vehicle must you bring and drive for your driving skills test?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.teaching_text: Showing up in a compact car cannot prove you can handle a heavier class of vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.question_text: Starting at the far right edge, what actions make up step one of a three-point turnabout?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.teaching_text: Stopping a few inches before the left curb keeps your front tires off the shoulder so step two stays crisp.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.question_text: Which way do you move and turn the wheel during step two of a three-point turnabout, and where do you stop?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.teaching_text: Halting several inches short of the right edge prevents backing into ditches or scraping the rear bumper on curbs.

sec01-card-sec01-F31.question_text: How do you complete step three of a three-point turnabout?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.teaching_text: Rolling ahead smoothly with left steering straightens the car cleanly into your new travel lane.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.question_text: Across all three moves of a three-point turnabout, which direction does the steering wheel turn on each leg?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.teaching_text: Both forward legs steer left while the middle reverse leg steers right, making the pattern effortless under exam pressure.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.question_text: What two broad license categories does North Carolina issue, and what determines the class you need?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.teaching_text: Your license class depends on the weight, configuration, and purpose of the vehicle you plan to operate.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.question_text: Which regular license class covers everyday personal cars and small trucks for most North Carolina drivers?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.teaching_text: Unless you haul heavy noncommercial rigs or drive commercial vehicles, regular Class C handles daily personal driving.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.question_text: What weight ratings and driver age rule define the vehicles covered by a regular Class C license?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.teaching_text: Towing combinations staying below that weight ceiling also require the Class C driver to be at least eighteen.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.question_text: Since both regular and commercial licenses use Classes A, B, and C, which specific credential is the ordinary everyday car license?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.teaching_text: Confusing commercial Class C with regular Class C is a classic exam trap when both systems share letter names.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.question_text: Which CDL-exempt vehicle combination requires a regular Class A license?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.teaching_text: When a non-CDL combination pulls a trailer rated ten thousand one pounds or heavier, regular Class C is no longer enough.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.question_text: What CDL-exempt single vehicle — and optional towed weight — falls under a regular Class B license?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.teaching_text: Single CDL-exempt rigs rated twenty-six thousand one pounds or more stay in Class B provided any trailer stays ten thousand pounds or under.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.question_text: How does the weight threshold that triggers a regular Class A license differ from the one for regular Class B?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.teaching_text: Class A hinges on a towed unit at ten thousand one pounds or more, whereas Class B hinges on a heavy single vehicle.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.question_text: Which separate handbooks must commercial license applicants and motorcycle applicants study?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.teaching_text: Standard car rules alone will not prepare you for air brakes, cargo endorsements, or two-wheeled lane positioning.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.question_text: Does being an unpaid volunteer excuse a driver from holding a commercial driver license for listed passenger or property vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.teaching_text: Unless a specific statutory exemption applies, driving commercial-grade passenger or cargo rigs requires a CDL even without pay.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.question_text: What two minimum weight ratings define a commercial Class A combination vehicle?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.teaching_text: Both thresholds must hit at least twenty-six thousand one pounds combined and at least ten thousand one pounds towed.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.question_text: Which single vehicles or towing combinations count as commercial Class B vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.teaching_text: Once the single or towing unit hits twenty-six thousand one pounds while any trailer stays under ten thousand one pounds, it is Class B.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.question_text: Outside Classes A and B, what two passenger or cargo features make a vehicle commercial Class C?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.teaching_text: Always count the driver inside that sixteen-person seating capacity when spotting a commercial Class C van or bus.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.question_text: Why isn't a commercial Class C vehicle defined by heavy weight alone?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.teaching_text: Smaller shuttle vans or trucks still require a commercial Class C license whenever they carry sixteen people or placarded hazmat.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.question_text: Which four vehicle categories are exempt from needing a CDL, and what license must their drivers still hold?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.teaching_text: Driving a heavy RV, farm truck, military rig, or fire apparatus skips the CDL but still demands the matching regular class.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.question_text: Which license allows on-duty volunteer fire, rescue, or EMS members to operate Class A, B, or C emergency vehicles?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.teaching_text: On-duty volunteer responders can drive heavy emergency rigs using their matching regular A, B, or C license without a CDL.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.question_text: Which five commercial hauling or passenger operations each require a special CDL endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.teaching_text: Liquid surge, articulated trailers, hazardous loads, and passenger evacuation each demand extra endorsement testing beyond a base CDL.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.question_text: What two credential options legally allow someone to ride a motorcycle on North Carolina public roads?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.teaching_text: A plain car license never covers two-wheeled riding unless you hold a standalone motorcycle permit or add a motorcycle endorsement.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.question_text: What existing license — and signature if under eighteen — must an applicant already have to get a motorcycle learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.teaching_text: Sixteen- and seventeen-year-olds need both a full provisional license and parental signature, while adults need a division license.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.question_text: How does a motorcycle endorsement differ structurally from a motorcycle learner permit?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.teaching_text: Both let you ride on public roads, yet an endorsement rides on your existing license while a learner permit is separate.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.question_text: What age, experience, CDL, and certificate rules apply to school bus drivers, and how do activity bus drivers differ?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.teaching_text: Activity bus drivers meet the exact same age, experience, and passenger-bus CDL endorsements while skipping the separate certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.question_text: What single credential requirement separates a regular school bus driver from a school activity bus driver?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.teaching_text: Activity bus drivers still need the exact same age, experience, and S and P CDL endorsements, just without the School Bus Driver's Certificate.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.question_text: Who is permanently barred by North Carolina statute from receiving or renewing a CDL with a P or S endorsement?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.teaching_text: State law blocks the division from issuing or renewing passenger or school bus CDL endorsements to anyone required to register as a sex offender.

sec15-card-sec15-F01.question_text: What two visual features let you recognize highway signs instantly, and what are the three sign groups?
sec15-card-sec15-F01.teaching_text: Even through fog, glare, or snow, outlines and colors reveal regulatory, warning, or guide meanings far ahead.

sec15-card-sec15-F02.question_text: Which single traffic sign uses an eight-sided octagon, and what colors appear on it?
sec15-card-sec15-F02.teaching_text: Reserving the octagon for red-and-white stop controls lets drivers recognize a required stop even from behind.

sec15-card-sec15-F03.question_text: How far ahead of an intersection does a stop sign typically stand, and what must you do?
sec15-card-sec15-F03.teaching_text: Rolling through slowly never counts because state law demands a complete stop at every stop-controlled corner.

sec15-card-sec15-F04.question_text: Once you make a complete stop at a stop sign, when may you pull forward?
sec15-card-sec15-F04.teaching_text: Pulling out on guesswork after a quick pause causes broadside collisions with cross-street cars or walkers.

sec15-card-sec15-F05.question_text: Where must you bring your vehicle to a halt when a required stop has no painted line or crosswalk?
sec15-card-sec15-F05.teaching_text: Stopping before entering the cross street where sightlines open keeps your bumper out of crossing lanes.

sec15-card-sec15-F06.question_text: What colors and shape identify a yield sign, and what action does it require?
sec15-card-sec15-F06.teaching_text: An inverted triangle stands out instantly so drivers ease off the gas and surrender right of way.

sec15-card-sec15-F07.question_text: When are you required to come to a complete stop at a yield sign?
sec15-card-sec15-F07.teaching_text: Forcing cross-street vehicles to brake for your merge violates right of way, so stop and wait whenever needed.

sec15-card-sec15-R01.question_text: How does your legal obligation at a stop sign differ from your obligation at a yield sign?
sec15-card-sec15-R01.teaching_text: Empty roads never excuse rolling a stop control, whereas an open yield approach lets you merge smoothly.

sec15-card-sec15-R02.question_text: Which distinct geometric outlines belong exclusively to stop signs versus yield signs?
sec15-card-sec15-R02.teaching_text: Unique silhouettes let you read cross-street priority from the back side of another driver's post.

sec15-card-sec15-F08.question_text: What colors and messages appear on rectangular or square regulatory signs, and what if you ignore one?
sec15-card-sec15-F08.teaching_text: Speed caps and turn bans on black-and-white or red-and-white rectangles carry full traffic-ticket penalties.

sec15-card-sec15-F09.question_text: Who is legally allowed to park in a stall marked by a handicap parking sign?
sec15-card-sec15-F09.teaching_text: Even quick errands in reserved accessible spaces block people who rely on wide access aisles.

sec15-card-sec15-F10.question_text: Which side of the highway holds the yellow pennant sign, and what zone does it mark?
sec15-card-sec15-F10.teaching_text: Mounted on the left shoulder where peeking passers look, the pennant backs up right-side passing bans.

sec15-card-sec15-R04.question_text: How does the yellow left-side pennant work alongside the rectangular DO NOT PASS sign?
sec15-card-sec15-R04.teaching_text: Even if a truck hides the right-shoulder rectangle, the left-side yellow pennant flags the passing ban.

sec15-card-sec15-F11.question_text: What message type and standard color scheme belong to diamond-shaped signs?
sec15-card-sec15-F11.teaching_text: Spotting a yellow diamond early gives you room to ease speed before curves, merges, or hazards arrive.

sec15-card-sec15-F12.question_text: What hazard ahead is signaled by a diamond sign painted black on orange?
sec15-card-sec15-F12.teaching_text: Construction and maintenance crews work feet from live lanes, demanding extra alertness and slower speeds.

sec15-card-sec15-R03.question_text: What changes in meaning when a warning diamond shifts from yellow to orange?
sec15-card-sec15-R03.teaching_text: Color flips the hazard context from everyday roadway geometry to active construction or maintenance crews.

sec15-card-sec15-F13.question_text: Why do highway crews place a STOP AHEAD warning sign well upstream of certain intersections?
sec15-card-sec15-F13.teaching_text: Curves, trees, or crests can hide an upcoming octagon until braking distance would be too short.

sec15-card-sec15-F14.question_text: What does a round yellow sign bearing a black X and RR warn you to do?
sec15-card-sec15-F14.teaching_text: Slowing early before rails gives you room to stop cleanly if a train comes into view.

sec15-card-sec15-F15.question_text: What colors and exact words appear on the crossbuck standing right at railroad tracks?
sec15-card-sec15-F15.teaching_text: White X-shaped blades mark the exact location of the rails right ahead of your bumper.

sec15-card-sec15-R05.question_text: How do the round yellow RR sign and the white crossbuck differ in where they stand?
sec15-card-sec15-R05.teaching_text: Knowing which marker gives advance notice versus trackside location is a favorite North Carolina sign question.

sec15-card-sec15-F16.question_text: After stopping for a train signal, lowered gate, or flagger, when is it legal to cross?
sec15-card-sec15-F16.teaching_text: Dodging around gates right after one train clears can put you straight into a second train on parallel tracks.

sec15-card-sec15-F17.question_text: How many times should you look each way before driving across railroad tracks?
sec15-card-sec15-F17.teaching_text: A second glance catches fast-moving trains that a cab post or trees hid on your first check.

sec15-card-sec15-F27.question_text: What absolute rule does the DO NOT STOP ON TRACKS reminder enforce?
sec15-card-sec15-F27.teaching_text: Queuing onto rails behind backed-up traffic leaves nowhere to escape if crossing bells start ringing.

sec15-card-sec15-F18.question_text: What zone or crossing does a five-sided pentagon sign warn about?
sec15-card-sec15-F18.teaching_text: Shaped like an old schoolhouse roof, the pentagon cues instant scanning for children near the street.

sec15-card-sec15-F19.question_text: How do speed limits typically change inside many school zones?
sec15-card-sec15-F19.teaching_text: Arrival and dismissal windows pack sidewalks with kids, so posted hours drop legal speeds sharply.

sec15-card-sec15-R06.question_text: Which two school areas use the five-sided pentagon, and whom must you watch for?
sec15-card-sec15-R06.teaching_text: Test questions often pair five-sided outlines against octagons or diamonds to check instant shape recall.

sec15-card-sec15-F20.question_text: What four kinds of helpful travel details do guide and informational signs provide?
sec15-card-sec15-F20.teaching_text: Reading advance guide boards early lets you pick the right lane smoothly without last-second swerves.

sec15-card-sec15-F21.question_text: Which compass directions generally match odd-numbered highways versus even-numbered highways?
sec15-card-sec15-F21.teaching_text: Checking whether a route number is odd or even orients you fast without touching a phone map.

sec15-card-sec15-R08.question_text: How can you tell a north-south highway from an east-west highway by its route number?
sec15-card-sec15-R08.teaching_text: Highway questions love flipping route numbers, where odd routes travel north-south and even routes travel east-west.

sec15-card-sec15-F22.question_text: How does the shape of a U.S. highway marker differ from a North Carolina state route marker?
sec15-card-sec15-F22.teaching_text: North Carolina uniquely frames numbered state highways inside a diamond while U.S. routes wear a shield.

sec15-card-sec15-F23.question_text: What shape marks North Carolina secondary roads, and what emblem marks interstate highways?
sec15-card-sec15-F23.teaching_text: Recognizing secondary rectangles versus tri-color interstate shields prevents accidentally turning onto local backroads or expressways.

sec15-card-sec15-R07.question_text: How do U.S. routes, interstates, and North Carolina state routes differ in shape and color?
sec15-card-sec15-R07.teaching_text: Interstates add red-white-and-blue to the shield, U.S. routes use plain shields, and state routes use diamonds.

sec15-card-sec15-F24.question_text: Which three emergency or help locations can blue-and-white roadside signs point toward?
sec15-card-sec15-F24.teaching_text: In unfamiliar areas, blue motorist-service panels guide you straight to medical care or troopers.

sec15-card-sec15-F25.question_text: Which three background colors are used on rectangular guide signs showing directions and distances?
sec15-card-sec15-F25.teaching_text: Green points to exits and cities, brown marks parks and historic sites, and blue highlights services.

sec15-card-sec15-F26.question_text: What should you do instead of stopping in a travel lane to puzzle over a road sign?
sec15-card-sec15-F26.teaching_text: Braking to a halt mid-roadway to figure out directions invites a high-speed rear-end crash.

sec15-card-sec15-F28.question_text: How do yellow pavement lines and white pavement lines differ in the traffic directions they separate?
sec15-card-sec15-F28.teaching_text: One glance at lane paint tells you whether neighboring cars are coming head-on or flowing alongside you.

sec15-card-sec15-R09.question_text: Which lane-line color separates opposing traffic, and which separates traffic moving together?
sec15-card-sec15-R09.teaching_text: Mixing up white and yellow on a multi-lane street can trick a driver into turning into oncoming lanes.

sec15-card-sec15-F29.question_text: What passing rule applies along a single broken yellow center line on a two-lane, two-way road?
sec15-card-sec15-F29.teaching_text: Dashed yellow paint permits passing from either side only when sightlines and oncoming gaps are completely safe.

sec15-card-sec15-F30.question_text: What passing rule applies across double solid yellow center lines?
sec15-card-sec15-F30.teaching_text: Curves, hills, or short sight distances make crossing double yellow stripes for passing illegal both ways.

sec15-card-sec15-F31.question_text: When a broken yellow stripe pairs with a solid yellow stripe, when may you pass with care?
sec15-card-sec15-F31.teaching_text: Only the lane bordering the dashed stripe has enough forward visibility to overtake safely.

sec15-card-sec15-R10.question_text: How does a broken yellow line on your side differ from double solid yellow lines?
sec15-card-sec15-R10.teaching_text: Read the stripe closest to your left tire first before ever pulling out to overtake.

sec15-card-sec15-F32.question_text: Which edge of a divided highway gets a solid white stripe, and which edge gets a solid yellow stripe?
sec15-card-sec15-F32.teaching_text: Consistent edge colors frame your travel corridor clearly on dark, rainy divided highways.
