sec15-card-sec15-F33.question_text: What does it mean if you look down and see the white edge line on your left and yellow on your right?
sec15-card-sec15-F33.teaching_text: Flipped edge stripes are an urgent red-alert clue that you entered a ramp or divided roadway backward.

sec15-card-sec15-F34.question_text: What is a center two-way left-turn lane strictly reserved for, and what two moves are banned in it?
sec15-card-sec15-F34.teaching_text: Using a shared center turn lane to overtake or merge sets up head-on collisions with opposing left turners.

sec15-card-sec15-F35.question_text: How do white and yellow reflective road markers help on wet nights, and what do red ones warn?
sec15-card-sec15-F35.teaching_text: Rain drowns flat paint at night, so raised reflectors guide lanes while glowing red studs stop wrong-way entry.

sec15-card-sec15-F36.question_text: What do raised blue reflective markers in the pavement point out?
sec15-card-sec15-F36.teaching_text: Fire crews arriving in smoke or darkness spot blue road studs fast to hook up water lines.

sec15-card-sec15-R11.question_text: How does the meaning of red reflective pavement markers differ from blue ones?
sec15-card-sec15-R11.teaching_text: Mixing up specialty reflectors is costly because red flags wrong-way danger while blue guides fire crews to water.

sec15-card-sec15-F37.question_text: Whose instructions must you follow when a traffic officer directs an intersection that has working lights or signs?
sec15-card-sec15-F37.teaching_text: Live officers see crash debris, emergency rigs, or gridlock ahead that automated timers cannot.

sec15-card-sec15-F38.question_text: What hand gestures and whistle blasts does an officer typically use for stop versus go?
sec15-card-sec15-F38.teaching_text: Pairing one long whistle blast and an open palm with stop—and short blasts with waving go—keeps intersections moving.

sec15-card-sec15-F39.question_text: What tool may a traffic officer use to direct drivers after dark?
sec15-card-sec15-F39.teaching_text: Bare hands vanish in headlight glare at night, so watch closely for illuminated wand or flashlight motions.

sec10-m01.narration_text: Let's run a rapid recap on the fifteen-to-fifty-foot rail stop zone, fifteen-hundred-foot horn triggers, and lowered gates. Fifteen to fifty feet back. Never pass closed, moving gates. Jump into the module quiz and lock down railroad stopping laws.

sec10-m02.narration_text: Time to review yellow advance signs, mile-long train stops, multi-track crossbucks, and flashing red lights. Trains win always, obey stops. Always yield at plain crossbucks. Head into the quiz and prove you own crossing signs and controls.

sec10-m03.narration_text: Quick rapid-fire check on hidden second trains, breakaway fiberglass gates, and keeping clear of backed-up queues. Wait lights out, second train. Keep driving forward, never reverse. Step into the quiz and crush active railroad-crossing decisions.

sec10-m04.narration_text: Here is your fast review on evacuating stalled cars first, reading the Blue Sign, and calling the railroad directly. Exit immediately, walk away fast. Crossing ID, railroad, emergency phone. Hit the quiz and nail every crossing-emergency priority.

sec10-m05.narration_text: Rapid-fire recap on right-hook bicycle checks, inside-mirror blind spots, one-way lanes, and rural road hazards. Bikes ride right beside cars. Narrower, darker, and higher speeds. Take the quiz and master city and country street tactics.

sec10-m06.narration_text: Let's lock in acceleration-lane merges, hundred-mile rest stops, white breakdown cloths, and missed exits versus wrong-way ramps. Match traffic speed before merging. Never slow, back, turn—next exit. Jump into the quiz and test your interstate driving instincts.

sec10-m07.narration_text: Final rapid review on two-hundred and seventy-five-foot headlight sightlines plus five-hundred-foot taillights and fifty-foot plate lamps. High two hundred, low seventy-five. Red five-hundred, white plate fifty. Finish Chapter Ten strong in the vehicle-lighting quiz right now.

sec13-m01.narration_text: Let's lock in animal-strike safety and the exact brake-failure steps for manual versus automatic cars. Pull over, lock doors, hazards. Manual downshifts first, auto brakes. Jump into the module check and prove your emergency instincts are sharp.

sec13-m02.narration_text: Quick fire recap on drying wet brakes, gearing down before steep hills, and handling a stuck gas pedal. Light brake drag heats water. Tap pedal, neutral, firm brake. Take on the quiz next and keep neutral versus low gear crystal clear.

sec13-m03.narration_text: Let's run back blowout steering, delayed braking, and keeping everyone safe during a roadside flat change. Grip tight, steer straight, ease. Wait until engine slows first. Head into the module quiz and nail every tire emergency rule.

sec13-m04.narration_text: Rapid review on shoulder breakdowns, passenger-side exits, and the white-cloth help signal. Full shoulder, passenger exit, away. White cloth, hood up, flashers. Knock out the practice check and lock down those breakdown habits.

sec13-m05.narration_text: Let's recap dodging right for wrong-way cars and easing smoothly back from a dropped shoulder wheel. Slow immediately, blast your horn. Never slam brakes or jerk. Step into the quiz and show you won't fall for panic-steering traps.

sec13-m06.narration_text: Quick review on ABS versus non-ABS braking and the two-step steering sequence out of a skid. Hold ABS firm, pump non-ABS. Ease gas, steer toward slide. Hit the quiz and prove your skid control sequence is automatic.

sec13-m07.narration_text: Let's lock in last-second crash defenses—turning right off-road, accelerating from rear hits, and helper protection. Horn, keep right, leave road. Accelerate clear, brace on headrest. Jump into the module check and nail every pre-impact survival move.

sec13-m08.narration_text: Final rapid recap on stopping immediately, clearing drivable cars, the thousand-dollar police rule, and info swaps. Stop immediately at every crash. Name, address, license, tag, insurer. Finish the chapter quiz strong and wrap up North Carolina emergencies clean.
